Team Fortress 2 is a first person shooter for noobs to cut their teeth on. At least, that's what it was for me. Fun, basic, definitely not Halo, CoD, or PS2 so anyone who tries to compare TF2 to those can go ♥♥♥♥ a refrigerator. It's easy to get into, controls are pretty damn simplistic, and although it doesn't tend to run well on lower-end hardware, most anything from 2010 and up can run it. Pay to win? Forget it. Even the most expensive weapons in the store won't give you that much advantage against a good veteran player. Competetive? Maybe. Most of the time it's just plain fun. Forget about kill streaks, KDR's, levels, weapons and the like. Just play the damn game and have fun.
It lives up to it's name; It's a heavily team-based game. Sometimes you'll get a game where one good Spy can take out an entire team's worth of lazy sentry-spammed Engineers in less than 30 seconds, but that's a somewhat unusual occurence. And I can tell you, the team with 6 snipers is gonna lose. Hands down. Pushing the Kart as Blu? The more scouts the better. Defending a point? A few engis with one or two pyros to spycheck and a heavy will win your game. Capping Points or Intel? Scouts to cap it and snipers or soldiers to take out those pesky sentries. Frankly there are hundreds of ways to play the game, even with good, bad, or just plain ugly players.
If you're new to the Steam or gaming arena, I highly recommend you start with TF2. Like I said, it ain't no replacement for a hardcore FPs like Halo or Planetside2, but it sure is one fun game when you have time to burn.

Team Fortress 2 is quite possibly one of the most addictive multiplayer games of all time. And I'm saying this as a guy who started in November 2014 and has had over 300 hours of game experience (which is nothing compared to some people who have well over 10,000 hours). This was the game that got me into online shooters. Some of you have may play Call of Duty.
If you have then read on because this review is for Call of Duty players.
Differences from Call of Duty:
- First of all, the gameplay. Call of Duty has a familiar "run and gun" aspect to the series. Straight up deathmatch. Just run around a corner, shoot a guy, then shoot another guy... NONE OF THIS IS IN TF2. There's a reason it's called Team Fortress 2; first of all, you have a team, and (depending on the gamemode), you must assault or defend territory (Control Points and Payload) or either defend or take certain pieces of Intelligence (Capture the Flag basically, only with a briefcase that has notes flying out of it). You can't be a lone man and carry the team because the other team WILL KILL YOU thanks to the advantages and disadvantages of each class (which I shall explain later). Instead, you need to think of yourself and your teammates. Think tactically. How can you help the team to win?
Should you assault the front lines? Go behind the the enemy and take them out one by one? Or will you defend and reinforce your own territory? How would this option suit your class? The options are limitless, though both risky and rewarding.
Oh, and also, most gamemodes do not allow you to respawn instantly. You have to wait for a while, meaning that dying is often not a good option to the team effort.
-Classes. In this game, you don't just select your weapons and quickscope every enemy that comes into site. Instead, you take advantage of each class's particular weapons, stats and special abilities.
There are nine of them, each with their own gameplay style and personality.
*The Scout - An extremely fast class who can double jump. This allows him to move quickly around the maps of the game and either weaken or take out enemies faster. He wields a scattergun and the ability to aim is especially important here (There is no auto-aim in Team Fortress 2). However, he has low health, meaning he will die easier then other classes (unless you dodge enemies with your speed) and is generally bad at long range combat.
*The Soldier - A class who has low speed but makes up for it because he can fire rockets at his feet to fling him anywhere and everywhere. He has a rocket launcher and is terrifying in close range combat and is a equally so at long range at long range depending on the circumstances. He can cause splash damage and take out enemies in seconds if mastered. However, for his downsides, he is average in all stats, never excelling in anything. Good for beginners.
*The Heavy - A very slow minigun wielder who has massive amounts of health and can kill almost all classes very easily at short range. However, due to his slow speed and large size, everyone often targets the Heavy by exploiting his weaknesses. Heavy may require support from other classes such as Medics in order to keep him alive and fighting. His main role is to defend certain points support heavy advances on enemy positions. The Heavy is a must on populated servers.
*Pyro - A rather quick and offensive class that can cause chaos for the enemy team. Pyro set people on fire and burn them to death. They excell in close range and can spot out Spies by lighting them on fire. Pyro is a fairly balanced class but can be countered by many classes such as Heavies and Scouts.
*Demoman - A versatile class that can fire grenades to protect positions and cause massive damage to the enemy team. A good Demoman is the bane of many peoples existence in the game and can wipe out opponents at all ranges. He is extremley hard to master and not recommended for beginners.
Also, KABOOM! You're dead.
*Engineer - A defensive and support class that can construct Sentries, (to control areas) Dispensers (to heal teammates) and teleporters (to bring his team to the front lines faster). Average at most stats, he can also damage and kill enemies, though not to the effectiveness of other classes. Spies can destroy his buildings.
*Spy - A support class designed for getting behind the enemy lines and backstabbing opponents. They can change the tides of a game by eliminating a dangerous target or destroying buildings by an engineer. Everyone fears them because they can disguise as teammates and promptly betray you moments later with a backstab before disguising again and killing off your team in secret. If you fail as a spy, it can mean instant death due to your low health and damage output.
*Sniper - Not like the ones in Call of Duty. You cannot quickscope with a sniper in this game nor will you do a whole lot other than die by attempting to do so on the front lines. No, instead, you must stick to back lines, stay as support and eliminate key targets with headshots on the battle. Snipers, much like spies, can change the course of a game by eliminating the best players and allowing your team to complete objectives easily.
*Medics - One of the most useful classes in the game. They heal teammates form injuries, keeping them alive and build up an "ubercharge" whilst doing so. Ubercharges have a range of abilities (depending on the weapon) such as Critical Hits and Invincibility. Medics are not made for direct combat and are weaker than most classes, though it is completely possible to play this way using your syringe gun and bonesaw as weapons.
- Maps are a lot larger in Team Fortress 2 due to the amount of players and tactics employed to boost chances of survival. They are very balanced and due to community support, they are usually bug free and far from exploitable.
All in all, it is HUGELY recommended to anyone looking for decent gameplay. And guess what? Its free to play. Download today!

Team Fortress 2 is one of the most loved first-person shooting game to date. Players have the freedom of choosing between nine different characters, each of different class such as power, technique, and speed. None of the characters are useless. Team Fortress 2 may appear like any other first person shooting game but with it’s cartoon like graphics, it has it’s own uniqueness. It feels like a cartoon has been given life.
Team Fortress 2 has different game modes which are capture the flag, control point, territorial control, king of the hill, arena, medieval modem, mann-vs-machine and the most loved one, payload. Payload gives it an edge over other games from the same genre. In the Payload mode, maps include a train track that runs through most of the arena. A bomb loaded cart makes it’s way from one base into another using this track. Players from the defending team, attempt to stop the cart from entering their base. Meanwhile, the offensive team must escort the cart through a series of checkpoints in a limited amount of time, to reach the final target.
Team Fortress 2 runs well on low-end machines, and performs even better on high-end machines. It requires the steam software platform to be installed on the PC/console in order for it to function. Recently it has been made available on most consoles i.e. PS3, XBOX 360 and also on the Linux operating systems. It has catchy theme tunes and over 50 weapons that are either free or can be purchased for a reasonable price.
Longevity is not easy for a first-person shooter. However even though this game was released seven years ago, it still has growing numbers of fans. The biggest contributing factor for this is the decision taken by the developer to publish the game for FREE in 2011.
There are many first person shooter games out there such as “Counter Strike” and “Unreal Tournament”, however Team Fortress 2 is different, it requires team work at all times, hence in this sense there is no other multiplayer game that can top it. Counter-strike may be competitive and realistic, but Team Fortress 2 is way way more fun and has more replay value.  The game also does a lovely job of framing your relationship with other players and nurturing them.

Counter Strike: A player is shooting at another player with no support.

Team Fortress 2: A player is healing one of his teammates while another is building a defence system.
The Developers of Team Fortress 2 have set a trend for all up coming online first person shooter games, they provide constant updates and keep on adding either new features and/or weapons.
However there is always room for improvement in every good game. In Team Fortress 2’s case they have not provided any single player or campaign mode. Also, in the multiplayer mode there aren’t too many maps provided.

I HATE writing reviews, but i like video game. If you like video games, make some pancakes!
Ingredients:
1 1/2 cups all-purpose flour
3 tablespoons sugar
1 tablespoon baking powder
1/4 teaspoon salt
1/8 teaspoon freshly ground nutmeg
2 large eggs, at room temperature
1 1/4 cups milk, at room temperature
1/2 teaspoon pure vanilla extract
3 tablespoons unsalted butter, plus more as needed
Now to make it
1. In a large bowl, whisk together the flour, sugar, baking powder, salt, and nutmeg.
2. In another bowl, beat the eggs and then whisk in the milk and vanilla.
3. Melt the butter in a large cast iron skillet or griddle over medium heat.
4. Whisk the butter into the milk mixture. Add the wet ingredients to the flour mixture, and whisk until a thick batter is just formed
5. Keeping the skillet at medium heat, ladle about 1/4 cup of the batter onto the skillet, to make a pancake. Make 1 or 2 more pancakes, taking care to keep them evenly spaced apart. Cook, until bubbles break the surface of the pancakes, and the undersides are golden brown, about 2 minutes. Flip with a spatula and cook about 1 minute more on the second side. Serve immediately or transfer to a platter and cover loosely with foil to keep warm. Repeat with the remaining batter, adding more butter to the skillet as needed.
6. Procedure for adding fruit to pancakes: Once the bubbles break the surface of the pancakes, scatter the surface with sliced or diced fruit, or chocolate chips, nuts, etc. Flip with a spatula and cook for 1 minute more, being careful not to burn toppings.

I am not kidding, this has acually happened to me many times.  Listen, if you are not comfortable with spending $100+ on a bunch of hats, then you will be frustrated constantly in TF2.

I originally decided to join the community against my will and be a buyer, but when I decided to use the weapons I want and stop paying I saw TF2 for what it has become in Valve's eyes: a cash cow to squeeze with an almost cult community that worships Valve everytime it produces cheap crappy skins and hats that only take their money.

I HATE writing reviews, but i like video game. If you like video games, make some pancakes!
Ingredients:
1 1/2 cups all-purpose flour
3 tablespoons sugar
1 tablespoon baking powder
1/4 teaspoon salt
1/8 teaspoon freshly ground nutmeg
2 large eggs, at room temperature
1 1/4 cups milk, at room temperature
1/2 teaspoon pure vanilla extract
3 tablespoons unsalted butter, plus more as needed
Now to make it
1. In a large bowl, whisk together the flour, sugar, baking powder, salt, and nutmeg.
2. In another bowl, beat the eggs and then whisk in the milk and vanilla.
3. Melt the butter in a large cast iron skillet or griddle over medium heat.
4. Whisk the butter into the milk mixture. Add the wet ingredients to the flour mixture, and whisk until a thick batter is just formed
5. Keeping the skillet at medium heat, ladle about 1/4 cup of the batter onto the skillet, to make a pancake. Make 1 or 2 more pancakes, taking care to keep them evenly spaced apart. Cook, until bubbles break the surface of the pancakes, and the undersides are golden brown, about 2 minutes. Flip with a spatula and cook about 1 minute more on the second side. Serve immediately or transfer to a platter and cover loosely with foil to keep warm. Repeat with the remaining batter, adding more butter to the skillet as needed.
6. Procedure for adding fruit to pancakes: Once the bubbles break the surface of the pancakes, scatter the surface with sliced or diced fruit, or chocolate chips, nuts, etc. Flip with a spatula and cook for 1 minute more, being careful not to burn toppings.

Ingredients:
1 1/2 cups all-purpose flour
3 tablespoons sugar
1 tablespoon baking powder
1/4 teaspoon salt
1/8 teaspoon freshly ground nutmeg
2 large eggs, at room temperature
1 1/4 cups milk, at room temperature
1/2 teaspoon pure vanilla extract
3 tablespoons unsalted butter, plus more as needed
Now to make it
1. In a large bowl, whisk together the flour, sugar, baking powder, salt, and nutmeg.
2. In another bowl, beat the eggs and then whisk in the milk and vanilla.
3. Melt the butter in a large cast iron skillet or griddle over medium heat.
4. Whisk the butter into the milk mixture. Add the wet ingredients to the flour mixture, and whisk until a thick batter is just formed
5. Keeping the skillet at medium heat, ladle about 1/4 cup of the batter onto the skillet, to make a pancake. Make 1 or 2 more pancakes, taking care to keep them evenly spaced apart. Cook, until bubbles break the surface of the pancakes, and the undersides are golden brown, about 2 minutes. Flip with a spatula and cook about 1 minute more on the second side. Serve immediately or transfer to a platter and cover loosely with foil to keep warm. Repeat with the remaining batter, adding more butter to the skillet as needed.
6. Procedure for adding fruit to pancakes: Once the bubbles break the surface of the pancakes, scatter the surface with sliced or diced fruit, or chocolate chips, nuts, etc. Flip with a spatula and cook for 1 minute more, being careful not to burn toppings.

Though TF2 has fame beyond many shooters, I still would give it a little praise here in this little review. Now you have to know that I am not a first person shooter type of gamer. Outside of TF2 my only other experiences are Wolfenstein 3D and Unreal Tournament, which I never even played multiplayer. However, TF2 has become my most played game ever, eating over 3000 hrs. of my life. It may be a bit on the downhill for me now, but it was a solid pick during my PhD.
The game's cartoonesque style and class based system make it so that even non-veterans can jump in and have enjoyment. I even managed to climb up the ranks a bit in competitive. What if you don't like to fight other people and just want to have some fun with friends? Jump into the game mode Man vs. Machine to have a unique 'tower defense' - like game. In short it has many different skill level and playstyle type of game modes to entertain a wide variety of players.
Besides, it is free to play and if you do not pay you get nearly the full game. What you get extra if you pay - even just a nickel is enough to get upgraded to 'premium'  status - are nice extra's like trading. This is not necessary to play, however, and rarely are the first weapons you receive (or 'stock'  weapons) downright outclassed by others - others weapons tend to have their own niches. Furthermore the community in general is friendly, so why don't you give it a try?
Worth installing, you will be having free fun for years.

This game is a must have for 12 year olds with low self esteem. Seriously if you have the maturity of a 12 year old child and want the opportunity to make yourself feel better about your crummy life by belittling people on an online multiplayer fps game then download this game right now. I have experienced many times on this game absolutely disgusting behaviour from other players in the “community.” It is sad. It is sad knowing that there are so many children growing up in this world who show complete and utter ignorance, unprovoked to people they do not even know.
For instance:
A kid said this to a friend of mine while in a match. “Hey liked how I wrecked you last round?” (No reply from my friend) “Oh what you got nothing to say? Must be too poor to buy a mic.” (So poor yet he owns a computer right?) (I then attempt to kick this child from the game for his ignorance) Random other guy who must have been this child’s friend starts. “What the f#$% you trying to do?” (My vote to kick the initial child fails) (They try and kick me) Shouts “Kick this f@#$^% out of here he's trying to send me pictures of his d$%^” (I get kicked).
Now I don't care about being kicked out of a game. There are many other lobbies I can join to play and try to have “fun” on. What I care about is how completely toxic the community is on this game. Yeah I get it, it is the internet you have to at some point accept the reality that there are many “trolls” and immature children out there. The problem for me is not ignoring it and moving on. The problem is when I, like many others, sit down to relax in their spare time and try to have fun playing a team based game get put into situations of unpleasant, abusive, conflict constantly it becomes something besides fun and enjoyment but rather stressful and disturbing. Literally every server will have people on that have nothing better to say besides overused insults. There is absolutely no need for it. There is not a single thing that requires someone to be a complete piece of trash in order to have fun or even be good at a video game. It ruins everything video games are meant to be about.
Besides the absolutely toxic community in which you cannot really change in anyway there are other issues. The game is goofy with it's cartoon style which is a hint that you should not take it too seriously. If you find yourself taking tf2 seriously then that is the point in time that you should uninstall it. Trust me once you start taking the game seriously you will degrade yourself by involving yourself with the toxic players, you will lose money, you will lose friends and you will no longer enjoy something you once did. I realized this after seeing how much I spent on the game, the situation I explained above and when I started to become frustrated at people dancing around the spawn wasting time (which should be the fun of it yet it became annoying).
Looking at the lucrative “micro transaction” style system involved, it is at least how I see it addicting. Who wants to use ugly stock weapons when they can open crates to get fancy shiny ones or simply buy them? Constantly buying more keys, to open more crates, in the hopes of getting something valuable to get your money back or make a “profit” (it hardly ever happens). It is exactly like gambling and the risk is greater than the reward. You may get an unusual hat but what does that actually do for you? Can you sell it and make a profit? Yes. Can you withdraw that money and buy yourself a bike, or a baseball bat, or pay the rent and bills? Nope. Every dime you spend on this game is forever invested into Steam. So you don't really make anything off of buying and trading these types of virtual items and they do not improve your skills in the game or increase your enjoyment. It gives you this false sense that you did but in the end it eats your money and that is it's only purpose. Spending money on games like this is okay if you really feel like it will bring you enjoyment but fair warning it can end up costing you a significant amount of money especially if you do not know what you are doing. I let myself became consumed in this system and have spent much more than I should ever have with next to nothing to show for in the end. I regret spending any money on this game on the virtual items especially now that I have lost my enjoyment of the game.
Overall I had fun. 800 hours on a free to play game in my opinion made it worth it. What I realize now though is that games like this are only as fun as the people you play them with. I started seeing a significant amount of toxic players no matter what server I was on and that killed my enjoyment. Listening to people constantly insult each other over nothing gets tiring. I guess maybe I am just at an age where I have to move on to another saga of gaming to find more enjoyment. Will I miss playing tf2? Probably not now that I have expanded my game library. Will I play it again? Likely but only for an hour or two here and there just to have fun. I will never invest my time, like I used to, back into this game because it is really not worth it. I would recommend if you want to have some fun (100-500 hours) try Team Fortress 2 out, BUT my warning and the point of my review, DO NOT invest a significant amount of time and/or money into this game. It is really not worth it once you become tired of the toxic community. Everything you worked on getting will increase your disappointment when you make the decision to stop playing the game.

Before I first started playing Team Fortress 2, I was a simple man. I had a wife, two kids, and the perfect job. All was going well in my life. It was perfect. And then, one day, I discovered the game, and started playing. First I had played for one hour. Then, 5 hours. Then, 50 hours. And then, thousands upon thousands of hours. I was too absorbed in it. My boss fired me, and my wife divorced me. I was find, though. I didn’t need them. All that mattered now was getting unusual hats, and refined metal. I began to be well-known in the community. Every day, I got hundreds of trade requests, sometimes even thousands. I was the king. I was on top. I sold my dog to buy a strange festive black box, and three unusual hats. What a great deal. Pretty soon, the world around me started to change. I had begun to blur the line between TF2 and reality. When I closed my eyes, I heard heavies calling for my assistance as a medic. While sleeping, I would see AFK players, waiting for a backstab. I would hear the yells and screams of my fallen allies, and within that I would hear the excited announcement of an eccentric man. “Bonus ducks!” I would hear him exclaim. Team Fortress 2 has ruined my life. The man I used to be is dead, and has been replaced by an obese, jobless, single 40 year old.  It has made me insane. I don’t even know what’s real anymore. The other day, I told a man at the bus stop I’d give him my fancy fedora, for a jar of his♥♥♥♥♥♥with Christmas lights on it. It has ruined me. I am nothing now. And I will continue to be nothing, until I can no longer take it, and hang myself. Finally ending my misery, once and for all, and finally ridding myself from the universe.

Can you withdraw that money and buy yourself a bike, or a baseball bat, or pay the rent and bills? Nope. Every dime you spend on this game is forever invested into Steam. So you don't really make anything off of buying and trading these types of virtual items and they do not improve your skills in the game or increase your enjoyment. It gives you this false sense that you did but in the end it eats your money and that is it's only purpose. Spending money on games like this is okay if you really feel like it will bring you enjoyment but fair warning it can end up costing you a significant amount of money especially if you do not know what you are doing. I let myself became consumed in this system and have spent much more than I should ever have with next to nothing to show for in the end. I regret spending any money on this game on the virtual items especially now that I have lost my enjoyment of the game.
Overall I had fun. 800 hours on a free to play game in my opinion made it worth it. What I realize now though is that games like this are only as fun as the people you play them with. I started seeing a significant amount of toxic players no matter what server I was on and that killed my enjoyment. Listening to people constantly insult each other over nothing gets tiring. I guess maybe I am just at an age where I have to move on to another saga of gaming to find more enjoyment. Will I miss playing tf2? Probably not now that I have expanded my game library. Will I play it again? Likely but only for an hour or two here and there just to have fun. I will never invest my time, like I used to, back into this game because it is really not worth it. I would recommend if you want to have some fun (100-500 hours) try Team Fortress 2 out, BUT my warning and the point of my review, DO NOT invest a significant amount of time and/or money into this game. It is really not worth it once you become tired of the toxic community. Everything you worked on getting will increase your disappointment when you make the decision to stop playing the game.

And then, one day, I discovered the game, and started playing. First I had played for one hour. Then, 5 hours. Then, 50 hours. And then, thousands upon thousands of hours. I was too absorbed in it. My boss fired me, and my wife divorced me. I was find, though. I didn’t need them. All that mattered now was getting unusual hats, and refined metal. I began to be well-known in the community. Every day, I got hundreds of trade requests, sometimes even thousands. I was the king. I was on top. I sold my dog to buy a strange festive black box, and three unusual hats. What a great deal. Pretty soon, the world around me started to change. I had begun to blur the line between TF2 and reality. When I closed my eyes, I heard heavies calling for my assistance as a medic. While sleeping, I would see AFK players, waiting for a backstab. I would hear the yells and screams of my fallen allies, and within that I would hear the excited announcement of an eccentric man. “Bonus ducks!” I would hear him exclaim. Team Fortress 2 has ruined my life. The man I used to be is dead, and has been replaced by an obese, jobless, single 40 year old.  It has made me insane. I don’t even know what’s real anymore. The other day, I told a man at the bus stop I’d give him my fancy fedora, for a jar of his♥♥♥♥♥♥with Christmas lights on it. It has ruined me. I am nothing now. And I will continue to be nothing, until I can no longer take it, and hang myself. Finally ending my misery, once and for all, and finally ridding myself from the universe.

A game from 2007 that supports luck instead of skill in the sense of random crits, looks over skill in the sense of hats, and spam over skill in the sense of every pyro weapon. It supports meaningless change with matchmaking that no one asked for, ignores any opportunity for meaningful change by leaving random crits in the game, and ignores everything said by a community more dedicated than that of any other game on Steam. Team Fortress 2 has more wit and charm than any other game I've played, an artstyle more timeless than the art it's based on, and is the third most played game on Steam. It also has a heap of ugly cosmetics that take away from the artsyle, a playerbase that consists of 60 percent gibus pyros, and a development team consisting of half of a person.
Despite its flaws, TF2 is an incredible game at its core (aside from random crits, that game mechanic is simply unjustifiable). It's just had so much♥♥♥♥♥♥heaped on it throughout the years that it looks like an olympian who decided to eat nothing but canola oil for 30 years before developing every type of cancer known to man. I recommend it, but it's just not what it used to be, and it sure as hell isn't what it could be.

Now, before you skip past this review, just take a moment to have a look. This is my opinion:
Team Fortress 2 is one of the best Free To Play games I could ever have. I belive the game used to cost something, but now it is free. The download time isn't one of those games that take 2 days and then if you quit you have to restart it. You can resume the download at any time, and it doesn't take long to install the game. Now for the actual GAMEPLAY.
The TF2 Gameplay is amazing. Powerups, Taunts, Upgrrades, AI's, Weapons. Thy are all amazing features that is each something that makes Team Fortress 2 well, Team Fortress 2. The way the game is animated, and the blood, means it is a bit more friendly towards younger players. The controls can be edited to the desired key (as most Steam games) which makes it easier to play, and you don't have to remember different controls for different games. The maps are very good within content, and features. They are very detailed and hardly ever glitch. The game doesn't usually lag, ranging from (worst) 4 - 37 (amazing) FPS rate. This is a long review, so lets summarize...
Team Fortress - as I said earlier - is one of the best (if not best) F2P game I have, and many others have. Hopefully, if you don't own the game yet, you soon will.

The download time isn't one of those games that take 2 days and then if you quit you have to restart it. You can resume the download at any time, and it doesn't take long to install the game. Now for the actual GAMEPLAY.
The TF2 Gameplay is amazing. Powerups, Taunts, Upgrrades, AI's, Weapons. Thy are all amazing features that is each something that makes Team Fortress 2 well, Team Fortress 2. The way the game is animated, and the blood, means it is a bit more friendly towards younger players. The controls can be edited to the desired key (as most Steam games) which makes it easier to play, and you don't have to remember different controls for different games. The maps are very good within content, and features. They are very detailed and hardly ever glitch. The game doesn't usually lag, ranging from (worst) 4 - 37 (amazing) FPS rate. This is a long review, so lets summarize...
Team Fortress - as I said earlier - is one of the best (if not best) F2P game I have, and many others have. Hopefully, if you don't own the game yet, you soon will.

text:
All in all a fun goof, just play it and go full tard. Though as an FPS or a game to enjoy I can't reccommend it. So if you are looking for something to waste your time on, by all means download it. If you are looking for something to invest your time in, look else where.
InterWebs:
It's showing it's age really badly. A lot of servers seem to be hosted on potatoes, Yet is more likely the just the prehistoric "netcode".
The server side thing tends to get rather insane when dealing with players with high pings, For instance being sniped 4 seconds after you where behind cover, back stabbing someone only for it to register as a front stab or people just stuttering in and out of existence (giving no hitmarkers) yet them having no problems hitting you as your server response time is good.
Also with no way to votekick people on the other team and no "ping restricted servers" that i could see, its nearly impossible to get rid of the people who join from the otherside of the world to play with 500+ ping and then say "i'm not lagging, the game looks fine to me". Unlike in other source games where anyone can initiate a "votekick" against anyone, this game only allows it on servers that enable the votekick function, and only allows team members to votekick other team members.
Loot/Timesync/Cashsink:
The drops come thick and fast the 1st few hours, then slow to a trickle. Unless you have friends who have a bunch of doubles to trade you, you will be waiting a long time before you can craft some decent equipment. Then again you keep getting "crate drops" which have a chance to give you random stuff if you spend money to buy "keys" to open, so it's like gambling for kids. You could also just go and buy said item for money if you prefer.
As the crates are random, just buying the items is probably cheaper in the long run. For instance if you are the type of person that says "I will only buy one key, and open 1 crate... and then im done" you will most likely end up suckered into the micro transaction model, and spending $100's opening crates, when you could have just bought what you wanted for 1/2 what you spent.
Also the inability to turn off crate drops gets rather annoying, as the pop up appears in game and its almost taunting you if you are trying to F2P.
Gameplay:
If you are wanting to play, find and "instant respawn server" otherwise you spend 20 seconds walking to the fight, get killed in under 1/2 a second, then wait 15 seconds to respawn, then repeat. It becomes a viscious "psych out cycle" where you die, wait about a minute, then go for another kill, die, get mad, wait another minute, and repeat getting madder each death until you are so mad you cant focus. Not to mention the times where you walk out of the spawn, and an enemy has made their way all the way back there and instant kills you, leading to another 15 second wait.
This is generally my problem with respawn timers. On a really bad day, you can spend more time "waiting watching a timer count down" than you can in the middle of the action. Ain't noberdy gert tym fer dat.
Not going to go into actual gameplay too much, as I think in general the gameplay is well balanced, yet the whole "interwebs" part is more of an issue than anything else. Mainly just thought I would pass on that tip.
Classes:
Meh, just watch some youtube videos if you are interested. Just remember its going to take a while to get any of that stuff if you are F2P.
Summary:
Its updated often, yet built on ancient netcode. Can't recommend it, but I am going to keep playing it.

YouTube Poop, often abbreviated as YTP, is a type of video mashup, created by editing preexisting media sources for humorous, confusing or shocking purposes and often containing mature content. YouTube Poop videos are traditionally uploaded to the video-sharing website YouTube, hence the name, but may be mirrored or uploaded on other video sharing websites like Newgrounds, Vidme, and/or Dailymotion.
n a typical YouTube Poop video, visual and auditory effects are used to alter the underlying work. Some of these videos may involve completely or partially repurposing sources to create or convey a story, while others follow a non-linear narrative. Some contain no storyline at all.[1] Alternatively, a YouTube Poop may consist solely of an existing video repeated in a slowed or remixed loop.[2] In many cases, YouTube Poops utilize a bizarre sequence of elements that may entertain, confuse or irritate, depending on the viewer.[1] Associate professor of cultural anthropology at Kansas State University Michael Wesch has defined YouTube Poops as "absurdist remixes that ape and mock the lowest technical and aesthetic standards of remix culture to comment on remix culture itself".[3]
Media sources of YouTube Poops may include television shows, movies, cartoons, commercials, video games, and other videos obtained from YouTube or elsewhere. There is no generally accepted limitation as to what kind of source material may be used for a YouTube Poop. Some primary sources include cutscenes from Zelda: The Wand of Gamelon, Link: The Faces of Evil, Hotel Mario and I.M. Meen as well as SpongeBob SquarePants, King of the Hill and works featuring Michael Rosen, Billy Mays and Dr. Rabbit. YouTube: Online Video and Participatory Culture notes YouTube Poop having a particular fascination with "low" Saturday-morning American cartoons from the 1990s such as The Super Mario Bros. Super Show!, Adventures of Sonic the Hedgehog and Mega Man as well as anime series, video game cutscenes and videos from YouTube itself.[4]
YouTube Poop is often derivative in the sense that the work of one artist (or "pooper") is sometimes used as the underlying work for another video. Lawrence Lessig, Professor of Law at Harvard Law School, referred to this behavior as an example of "call & response" within a remix culture.[5]
Due to the use of copyright materials and the manner in which these sources are depicted, YTP videos may be removed from YouTube following a DMCA complaint. However, political scientist and author Trajce Cvetkovski noted in 2013 that, despite Viacom filing a copyright infringement lawsuit with YouTube in 2007, YouTube Poops such as "The Sky Had a Weegee" by Hurricoaster, which features scenes from the animated series SpongeBob SquarePants (in particular, the episode, "Shanghaied") and a satiric caricature based on Nintendo's Luigi as he appears in the educational video game Mario Is Missing!, remained on YouTube.[6]
The law in the United Kingdom does allow people to use copyrighted material for the purposes of parody, pastiche, and caricature without infringing on the copyright of the material.[7] Copyright owners are only able to sue the parody, pastiche, or caricature creator if the parody, pastiche, or caricature contains hateful or discriminative messages. If the case is then taken to court, it will be down to a judge to decide whether the video meets these criteria.[8]
Individuals involved in YouTube Poops sometimes make efforts to take their videos down due to the mature and defamatory content prevalent in them, especially if they have a large audience of children watching their work. Children's poet Michael Rosen (who claims to have "become a cult" among YouTube Poopers)[9] initially attempted to take his videos down, but after a few frank discussions with YouTube Poopers, he decided to allow the videos to stay online.[9] Rosen issued a warning on his website, saying that: "Quite a few people have fun taking my videos and making new versions of them, known as 'poops' or 'YTPs'. Many of these are not suitable for young children. I am not responsible for either the words or pictures of these.[10][11]"

Overall, this game is WAY better than Call of Duty, Call of Duty seems so repetitive in the sense of killing people, but in this game you have so many more ways to kill people, suicide bombing, backstabbing, and much more options of killing. Not only that, but tf2 has much more gamemodes that you can play, an example would be dodgeball, CTI (Capture the Intelligence), Capture Points, even a zombie apocalypse type mode. Even around halloween, there is a fresh new skin of a gamemode, ._. ...
I also want to point out the creative weapons, instead of choosing a primary, secondary, melee, and perks, you immediatly get a weapon that fits with the class, as well as the upsides and downsides (e.g Scout is fast but has low health). I would also like to point out, you're health doesn't just regenerate, you need health packs, a dispenser's healing, or a medic's medigun stream of health, so the game is much more realistic, kind of...
Oh, and the hats, ALL THE HATS. The hats cost money though, from $2.99 to $15.99, don't worry though, as you can earn these hats from drops, and there are achievement hats like the Ghostly Gibus and that one hat with a camera on it (I don't remember the name...).
If you have amazingly expensive weapons, but no hats, then you can trade weapons for hats. Yes, there's trading. The trading system isn't JUST for Tf2, it's also available for Steam trading cards, backrounds, and games, but back to the Tf2 trading. Each item in Tf2 has a value, so if you have a 12 Bud Unusual hat, you can trade that for a ton of stranges. etc, etc.
So that's all I have to say, I really like this game, and now that it's free, I recommend you play it.

*Team Fortress 2, a team based multiplayer that manages to be both quirky and fun, but also unique.
- I have played this game from around 2009 (Orange Box) on my console and always felt it was a great game. Consoles, of course don't provide as much "Depth" as the PC or Mac version. But when switching to PC I loved the game all over again, but it wasn't without its faults.
*What it does right
- It create 9 unique classes that bring their own skills to the table.
- Community that pours much effort into DLC.
- Can jump in when tired of other games.
*What it needs to be improved upon
- Too much focus on buying "hats"
- Wish that Valve would please listen to the community more about what needs to change, so that this game may thrive far into the future
*Overall it is a solid shooter that I can always jump into with friends. I only wish that Valve would offer more of a"change of pace". Meaning that they would listen to the people instead of just throwing hats at us to shut us up. Anyway, there is no need to ramble on. I recommend this game any and every gamer, it's very different, in a good way.

*Team Fortress 2, a team based multiplayer that manages to be both quirky and fun, but also unique.
- I have played this game from around 2009 (Orange Box) on my console and always felt it was a great game. Consoles, of course don't provide as much "Depth" as the PC or Mac version. But when switching to PC I loved the game all over again, but it wasn't without its faults.
*What it does right
- It create 9 unique classes that bring their own skills to the table.
- Community that pours much effort into DLC.
- Can jump in when tired of other games.
*What it needs to be improved upon
- Too much focus on buying "hats"
- Wish that Valve would please listen to the community more about what needs to change, so that this game may thrive far into the future
*Overall it is a solid shooter that I can always jump into with friends. I only wish that Valve would offer more of a"change of pace". Meaning that they would listen to the people instead of just throwing hats at us to shut us up. Anyway, there is no need to ramble on. I recommend this game any and every gamer, it's very different, in a good way.
*9.2/10

Team Fortress 2 is an excellent game to the Team fortress franchise and it MUST be a game in your libary, especially when it is a Free to play! Even though I am probably classed as a noob in this game, I still have tons of fun while playing TF2.
This game is, what I would call, a cartoon styled FPS. With many different classes to select, there is a whole lot of different items and weapons to purchase and collect. There are also various game-modes that may require you to fight against world-wide players, or mabye you having to fight off waves of robotic figures!
During online sessions, you will be able to recieve tools, items and weapons just by playing the game, so the more time you spend on the online matches, the more 'loot' you will aquire! With your findings, you will be able to either equip it on to your online solider, or you can trade it with fellow soliders.
In relation to GMOD (another Steam game available for purchase) TF2 supports mods! So as well as all the default gamemodes, you will also enjoy the community created gamemodes/minigames.
Fortunately, TF2 doesn't give your graphics card a hard time, its extremly easy to run and the game just looks beautiful! TF2's graphics are sort of 'cartoony', so don't expect realistic graphics like Battlefield 4. I specifically like TF2's graphics because the shading is very smooth and the lighting makes the game look pleasant.
I absoulutely adore TF2, it is perfect for any casual gamer like me :). The graphics are great and so is the gameplay, but like with everything, it is NOT perfect. The only thing I dislike about TF2 is the un realistic movement, the bad thing is when you walk in a direction then just stop, you sort of slide just a tad bit. But that was just my opinion!
Overall, I love TF2 and i highly recommend this game to anyone! With a couple of mistakes that may need tweaking a bit, TF2 is obviously not perfect, but that can relate to all games.
Anyway, thanks for reading my review on Team Fortress 2!
~IceReek24 :)

This game is based around 9 classes fighting against another team of other classes. In other words a team based game. When ever you start playing you choose between a red or blue team and get to choose the class you want to play as. The classes are Scout, Soldier, Pyro, Demo Man, Heavy, Engineer, Medic, Sniper, and Spy. I reccomend if you are just starting to play this game, do not start with playing spy. He is the hardest class to master. There are also a variety of game modes. King Of The Hill, Capture the Flag, and Payload are just a few of them. Here is a list of the pros and cons.
Pros:
- Free to Play
- Variety of Classes
- Variety of Game Modes
- Hats
- Lots of Weapons for Each Class
- Constantly Updated
- A Lot of Humor
Cons:
- Some Bugs and Glitches Here and There
Hope this recommendation helped. I encourage you to play this game. Thank You.

This game... This game... I have dedicated over 200 hours of playing time to this game, leaving every other game in my library collect dust (with the exception of fallout new vegas), however; I feel like I could easily put in another 1000 hours without getting bored. This game is, by no means, a free to play, play to win, but it is very tempting to spend hundreds of dollars on cosmetics, stranges, killstreaks, and (of course) hats. Most of the things that truly make the game more exciting, such as new strategic weapons, are obtained through time and determinations, not money. There is a very strong continuum of skill throughout the game, making some servers too difficult or too easy, depending on chance. The latest update, while rebuked by some, is actually quite interesting. The new weapons aren't too underwhelming and the gifts are pretty excitng, like a raffle of sorts. Overall, it is one of my favorite games and one I hope will stay around for another six years.

Team Fortress 2 has been regularly updated since its inception in 2007, after over nine years in development. Due to all these updates, the game has actually taken on several incarnations. In other words, I will be individually reviewing the following three separate games:
Team Fortress 2 (2007-2010)
Hat Fortress 2 (2010-2012)
Dressup Fortress 2 (2012-present)
But first,
General:
-You can regularly defy the laws of physics in too many ways to be listed.
-Scouts can fly by flapping their legs.
-A can of soda turns you into the Super-Matrix; you can make bullets dodge you.
-Some pistols can make you jump higher or fully absorb the impact of falling at any velocity.
-Coating someone in milk and then beating them up will cure your cancer.
-Steel-toed boots make shooting rockets at your feet less unhealthy.
-Whipping people makes them run faster.
-A big Russian guy can survive as many direct hits from an anti-tank missile as a Russian T-72 tank can.
-Blowing into a seashell can patch the gunshot wounds of everyone around you.
-Flamethrowers can also shoot a powerful blast of air that can send people flying or rockets back to their maker.
-You can beat people to death with a bottle of whiskey.
-You can decapitate people with a golf club.
-Harmless explosives.
-Eating a sandvich will cure AIDS, mend katana wounds, and treat your erectile dysfunction.
-Hitting a machine with a wrench will fix it, upgrade it, and resupply it.
-Dispensers generate ammo for your weapon and pills for your back pain.
-A remote control with one big red button can be used to destroy one of any four buildings of your choosing.
-You can shoot up morphine with a crossbow.
-You can use a beam of light to turn someone’s exterior skin and clothing into pure titanium armor.
-Pretending to play the violin with a bonesaw used for amputation will cure the common cold.
-Urine is more effective than a fire extinguisher.
-Frenchmen with ski masks are incapable of stabbing their victims in the neck. When they encounter Australians with shields on their backs, they’ll stab the shield first… Making the shield disintegrate.
-A pocket watch can partially absorb the damage caused by a rocket, create a deceased doppelganger of you, all while you become invisible and walk away.
-If you backstab someone with an icicle, they’ll instantly transform into a highly-durable ice sculpture.

Team Fortress 2 (2007-2010)
This was a team-based first person shooter involving two identical teams, differing only in color and artistic design, vying for control of various strategic locales around the world. You could play as one of nine cripplingly overspecialized classes. The various classes would have to pool their strengths together and cooperate in order to prevail over the opposing team. However, this was easier said than done as communication and teamwork were (and still are) generally foreign concepts. Teams would have to beat each other up and steal their briefcases, beat each other up and steal their stage lighting platforms, and beat each other up to push a high explosive bomb cart into a pit. Hats were just a cool side thing. Many people would stand around and do nothing on dedicated idle servers so that they could amass the metal necessary to craft themselves a new hat.
Overall, Team Fortress 2 was a fun and highly addictive game whether or not there was a team or no team involved.
Over 9 out of 9, worth the weight.
Hat Fortress 2 (2010-2012)
The Mann-Conomy Update, released on September 30, 2010, marked the end of Team Fortress 2 and the birth of Hat Fortress 2. Players no longer needed to idle to get hats. They could also buy them, trade for them, and even sell them for other hats. In addition, keys were also introduced, giving players the ability to throw away their parent’s or their own hard-earned money on opening virtual crates in the hopes of getting virtual hats. More often than not, they ended up getting worthless virtual guns. The Mann-Conomy fever quickly swept over Team Fortress 2, reducing it to a side game. Hat Fortress 2 was about accumulating as many hats as possible by any means necessary and then using the Team Fortress 2 mini-game to show them off to others. The free-to-play update in 2011 further enlarged the player base, increasing the popularity of Hat Fortress 2, its modes, and related fun mini-games. As Hat Fortress 2 was further refined and developed, new elements were added, including unusuals and non-hat cosmetic items. Eventually, so many new cosmetics came in that Hat Fortress 2 gradually evolved into another game.
11 hats out of 10.
Dressup Fortress 2 (2012-Present)
This is the current and ultimate form of Team Fortress 2. The game is centered on assembling a complete outfit for each of the classes that you play. You can acquire the components for your dream outfit by unboxing crates of all shapes and sizes and/or by implementing any one of the many trading strategies out there. You can show off your outfits, topped off with exorbitant unusual hats, in a multitude of ways. You can do the conga, hi-five other folks adorned with fancy and quirky outfits, play intense games of rock, paper, scissors, or play Jack Black’s guitar. You can also play whatever vestiges remain of the old Team Fortress 2. You could also play Mann vs. Machine and acquire stock weapons with robotic skulls hanging from them or perhaps even become The Man with the Golden Gun. If neither of those are satisfactory, there are a wide range of other mini-games to play, some of which have been around since the days of old Team Fortress 2. They include, but are not limited to: Versus Saxton Hale, Freak Fortress 2, Jailbreak, Balloon Race, TF2 Kart, magic spells in Halloween event maps, Slender Fortress, Surf maps, Jump maps, and TF2Ware.
In conclusion, Dressup Fortress 2 does provide something for everyone, so I guess it’s alright.

Team Fortress 2 has been regularly updated since its inception in 2007, after over nine years in development. Due to all these updates, the game has actually taken on several incarnations. In other words, I will be individually reviewing the following three separate games:
Team Fortress 2 (2007-2010)
Hat Fortress 2 (2010-2012)
Dressup Fortress 2 (2012-present)
But first,
General:
-You can regularly defy the laws of physics in too many ways to be listed.
-Scouts can fly by flapping their legs.
-A can of soda turns you into the Super-Matrix; you can make bullets dodge you.
-Some pistols can make you jump higher or fully absorb the impact of falling at any velocity.
-Coating someone in milk and then beating them up will cure your cancer.
-Steel-toed boots make shooting rockets at your feet less unhealthy.
-Whipping people makes them run faster.
-A big Russian guy can survive as many direct hits from an anti-tank missile as a Russian T-72 tank can.
-Blowing into a seashell can patch the gunshot wounds of everyone around you.
-Flamethrowers can also shoot a powerful blast of air that can send people flying or rockets back to their maker.
-You can beat people to death with a bottle of whiskey.
-You can decapitate people with a golf club.
-Harmless explosives.
-Eating a sandvich will cure AIDS, mend katana wounds, and treat your erectile dysfunction.
-Hitting a machine with a wrench will fix it, upgrade it, and resupply it.
-Dispensers generate ammo for your weapon and pills for your back pain.
-A remote control with one big red button can be used to destroy one of any four buildings of your choosing.
-You can shoot up morphine with a crossbow.
-You can use a beam of light to turn someone’s exterior skin and clothing into pure titanium armor.
-Pretending to play the violin with a bonesaw used for amputation will cure the common cold.
-Urine is more effective than a fire extinguisher.
-Frenchmen with ski masks are incapable of stabbing their victims in the neck. When they encounter Australians with shields on their backs, they’ll stab the shield first… Making the shield disintegrate.
-A pocket watch can partially absorb the damage caused by a rocket, create a deceased doppelganger of you, all while you become invisible and walk away.
-If you backstab someone with an icicle, they’ll instantly transform into a highly-durable ice sculpture.

Team Fortress 2 (2007-2010)
This was a team-based first person shooter involving two identical teams, differing only in color and artistic design, vying for control of various strategic locales around the world. You could play as one of nine cripplingly overspecialized classes. The various classes would have to pool their strengths together and cooperate in order to prevail over the opposing team. However, this was easier said than done as communication and teamwork were (and still are) generally foreign concepts. Teams would have to beat each other up and steal their briefcases, beat each other up and steal their stage lighting platforms, and beat each other up to push a high explosive bomb cart into a pit. Hats were just a cool side thing. Many people would stand around and do nothing on dedicated idle servers so that they could amass the metal necessary to craft themselves a new hat.
Overall, Team Fortress 2 was a fun and highly addictive game whether or not there was a team or no team involved.
Over 9 out of 9, worth the weight.
Hat Fortress 2 (2010-2012)
The Mann-Conomy Update, released on September 30, 2010, marked the end of Team Fortress 2 and the birth of Hat Fortress 2. Players no longer needed to idle to get hats. They could also buy them, trade for them, and even sell them for other hats. In addition, keys were also introduced, giving players the ability to throw away their parent’s or their own hard-earned money on opening virtual crates in the hopes of getting virtual hats. More often than not, they ended up getting worthless virtual guns. The Mann-Conomy fever quickly swept over Team Fortress 2, reducing it to a side game. Hat Fortress 2 was about accumulating as many hats as possible by any means necessary and then using the Team Fortress 2 mini-game to show them off to others. The free-to-play update in 2011 further enlarged the player base, increasing the popularity of Hat Fortress 2, its modes, and related fun mini-games. As Hat Fortress 2 was further refined and developed, new elements were added, including unusuals and non-hat cosmetic items. Eventually, so many new cosmetics came in that Hat Fortress 2 gradually evolved into another game.
11 hats out of 10.
Dressup Fortress 2 (2012-Present)
This is the current and ultimate form of Team Fortress 2. The game is centered on assembling a complete outfit for each of the classes that you play. You can acquire the components for your dream outfit by unboxing crates of all shapes and sizes and/or by implementing any one of the many trading strategies out there. You can show off your outfits, topped off with exorbitant unusual hats, in a multitude of ways. You can do the conga, hi-five other folks adorned with fancy and quirky outfits, play intense games of rock, paper, scissors, or play Jack Black’s guitar. You can also play whatever vestiges remain of the old Team Fortress 2. You could also play Mann vs. Machine and acquire stock weapons with robotic skulls hanging from them or perhaps even become The Man with the Golden Gun. If neither of those are satisfactory, there are a wide range of other mini-games to play, some of which have been around since the days of old Team Fortress 2. They include, but are not limited to: Versus Saxton Hale, Freak Fortress 2, Jailbreak, Balloon Race, TF2 Kart, magic spells in Halloween event maps, Slender Fortress, Surf maps, Jump maps, and TF2Ware.
In conclusion, Dressup Fortress 2 does provide something for everyone, so I guess it’s alright.

For those unfamiliar, TF2 is a Class Based Shooter, based on the Team Fortress mod for Quake and Team Fortress Classic, which was a mod for the original Source Engine. A CBS is commonly a First-Person shooter, such as Enemy Territory, Battlefield, and Battlefront, although some CBS titles, like Battle of Heros, is a Third-Person shooter. TF2 is the former. Unlike the example titles, however, both teams are exactly the same, and neither side has any kind of special unit or weapon that's only available for that side (Unlike Battlefront giving each of the four factions a Unique Unit with Unique weapons). There are nine classes in total: Scout, Pyro, Soldier, Demoman, Heavy, Engineer, Medic, Sniper, and Spy. This is also quite a few more classes than some other game have had (Again as an example: Battlefront had only six classes per team, and some Battlefield titles, such as Hardline, only have four classes). Although it is a lot of classes, each one carries a bit of weight, and can be very important to a team (Although in general play, teams will have multiple members of each class, and some cases one class will not even exist during a game).
The Scout is a fast moving class that can get in close with a shotgun and blast enemies at close range, and then quickly pull out to evade a counter-attack. The soldier, while slow moving, is armed with a very powerful rocket launcher. The Pyro moves fairly quickly, and needs to get close to make use of his flamethrower. These are considered to be the offensive classes, and are meant to push for an objective.
The Demoman can create explosive traps with sticky bombs, and has excellent melee capabilities. The Heavy wields a minigun and has a very high amount of health, which makes up for his slow walk. The Engineer can build ammunition dispensers and automated turrets which will shoot any nearby enemies. These are the defensive classes, and are used to hold a position (Although Heavies, when paired with a medic, can also turn into a menacing offensive force).
The Medic, as the name suggests, heals team-mates in the thick of battle. Snipers, again as the name suggests, use a sniper rifle to pick off enemies from a safe distance. Spies can cloak themselves and get behind enemy lines to take out deadly players with a swift one-hit-kill backstab with a knife. These are the support classes, and are meant to help the rest of the team succeed.
As mentioned this game has objective based gameplay, such as capturing points, stealing intelligence (Capture the Flag), King of the Hill, and several kinds of demolition based missions. So, probably not as advanced as an Enemy Territory game, but probably a bit more mission related flesh than a Battlefront game.
So if you like team based class shooters, give TF2  a try. The base game is free, and the cosmetics are optional. There are a lot of extra weapons available to all players, and new content is added semi regularly, though mostly in the form of cosmetics. Sometimes new weapons are added too. Also, the community is still quite large, and community servers host a barrage of custom maps and content that can enhance the experience.

Alright, gonna change my review from 2014...
I used to LOVE this game. I started playing in 2012 when I was 13 and I am now 18 and an experienced player (not saying I'm the best, just saying I know how things work). After 4 years of playing this game, I retired in 2016. Why? It just got worse...
It's sad to say but valve has put this game on life support, letting it rot and not fixing the ever-lasting issues. Nowadays, hackers rampage through servers, the new matchmaking system is totally unbalanced even though Valve said they made it more "fair" about 3 times, and then, for me, the biggest issue...
It seems like ever since the gun mettle update, hit detection has been utterly ♥♥♥♥ED. As a sniper main, I used to be able to land consistant headshots but now, I was lucky if a shot right in the chest registered. It's like this game rewards players for running on a♥♥♥♥♥♥connection. A Heavy can be standing completely still doing NOTHING and my fully charged 150 damage body shot becomes a 0 damage "miss".
Why, Valve? Do you know how much money I have sunk into this game just to help keep it alive? Hand this game over to the community, I'm sure we could all do a better job and fix the issues you refuse to.
The game's engine has never been updated (not including graphics) since its release and is only getting worse. It's clear that CS:GO is Valve's golden child and TF2 is the step-child trying their best to earn praise from daddy, only to get knocked back down as soon as things get just a little better.

Once you play this game, you never stop. You never stop spending money. You never stop urging to buy crate keys. You never stop urging to buy guns, whether it be rare or vintage. You will never be able to turn back. I am not paid to say this. I think I need help.

Short version:
Pros:
-nine classes with very diverse gameplay
-lots of unlockable weapons (and most are sidegrades, maybe more fun but not needed to win)
-almost ten years(!) of updates, new maps, etc.
-very unique style, both visually and thematically speaking
-lore (seriously, this game has backstory! read the comics, they're amazing)
-a very passionate community
-a small but fun competitive scene (ask me if you want help/mentoring, I'd love to get some more players in the league)
-complicated economy
-hats, so many hats
Cons:
-infrequent updates (Valve just doesn't have the time or manpower to sustain the game like it used to)
-some balance issues with weapons (not glaring but occasionally annoying)
-some bugs have been in the game since the dawn of time
-poorly optimized, very cpu intensive (however there are community made cfg files to help with this, google "Comanglia's config")
Long version:
This game literally changed my life. I'm not even kidding.
I doubt I can say anything about the game that hasn't already been said but I'll try. TF2 has changed a lot over the years, but at it's core it's still the same goofy, bloody shooter. Nine mercs, tons of weapons, too many maps to ever play. Considering the sheer number of variables at work in any given match, it's a miracle that things are even remotely balanced. Sure, there's a neverending debate on that, but it's hard not to scrutinize everything when updates have become relatively infrequent. Ultimately, anyone can hop in and have a blast without ever getting a headache
The comp scene is small but really tight and is actually quite easy to get into. I started with about 40 hours in the game (not that I'd recommend that but it's possible) and have been a part of it ever since. Although Valve's support is very limited here, there are some great community-run leagues that hold multiple seasons a year (plus other small tournaments that pop up here and there). Hit me up if you're interested in participating. I'd love to show you the ropes.
I don't know what else to say. If you haven't played TF2, give it a shot. Maybe it'll be too silly for your tastes, maybe you'll fall in love like I did. It's free, you risk nothing by trying it, but you've got a lot to gain. I'm going to grow old with countless fun memories of this game and the people I've met playing it. I think thousands of other people can say the same.

This game shows true brilliance through the diversity in character and weapon design (mostly character design in my oppinion). I am not that devoted to the game, but in the several hours I have spent with it, the game has been a blast exploring the pros and cons of each class. Everyone in the cast has their own feel and personality with them besides their differences in the way they play, and this makes each class feel fresh even though their only a small cast to select from. When playing as the Heavy class, you get a different personal feeling different from any other class, and the same is true with all the other classes. The game is free to play, and if you would like, you can purchase ingame costumes, taunts, and other things, and these do not make the game play any different. These are completly optional and never give advantage to one player over another. This game has a lot of depth and you could carry on about level design, class balance, etc., but the game is free, so try it yourself! My overall oppinion of the game is possitive, and I enjoy this game a lot.

After playing 1000+ Hours, I might do a re-write of the re-write of my review
Stage 1: Graphics
Everyone knows the cartoony graphics of Team Fortress 2, IMO, the change from a Realistic Shooter that Team Fortress 2 was supposed to be, was a good idea. The graphics are amazing, HD and no lag when at high, hopefully, TF3 (If they actually do make one) has the same graphics from the current game that everyone loves.
Rating: 10/10 - Beautiful Art Design
Stage 2: Gameplay and Mechanics
In the usual FPS, its simple, WASD to move and Mouse 1 to shoot and kill everyone to win. Well, in TF2 its much different, Custom Weapons that allow whole new styles to play, Gamemodes that never get old (Especially Payload and Control Points) and the creative maps, no map is the same except for its gameplay mechanics. One problem I have with this is, they don't have a filter that allows premium players who have higher skill than free to players, this causes unbalance in some teams when a team where its mostly free to players and and other team where its highly skilled players always destroy the other team. As well as the auto balance, it makes people who are about to win then BAM! the player is now on the losing team.
But overall, the mechanics of the game may have little downsides but never stop people from enjoying the gameplay and different weapons.
Rating: 8.5/10 Close to amazing
Final Stage: Community, Updates and Content
First, I'll start with the community, the TF2 Community is amazing, a lot of faithful players who love this game to the very end, but it has some flaws, free to players, These people are so stupid, these players can't even listen to direction, I've tried coaching and it sucks so much, they don't listen to you at all and clueless to what is happening. Second, Premium, those people are mean, in trading they force you to pay more than what its worth, they should add rules to trading, chatting and other things that can effect new players. I hope those who are mean, become good and help those who are new and change the way they play.
Second, Updates, the updates are lacking very lacking, Valve step it up, after some updates, TF2 is losing their community I mean the EotL was overhyped, there was supposed to be new weapons and a new map then Valve says "the map was too confusing for new players" how about rd_asteroid? Even players who played for a long time don't get cp_steel. Basically, step it up Valve.
Finally, Content, there is A LOT of content in this game, mostly hats. They should focus more on weapons than hats. That covers most of that but now, gamemodes, no new game modes for a long time, except for Mann Power but recent players of the Gamemode think its bad. Valve is focusing on hats and bugs.

So the infamous Team Fortress 2!
The game has been around for a long time, 8 years to be exact and was first brought out on Xbox 360 as a bundle (the orange box), still to this day the game has a large community keeping the game alive.
This game is a huge benefactor in the trading community and is constantly having various updates to the game for new items and refreshes to keep the game going.
As most of you already know, Team Fortress 2 is a multiplayer FPS with an objective to defeat the opposing side (been Blu or Red depending on what side you are on) throughout various types of game modes.
The class system consists of 9 characters to pick from:
1.) Scout, a fast agile character primarilly played to get into the enemy base and capture/steal the intellegence.
2.) Soldier, a slow but strong character weilding a rocket launcher, he is played to be offensive and support the team by killing everyone basically.
3.) Pyro, played to be offensive and "spy check" so the spy does not get into your back line and take out your team and sentries etc.
4.) Demoman, a slow character played to support your team by getting into the back line and drop bombs everywhere and destroy their defences and keep the enemies in their spawn.
5.) Heavy, the heavy is a very slow charcter but to make up for this he weilds a minigun and has a tonne of heath, you guessed it, he just sits there as a tank and kills and defends as he pleases.
6.) Engineer, the engineer is solely a defensive character who supports the team. He is very versitile, he builds sentries to defend, sets up teleporters and has a dispenser which regrenerates heath and stocks up on ammo for nearby friendlies.
7.) Medic, as the name says the medic is a support and runs around healing your team, pretty straight forward.
8.) Sniper, now the sniper sits back and defends with his rifle, this character can take out anyone with a single shot, making him a valuable asset to any team.
9.) Spy, the spy supports the team greatly by getting into the back line and to take out the engineers gear, doing so allows the scout to get in the base and capture the points and grab the intellegence. doing so will win the game.
All of these characters fit together and each of them play their own role towards winning the game.
So now we have that out of the way, i would say this is a great game, especially because it's completely free and things you buy from the store or market have no actual affect in game and are purely visual changes to the game which makes it a completely even game so no "Pay 2 Win".
I would definitely reccomend this to anyone who enjoys FPS titles.

It's not your average FPS game.  Unlike, say, Call of Duty, there's 9 different character classes, each of which has a unique set of weapons to use.  Several game modes to enjoy, from your typical deathmatch-style arena mode, to capture the flag, to the co-op mode, Mann vs Machine (you and up to 5 friends vs a horde of robots).  And some of the dialogue is pretty funny, too.  Killed an enemy with an automated sentry gun?  "Now I told you not to touch that darned thing!"  "Another satisfied customer", etc.  All this...and HATS!  Some great-looking, some not-so great looking, and some just downright silly.  If you like FPS games, but also have a good sense of humor, this is probably the game for you.  Want a full account?  Less than 50 cents out of your steam wallet, and you upgrade from free account to full.  Can't argue with that price.

When you come out of the gate as a heavy with a medic in tow, you're a formidable offensive force, but if a spy loops around to backstab the medic and you round the corner on a pyro, it can all come undone in a matter of seconds. Snipers can cover expected enemy paths, but rocket-jumping soldiers have a knack for finding alternative routes and raining explosive death from above. You may think you have a comparatively weak scout dead to rights, only to be stunned by a baseball and beaten to death. As you watch your giblets splatter on the ground and see a freeze-frame of your gleeful killer, it's hard not to chuckle at the sheer variety of ways you can meet an untimely demise. And the humorous quips, ridiculous outfits, and histrionic announcer help cultivate this lighthearted tone.
Of course, this core dynamic has persisted for most of TF2's life span, so if you stopped playing it a few years ago and come back for a few matches, you'll find things are very familiar. Learning the ropes and getting the hang of your chosen role is still a gratifying experience, and mastering advanced techniques doesn't just make you deadlier; it gives you more options for how to approach combat. Keeping your options open is still valuable too, because being flexible with your choice of character can help you avoid ending up on a catastrophically imbalanced squad. It is Team Fortress, after all.
But though there is much that has remained constant about the core game, there have been some notable changes over the years, as well as regular infusions of new weapons and items. Of the hundreds of things available in the online store, some can be unlocked through play, while others must be purchased with actual money. From small doodads that cost less than a dollar to massive bundles that cost hundreds, there's a wide range of ways to customize your experience.
Many of the items offer nothing more than a playful twist on the game's already cheeky cartoon aesthetic. You can buy hats, shirts, shoes, and other cosmetic gear to dress up like a character from Adult Swim or don spooky seasonal garb that you can wear only during Halloween or a full moon. Even if you don't fancy shelling out for any of this stuff, it's fun to see some visual variety as you try to light your opponents on fire.
Other weapons have more of an impact, like the ones that give your character a new chargeable and expendable power. The scout can build hype, which turns his usual double jump into a triple, quadruple, or quintuple jump, and the soldier can build rage, which allows him to rally his nearby teammates to do extra damage. Skills like these have more of a meaningful impact on the action, bringing something new to the table that your enemies must contend with. And then there are the totally out-there loadouts, like the one that turns the grenade-launching demoman into an extra from the movie Braveheart.In addition to the cosmetic options, there are a lot of weapons and items that offer small buffs or subtle tweaks to your attributes. Depending on which healing gun the medic equips, for example, he can imbue himself and his targeted ally with extra damage resistance or enable himself to match the speed of his target. Differences like these don't do much to change the core action, but they do give experienced players substantial room for strategic variation.
