When you come out of the gate as a heavy with a medic in tow, you're a formidable offensive force, but if a spy loops around to backstab the medic and you round the corner on a pyro, it can all come undone in a matter of seconds. Snipers can cover expected enemy paths, but rocket-jumping soldiers have a knack for finding alternative routes and raining explosive death from above. You may think you have a comparatively weak scout dead to rights, only to be stunned by a baseball and beaten to death. As you watch your giblets splatter on the ground and see a freeze-frame of your gleeful killer, it's hard not to chuckle at the sheer variety of ways you can meet an untimely demise. And the humorous quips, ridiculous outfits, and histrionic announcer help cultivate this lighthearted tone.
Of course, this core dynamic has persisted for most of TF2's life span, so if you stopped playing it a few years ago and come back for a few matches, you'll find things are very familiar. Learning the ropes and getting the hang of your chosen role is still a gratifying experience, and mastering advanced techniques doesn't just make you deadlier; it gives you more options for how to approach combat. Keeping your options open is still valuable too, because being flexible with your choice of character can help you avoid ending up on a catastrophically imbalanced squad. It is Team Fortress, after all.
But though there is much that has remained constant about the core game, there have been some notable changes over the years, as well as regular infusions of new weapons and items. Of the hundreds of things available in the online store, some can be unlocked through play, while others must be purchased with actual money. From small doodads that cost less than a dollar to massive bundles that cost hundreds, there's a wide range of ways to customize your experience.
Many of the items offer nothing more than a playful twist on the game's already cheeky cartoon aesthetic. You can buy hats, shirts, shoes, and other cosmetic gear to dress up like a character from Adult Swim or don spooky seasonal garb that you can wear only during Halloween or a full moon. Even if you don't fancy shelling out for any of this stuff, it's fun to see some visual variety as you try to light your opponents on fire.
Other weapons have more of an impact, like the ones that give your character a new chargeable and expendable power. The scout can build hype, which turns his usual double jump into a triple, quadruple, or quintuple jump, and the soldier can build rage, which allows him to rally his nearby teammates to do extra damage. Skills like these have more of a meaningful impact on the action, bringing something new to the table that your enemies must contend with. And then there are the totally out-there loadouts, like the one that turns the grenade-launching demoman into an extra from the movie Braveheart.In addition to the cosmetic options, there are a lot of weapons and items that offer small buffs or subtle tweaks to your attributes. Depending on which healing gun the medic equips, for example, he can imbue himself and his targeted ally with extra damage resistance or enable himself to match the speed of his target. Differences like these don't do much to change the core action, but they do give experienced players substantial room for strategic variation.
These options broaden the field of viable strategies, which helps keep combat lively and varied. And fortunately, none of the purchasable weapons or items tip the scales unfairly towards those willing to pay. Buffs and bonuses usually come with caveats, and the weapons that bestow new abilities are usually unlocked for free. For this review, I spent some money on goofy hats and some of the stranger weaponry on offer, like the pyro's flamethrower that actually shoots bubbles and rainbows. It was fun to play with the new gear, but I still found myself switching my loadout between free and paid weapons regularly to adapt to the match situation.

Total Noob's Guide To the Nine Classes Of TF2
This guide is meant for people who have never played this game before.
, all with a unique, distinct playstyle and multiple styles of play for each. Each has a distinct sillhouette and body shape so you can easily tell what you're up against or have on your side with a glance. Unlike other popular FPS like Call of Duty or Battlefield, the
with one or two different weapons. Each class has 3 weapons or tools, and the only items shared between classes are the Shotgun (Soldier, Pyro, Heavy, Engineer) and Pistol (Scout & Engineer). Each class also has
, with many weapons giving or removing max health, like the Battalion's Backup for Soldier, which takes away your shotgun in exchange for +20 max health and a special ability you gain by dealing damage that lets you temporarily make yourself and nearby teammates take 35% less damage from all sources. There are
, from running to jumping to blowing your own feet up and riding the explosion.
by other classes. This means that a certain class is particularly effective at killing another.

A fast-talking Boston kid, the Scout is the fastest class in the game by a large margin. He runs at 133% base speed, and can double-jump to reach high areas. His default loadout is composed of a Scattergun, which is a specialized shotgun that does bonus damage at close range, a Pistol, which does less damage than the Scattergun but is more accurate at long range, and the Bat, a baseball bat that does less damage, but attacks faster than the melee weapons of other classes. The scout can deal more damage at close range than almost any other class, able to do up to 105 damage a Scattergun shot, with almost 2 shots a seconds. However, this is balanced by the fact that the Scout is tied for the least amount of health, with only 125. Counters Demoman. Is countered by Engineer.

An American patriot, who loves nothing more than his God-given land, the Soldier is considered the most balanced class in the game by many. His many loadout options give him huge versatility in almost any situation. His health, the second-highest in the game at 200, is countered by his incredibly slow speed, at 80%. However, both of those facts can be negated by rocket-jumping, which is the act of flying through the air, propelled by the explosion of his own Rocket Launcher. This can be quite self-damaging, but a skilled rocket jumper can beat even the fastest scouts in a race. His default loadout consists of a Rocket Launcher, which can do up to about 90 splash damage, a Shotgun, for enemies so close you'll hurt yourself if you use your Rocket Launcher, and a Shovel, which is statistically identical to most of the stock melee weapons, with medium damage and speed. The soldier can 'juggle' targets in the air with his Rocket Launcher's knockback, and can easily kill large groups or Sentries from a distance. However, he does not counter any class to a large extent, nor is he countered by any class much. He is slightly more effective against Engineers, however, but a good Pyro can shut down a Soldier.

A mumbling, unintelligible thing, nobody knows much about the Pyro. Its health, at 175, is tied for third-most, and its speed is average, at 100%. The Pyro's default loadout consists of a Flamethrower, which can both light enemies on fire for afterburn damage and a secondary fire blast of compressed air, reflecting projectiles like rockets and
. Its loadout also includes a Shotgun, the same as used by the Soldier, but for Pyro, it is more effective at medium range, where targets cannot be reached by the small range of the Flamethrower. Its loadout also includes a Fire Axe, identical gameplay-wise to the Soldier's shovel. The pyro's most glaring weakness is its complete lack of accurate long-range weapons. Even with unlocks, Pyro has no weapons that can hit a moving target at long range with any degree of accuracy. However, the Pyro's afterburn has a psychological effect as well as damage, as burning enemies will often flee in search of a healthkit or Medic instead of staying to fight. The pyro is by and large the most effective Spy-killer, as the flames will short out the Spy's cloaking device and kill him in seconds. Well-timed use of the airblast also makes Pyro the closest thing to a Soldier counter in the game, able to kill the soldier by reflecting his own rockets back at him. However, the Pyro is destroyed at close range by the Heavy, as he has enough health to survive a few moments of fire, and his close-range damage is far more than the pyro's.

A one-eyed drunkard from Scotland, the Demoman is famous for having the highest damage of any class in the game. His health, at 175, and speed, just below average at 93%, make him a force to be reckoned with. His default loadout consists of the Grenade launcher, which fires grenades, also known as 'pills' or 'pipes' that bounce off of walls and roll on the floor; they will explode on contact if they hit an enemy before they hit the floor. His loadout also includes the Stickybomb Launcher, considered balanced by some and overpowered by others. This weapon allows the Demoman to fire bombs that will stick to walls and floors, and detonate them whenever he wants with a right-click. The bombs do slightly more damage then a Soldier's rockets, and up to 8 can be placed at once, making the Sticky Launcher a powerful offensive, as well as defensive, weapon. His melee weapon is a bottle o' scrumpy, which behaves identically to the Shovel and Fire Axe. The Demoman can sticky jump with his Stickybomb Launcher, similar to the Soldier's Rocket Jump. The Sticky Jump, however, is more challenging, more self-damaging, and propels you further and faster. The Demoman's biggest weakness is a lack of hitscan weapons. Hitscan is when you do damage on what you click on the moment you click, like a sniper rifle or pistol. The Demo has no hitscan weapons at all, even with unlocks. This means that a class that is hard to hit with projectiles like pipes or stickies, like the Scout, can kill a Demo with ease. The Demoman is the best class at dealing with Engineer nests, however, able to destroy every building and player in one with just four or five stickies.

A massive weapons enthusiast from Eastern Siberia, the Heavy Weapons Guy is the biggest, fattest, and slowest class in the game. At 77% speed, he is almost painfully slow, but with 300 health, incredibly hard to kill. His default loadout consists of a Minigun, with massive damage, but a long spin-up and spindown time, as well as reduced movement speed when firing, as well as the Pyro and Soldier's shotgun. His melee weapon, identical to most, are his own bare fists; he punches with the same power as being hit with a fire axe or pipe wrench. He makes a great Medic buddy, due to his large health and size forming a human shield for the medic. He excels in killing Pyros, due to his high health and damage at the Pyro's only effective range. However, his slowness leaves him vulnerable to the instant-kill abilities of Spies and Snipers.

An amiable fellow from Bee Cave, Texas, the Engineer has 11 PhDs and a penchant for technology. He has only 125 health, tied for lowest, and moves at 100% speed, the standard. Let's start with the fact, that I have never write any review, so don't be too harash with mine, please.
Team Fortress 2. What can be said about this game? Some people might just look at it and say: "Regular FPS. You play with maybe even 100+ people a day, and shoot to win." Or is it?
What I like mostly about TF2, is the fact that everything there is build on the TEAMWORK. After all, this is called "TEAM Fortress 2", not "Deathmatch Fortress 2". Playing as a lone wolf will lead you to no where, and even eventually make you rage quit from playing this game. For good.
It's not about your high score, or how many kills you get at the end of the round. (altough it still motivate you to fight more and shows that you are the experienced player to others) It's all about doing the objective together with your team, to win the game. And every new game there is completely different than previous one, so working together as a team is really important with every challenge that comes with every new game mode, team members and map the game is going on of course.
So we already know, this game is all about team work, and doing current game objective. Got it? Good, and keep it that way!
Let's go with the next thing - weapons! Even though there's not many of them, as the cosmetic items (that would be something) there's still a lot of them, to pick and choose from. And most of the weapons usually change to way of playing your current class, so it makes the game even more interesting and challenging. We have weapons that heal or overheal you on killing your opponent, slow down enemies who are shot, gives you speed boost, hurt enemy after attacking him... the list is long, every weapon have it's pros and cons, so everyone can choose, try out every weapon and  stick with it, as this style of fighting with it fits him most. Thus makes your gameplay completely different everytime you join on a random server, with new random people.
More guns = more fun. Check them out, and find your style. That's our conclusion here. One tip though - every time you will get a new weapon, don't think you have advanced to a next level or something and this new weapon is way better than the previous one! Carry on...
Classes you're playing! There are 9 playable classes in game, avalible from the beggining, so there's no any "This class avalible after reaching that level." No. You can play as who do you want, from the beggining. So you can try out every game style and see which one fits you most, as with every class you're playing completely diffrently than with previous one. So, the classes are: Scout, Soldier, Pyro, Demoman, Heavy, Engineer, Medic, Sniper and (my favourite) Spy. Every class have it's pros and cons, just like the weapons you can get so the choice of your favourite one are a little easier. For example - Scout is the fastest one of all the classes, can make double jumps and even capture points 2 times faster than anyone else. But he is really easy to kill in battle, unless you're good at dodging incomming spam of bullets and rockets. Much better for a frontal attack are classes like Soldier, armed with his rocket launcher and the possibility to do a "Rocket Jump" to help him reach bigger distances in a short time, due to the fact he's really slow. But that's just a short example of everything that each class is avalible of. And honestly? Too lazy to write down all of them, that's all... meh.
Worth to mention, that every class have it's own personality, which makes them a bit more cooler and interesting to play with. Another example? Fine. Scout is pretty much kind of a cocky guy, who likes to annoy others, and think that every girl wants him, and every guy wish to be like him. Soldier is a stereotypical example of an American patriot, who most likely lost all his brain cells durning WW2. Heavy is a very calm and serious guy, until his minigun starts to spin and the battle starts. Then he's like a wild, angry bear, that hates people. And so it goes as well, with the other 6 classes.
So, 9 different mercs for a usually 12-24 teams. Sounds cool? Because it is... that is, until most of them are only Spies or Snipers.
Exactly, most of the players think that this game is like CoD - thus they go full sniper force, believing they have nailed everything. No, no, NO! This game is nothing like CoD! A team full of snipers, will never win. I was once in a team where out of 10 players we had 8 snipers, one spy and a soldier which was me. So, I think you can say how that round went? (inb4 MLG jokes) So, what I mean is - teamwork is important, we know that. But, when there's not enough classes that will provide enough firepower for the team, the teamwork won't help you much, or does not exist there at all.
Okay, time to move on to...
HATS!
This is something completely random, that makes this game unique. In this game, you can wear on every class a nice and fancy hat, or other cosmetic, that will make you look diffrent from the others. Here's my question - can you wear a hat in every other FPS, than Team Fortress 2? No. Or dance Conga? Of course not. Or being a total annoying brat and taunting after every kill, no matter how much skill you put into your kill? Of course not! Another reason why TF2 is so unique, and why we love it so much.
Okay, slowly getting tired of thinking what to poot here.
So, conclusion time!
Team Fortress 2 is an awesome game, unique in her own beautiful way and great to play. I recommend playing it, together with your friends! "But they have no money..." This game's free! Just download, learn how to play and get good!
The only thing that makes me really angry about this game are most of the time unbalanced teams, the autobalance curse in the worst possible moment of the round, or the fact the prices are getting higer in its shop...

TF2 is a really addictive and fun game. It's a cartoony sort of shooter and is a must have for any pc gamer who enjoys a good First Person Shooter. It's not serious, like it's counter part CS:GO, it's just a game to relax and have a good bit of fun.

If you're looking for a serious game where you can try-hard your little panties off, than head over to CS:GO where the rest of the try-hard community (myself included) will welcome you with open arms.
The downside to the game is that not all weapons are available to you immediately, you must either find the guns or buy them from the shop. DON'T WASTE YOUR MONEY ON THE IN-GAME ITEMS, YOU WILL REGRET IT.
Overall I would give this game a 7.5/10 :D

I actually really like TF2, BUT and this is the game breaking but, it's not something I feel like just starting out I could really get into.
I've played enough rounds to realize that a lot of the people who play already have top tier gear. Time and time again I'll be one shotted -- even playing a heavy -- by somebody with some LE piece of gear that's incredibly OP. I honestly don't know how many times I've died five feet out of the start gate killed in a single shot by a sniper.
It's not fun to be repeatedly killed by somebody camping the spawn point either as a spy or a sniper picking people off as they come back. It doesn't always last, normally somebody on your team has OP LE gear as well or has been playing just as long and can help kill over the people doing it, but, it happens often enough that it's a problem.
What I enjoy about TF2 is that when you actually play against people around your skill level it's well balanced. I've played several games against a group of all new players like I was, and those were some of the closest most exciting matches. It's a fun game and a great concept! My complaint isn't about the game itself so much as the way multiplayer works.
When I play with teams of vets who all know the best routes and have great gear, I just feel useless.
Sure, I could play enough to get good gear -- but it's not in my nature to essentially freeload, or worse hinder, a team because I'm the weak link until I get to that point. I'm also not really interested in paying real money to buy gear on the marketplace. I don't think having good gear would fix lack of experience and so I like to play and earn my gear the old fashioned way.
There's just currently not a great way to do that.
But, if you like MMOs and are willing to overlook their weaknesses as a class (vets vs. new players being the big one here) then TF2 is one of the funniest most enjoyable one out there! Just know what you're getting into starting out, because I feel like if you can get over that initial "hump" it would be a great game.
Pros
+ Updated content regularly
+ Lots of players
Cons
- Hard to first start out
- Marketplace heavy

Over the last 8 years Valve (and its community) have been refining elements to Team Fortress 2, adding new content and catering to the fans. The game has greatly evolved in many elements; the most prominent being the 'free to play' model. Fortunately, this 'free to play' model is unlike most other games in that the content is not too severely restricted. Regardless, this game is worth full retail price and then some and contains some of the most fun I have had in any shooter for years, easily outranking the likes of Call of Duty and even Battlefield.
The most jarring element to this game is also its most well balanced and thought out in the whole game - the classes, of which there are nine. When I first saw the class selection screen I was worried that I was getting into an overly complicated and difficult game to truly understand, but shortly after I found I was constantly switching between classes to turn the tides of the match. Each class has its own unique playstyle and surprisingly intricate backstories and personalities. Whether you are playing as the distinctively Australian Sniper, the stereotypically German madman Medic, or the 'black, Scottish cyclops' that is the Demoman, the classes will keep you coming back for months on end, wanting to find new items and perfect your techniques. The unique World War 2 cartoon-y art style gives a lasting and memorable impression which I will forever associate with TF2.
In case you didn't know, Team Fortress 2 is a class based shooter, heavily reliant on objectives and teamwork. Each class has its own roles and weapons to mess around with and are generally well balanced. There are several different game modes, ranging from 'Payload' which sees one team trying to move a cart to the end of a rail with the other trying to stop them, to 'Control Points' which sees two teams attempt to gain control of multiple different points on the map.
The community is a hugely important part of Team Fortress 2; nowadays most of the items introduced into the game (of which there are many) are created by the fans. Content creators can enter their ideas into the workshop for approval of Valve and the best are added into the game. The community can even make their own game modes and maps such as 'Death Run' which sees one person trying to stop a team cross an obstable course by deploting traps.
Items are one of the most addicting parts in this game. All the different weapons, hats, and other aesthetic items will keep you laughing and wanting to find more to complete your character builds. Some favourites of mine are the 'B.A.S.E Jumper' which allows you to deploy a parachute in mid-air and the 'Crusader's Crossbow' which is a ranged weapon for the medic which both heals allies and damages enemies. Unfortunately some items can be hard to come by and you may end up having to buy some from the in game store. I was happy to do this however, as the game is free anyway.
Here are some basic pros and cons to the game:-
+ Deep, balanced class systems.
+ Well thought out items.
+ Community items, maps and game modes keep the game fresh.
+ It's free!
+ Well structured maps and game modes.
+ Characters have interesting personalities.
+ The game is constantly being updated with new content and is still going strong even after eight years!
- In-game community can be a little dodgy.
- Items are frustrating to come by.
- Halloween restricted items should not exist!
You have no excuse not to give this game a try; it is free and one of the greatest, most balanced shooters you will ever play in your life.
~ Dovahkiwi

I actually really like TF2, BUT and this is the game breaking but, it's not something I feel like just starting out I could really get into.
I've played enough rounds to realize that a lot of the people who play already have top tier gear. Time and time again I'll be one shotted -- even playing a heavy -- by somebody with some LE piece of gear that's incredibly OP. I honestly don't know how many times I've died five feet out of the start gate killed in a single shot by a sniper.
It's not fun to be repeatedly killed by somebody camping the spawn point either as a spy or a sniper picking people off as they come back. It doesn't always last, normally somebody on your team has OP LE gear as well or has been playing just as long and can help kill over the people doing it, but, it happens often enough that it's a problem.
What I enjoy about TF2 is that when you actually play against people around your skill level it's well balanced. I've played several games against a group of all new players like I was, and those were some of the closest most exciting matches. It's a fun game and a great concept! My complaint isn't about the game itself so much as the way multiplayer works.
When I play with teams of vets who all know the best routes and have great gear, I just feel useless.
Sure, I could play enough to get good gear -- but it's not in my nature to essentially freeload, or worse hinder, a team because I'm the weak link until I get to that point. I'm also not really interested in paying real money to buy gear on the marketplace. I don't think having good gear would fix lack of experience and so I like to play and earn my gear the old fashioned way.
There's just currently not a great way to do that.
But, if you like MMOs and are willing to overlook their weaknesses as a class (vets vs. new players being the big one here) then TF2 is one of the funniest most enjoyable one out there! Just know what you're getting into starting out, because I feel like if you can get over that initial "hump" it would be a great game.
Pros
+ Updated content regularly
+ Lots of players
Cons
- Hard to first start out
- Marketplace heavy

My experience playing TF2 for over a year now has been fun but has come to my thoughts why so many people♥♥♥♥♥♥on this game. I mean, I do understand half the reasons why but that doesn't bother me and the insanity of people just wanting hats all the time,(Not to mention all the F2P's). The Game has good brilliant gameplay and all classes are equally balance exect a little nerves on the Medic or Spy. Weapons are even out for all classes, My Personal Favorites are the gunslinger(Even though its probably the most useless weapon in the game), The Sandvich for the Heavy Since I can heal myself and other players, and finally the Degreaser for the Pyro,(Being it the only useful Flamethrower for him/her in the game). The Maps are even out as well, Personal Favorites,2Fort,BadLands,Turbine and Doomsday. MvM is also equal but some classes like Sniper,Scout,or even Spy are kinda useless in this mode. Upgrades are Evened out for classes and also for different weapons like The Direct Hit or The Loose Cannon. Power Up Canteens are very useful as well for the mode, I mainly use mine for extra crits or instant ubercharge. Now I do have some problems about the game that do get on my nerves, for 1: Sometimes I get on TF2 and my items are not working and I have to wait for a while just for the item server to work. Another thing is that I sometimes get the occasional "Servers are Unavilable" Thing and also somehow I'm still on a server playing still with no problems even though my internet connection isn't working! Some Maps on Gamemodes can sometimes be also like MvM were some classes can be useless like Sniper. Either way, TF2 is a fantastic FPS for all gamers. Some Games like Call Of Duty might be wearing out and gamers want a new game and so TF2 is a perfect new experience for those gamers. And probably the people that first bought TF2 7 Years ago are still around playing(mostly all of them). And Hopefully I will still be around playing TF2 with people for quite a long time!

Over the last 8 years Valve (and its community) have been refining elements to Team Fortress 2, adding new content and catering to the fans. The game has greatly evolved in many elements; the most prominent being the 'free to play' model. Fortunately, this 'free to play' model is unlike most other games in that the content is not too severely restricted. Regardless, this game is worth full retail price and then some and contains some of the most fun I have had in any shooter for years, easily outranking the likes of Call of Duty and even Battlefield.
The most jarring element to this game is also its most well balanced and thought out in the whole game - the classes, of which there are nine. When I first saw the class selection screen I was worried that I was getting into an overly complicated and difficult game to truly understand, but shortly after I found I was constantly switching between classes to turn the tides of the match. Each class has its own unique playstyle and surprisingly intricate backstories and personalities. Whether you are playing as the distinctively Australian Sniper, the stereotypically German madman Medic, or the 'black, Scottish cyclops' that is the Demoman, the classes will keep you coming back for months on end, wanting to find new items and perfect your techniques. The unique World War 2 cartoon-y art style gives a lasting and memorable impression which I will forever associate with TF2.
In case you didn't know, Team Fortress 2 is a class based shooter, heavily reliant on objectives and teamwork. Each class has its own roles and weapons to mess around with and are generally well balanced. There are several different game modes, ranging from 'Payload' which sees one team trying to move a cart to the end of a rail with the other trying to stop them, to 'Control Points' which sees two teams attempt to gain control of multiple different points on the map.
The community is a hugely important part of Team Fortress 2; nowadays most of the items introduced into the game (of which there are many) are created by the fans. Content creators can enter their ideas into the workshop for approval of Valve and the best are added into the game. The community can even make their own game modes and maps such as 'Death Run' which sees one person trying to stop a team cross an obstable course by deploting traps.
Items are one of the most addicting parts in this game. All the different weapons, hats, and other aesthetic items will keep you laughing and wanting to find more to complete your character builds. Some favourites of mine are the 'B.A.S.E Jumper' which allows you to deploy a parachute in mid-air and the 'Crusader's Crossbow' which is a ranged weapon for the medic which both heals allies and damages enemies. Unfortunately some items can be hard to come by and you may end up having to buy some from the in game store. I was happy to do this however, as the game is free anyway.
Here are some basic pros and cons to the game:-
+ Deep, balanced class systems.
+ Well thought out items.
+ Community items, maps and game modes keep the game fresh.
+ It's free!
+ Well structured maps and game modes.
+ Characters have interesting personalities.
+ The game is constantly being updated with new content and is still going strong even after eight years!
- In-game community can be a little dodgy.
- Items are frustrating to come by.
- Halloween restricted items should not exist!
You have no excuse not to give this game a try; it is free and one of the greatest, most balanced shooters you will ever play in your life.
~ Dovahkiwi

First of all, I love Team Fortress 2
My friends introduced me to this game years ago and I've been playing ever since. TF2 is still a game I play every now and again, but I am finding an increasing number of cons to outweigh the pros in this game.
Ever since I hit around 1000 hours I've noticed that the public servers are all the same. There are the new, "bad" players that don't know exactly what the're doing, and the very game-savvy "pub-stompers" that are the more experienced players. There really are no in betweens in this game.
Also, most of the updates are cookie cutter, releasing the same thing every time. A new map or two, some weapons, a taunt, some changes, and some more crates to feed valve more money. Some acceptions to this are, The Uber Update, which made the game free, The Tale Of Two Cities Update, which expanded on the fun and exciting mvm gamemode, and the Gun-Mettle Update, which initially introduced weapon skins and contracts to, in my opinion, copy CS:GO.
The community is becoming increasingly more toxic and divided as more and more updates fertalize the rift between is it "OP" or not, or, is this a♥♥♥♥♥♥update or not. Its really nothing like the interactive community I came into the game with.
If you took the time to read that, thank you. If not, tl:dr Even though this is probably a one of the funnest free-to-play games I've ever experienced,the increasingly toxic community and cookie-cutter updates are slowly killing the game.

I can gladly say, as of this review, this game is 95% of my free time. The game is so addicting.  The 9 classes are all perfecty balanced, and there is not a single class that stands atop the rest. Any of the classes can be someone's favorite (For example, the Heavy could be someone's favorite, and so can the Sniper, and the Pyro (My class of choice)). All of the classes have at least three different strategies (I.E: The Pyro can be a strategic Pyro (Airblasting at the right time, switching when necessary, ect.), a Spy-checker, or pull off the infamous W+M1 strategy) that can all work well. Every class has a different use, and a whole team of one single class just won't work.
The weapons are also properly balanced too (Aside from the sun-on-a-stick). Very few of them are just direct upgrades to the stock weapons. For example, all three watches are all so viable. The C&D is perfect for patient players. The Dead Ringer is great for escaping tight situations (Though Pyros will easily counter this, unless you use Spy-cicle). The normal watch is the basic watch, and can still be used just as well as the Dead Ringer and Cloak and Dagger with the increased cloak time, the ability to collect cloak from ammo boxes and the quieter decloak noise.
And the game is so much fun! One thing that TF2 has over some other FPS games, such as Call of Duty and Battlefield, is that the classes all have their own personalities, making them more fun characters  than the generic CoD characters that have bland personalities (Though I admit the Administrator is a bit dry in personality.).  Gameplay-wise, the many ways to play and the many other mechanics (Dropping, Crafting, Trading) will leave you coming back for more almost every day.
Overall, Team Fortress 2 is an extremely fun and balanced game that will have you playing for hours on end. I recommend this to anyone that is a fan of First-person shooters, and to people trying to get into FPS games.

Team fortress 2 is a game that is as great as the portress. You play on various maps, no matter what I always find it hilarious. You play as one of 9 mercenaries from different countries, on each map there is no gap, designed tactically so that every class can be able to kick some♥♥♥♥♥equally.

You can distract a sentry with a chug of bonk from another entry and with one konk from a mate that sentries fate is decided. Or grab the intel and run like hell has broken out in the area for fun.
If scout is annoying and you want someone with a louder shout, you could go soldier the man who is as scary as a boulder, armed with a rocket launcher the results are grandly stauncher! You have multiple banners an trumpets, each with different manners of effect to protect your allies, or boost them to the enemies roost. Or if you're bored, get out a shovel and pulverize the enemy like they've been hiding in a hovel.
But if you want to be a drunken scott, you certainly can and its as fun as being shocked by 1000 electrical watts! You fight with a grenade launcher and a bottle, or a blade if you want to add onto the throttle. Pull out the eyelander and charge'n'targe to pander to your sick barge. Fight your best to destroy whatever pest is attempting to melee fight, because clearly they weren't that bright to fight a drunken man who can stomp you like a tin can.
Or if you want to dawn a gas mask for my favourite class, the pyro spewing fire to change enemy attire into ash, while you laugh and dash in to smash their heads with an axe. A psychopath who doesn't hesitate to unleash his wrath upon the map. Charred and scarred bodies in burning coal mines, which is probably costly in fines. But with flare in hand do you dare to land a critical strike, and extinguish your cohorts while they're burning like a shrike.
Or to easily kill a tankier enemy just become a ♥♥♥♥♥♥, with the sniper a foot blowing heads open from the root, of where you stand which I find very grand. The satisfaction from their reaction and watching the brain matter patter to the ground. You have a smg and a shield to help protect you in the field, but if that’s not enough you got a machete for when things get tough. Or if you're normal you can be very formal, with jarate in a jar you chuck from far soaking the enemies in urine.
Better yet do not fret, pick up a minigun and have a lot of fun. Mowing down the opposition with destructive suppression, enjoying a sandvich whenever you find yourself cornered in a ditch. Though it'd be wise to use it to help heal allies, cooperation is a major key to the enemies destruction. But if angry, break out a tangy steak, and go break an enemy’s face with your fist, each hit spilling so much blood like a huge mist.
Or to become near immortal and quite vital to your teams survival, you could become the medic an interesting pick. You stay close to the group not wanting to stray, with a medigun in hand you run with your crew to ruin the enemy like a bad bowl of stew. With an ubercharge you make a huge barge. Critical strikes or ubercharges for real, which are very analytical when they deal true damage. If cornered don't get bothered get your ubersaw out and cut the enemy like a cat paw, use a crossbow when you need to allow for long range heal. A medical vow which Is very high brow, to do no harm but I laugh while making a human limb farm.
If camping is what you prefer pardner, than look for farther. Be smarter and barter with sentries a lot of kills which fills my heart, watching so many die to my sentries like pennies on the sidewalk. You can help your cohorts with some teleports, teleporters ready to help steady the fight on the front which I'll be quite blunt, is wasted often because someone became somewhat too soften. Building them five steps away from spawn, a major thrive to a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ swan. To aid the fight an supply the braid of the team, a dispenser can help condenser the teams health. But again it is wasted like a pasted chain, kept mostly beside the sentry to guard an entry instead of make a fight quite tight. But if its a bore grab a mini sentry and even the score, get in on the combat being as threatening as a gnat.
But if you want to be subtle like a cuttle, pick up a watch and attempt to botch the enemy’s defenses, forcing them to hesitate their offenses. Disguise yourself and chastise the enemy for trusting you, before busting their spine with a fine knife to the back. Go through an odd entry, and sap the engies sentry. When he charges aim your ambassador, like a bally matador and headshot them right on the spot. Before cloaking away to enjoy more smoking while choking the tactics of the enemy.

That aside I play it competitive as well I find it hard to get repetitive.
To drop the rhyme for a moment, I have to be honest. Without this game, I'd of been bored so often. And I've met some of the greatest people, and my best friends through this game. No matter what I will love this game, I may have arrived late to the party only joining a few years ago, but I will always be happy to be a part of the team fortress 2 community.

-Nice graphics, always

-Allow community weapons and maps

-Coop mode or pvp mode
-Ability to choose custom server
-Balanced 9 class :
Scout : fast but low health
Soldier : High blast but slow projectile speed
Pyro : High damage and flame but close range
Demoman : High blast but inconvenient
Heavy : Deadly but slow
Medic : Healing ability but low damage
Sniper : High bullet damage but slow firing speed
Spy : High damage at enemy's back but slow attack
-Love gibbing enemies
Cons :
-Buying things cost money, always
-People only talk about unusual, rare and collector's
-The war gets ruined when people start "conga" ing after the Love and War updates
-Always get stabbed IN THE FRONT
Overall :
Always be loved, always perfect.

This review/rating can be divided into two sections pre/post F2P(June 23, 2011).  It is very important to distinguish between these two because they are really two different games.
Pre-F2P TF2  (10/10) - For the first few years of TF2's existence, the game managed to have an absolute killer dynamic with a great playerbase that relied heavily on teamwork and a great community fostered by Valve's friendliness to the modding community.  Valve really worked with the community to create new scenarios, maps, and weapons these first few years that helped vastly improve the game.
Post-F2P TF2 (5/10) - The easiest way to describe the state of the game today would be a male dress-up Barbie simulator.  I don't fault Valve for trying to capitalize on a game that is at the time of this writing over 7 years old, but the best times for this game are now well past.  There's just too many new hats and new weapons to choose from, from which the majority are useless.  Sure there are still plenty of servers to play in, but the majority of the servers are devoid of players with skill, microphones, and teamwork.  There's still a few fun servers (see the No-Heroes servers) but donating is about the only way you will be able to see the inside of one of these servers when its full.  The only bright side is that Valve is still adding new content with multiple updates a year.
This is a very fun, chaotic multiplayer game that is sometimes overwhelming but is still amazingly addictive.

What is Team Fortress 2?
Team Fortress 2 (commonly abbreviated as TF2) is a team-based first-person shooter (FPS) multiplayer video game developed by Valve Corporation. It is a sequel to the original mod Team Fortress based on the Source engine. It was first released as part of the video game compilation The Orange Box on October 10, 2007 for Windows and the Xbox 360. A PlayStation 3 version then followed on November 22, 2007. The game was later released as a standalone package for Windows on April 9, 2008, and for Mac OS X two years later. Team Fortress 2 is distributed online through the Steam system, while retail distribution was handled by Electronic Arts. On June 23, 2011, the Windows version of the game became a free-to-play title, supported by micro-transactions for unique in-game equipment through Steam. The development of Team Fortress 2 is led by John Cook and Robin Walker, who originally created the Team Fortress modification for Quake in 1996.

At first, I thought Team Fortress 2 was a fantastic game. It was a solid team based FPS with an interesting variety of classes and many weapons and items for all of said classes. It seemed great. After a while of playing it, I have realised how boring it is.
My problem is that really to have fun, you need to have lots of these weapons to add variety (because otherwise it is repetitive). The only problem is that you have to earn these weapons or trade for them - and by the time you've done all that (which is, again, repetitive and boring), you are tired of playing the game anyway because all you've done is sit around and trade or do the exact same thing over and over.
Then there are the people that you may encounter in the servers:
Mic-spammers.
High-pitched annoying people (raging or asking to trade mostly).
Spawn Campers.
Etc.
(But that stuff is usually on all games with a mic or whatever)
I would recommend this game if I felt that you didn't  have to earn the fun rather than just get into the game and have fun right away.

It used to be THE BEST free game a few years ago. FREAKING AMAZING FUN Team Fortress 2 !!!!!!
I loved the game, I loved the whole concept of playing classes with different roles, strenghts and downsides, all of it combined into a shooter. And to some extent it's still the same game it was a few years ago, with some changes regarding the matchmaking.
However this is the exact problem with TF2. IT'S THE SAME ♥♥♥♥ING GAME. It was fun for a while, I love the game at its very core, but the issues it had weren't ever fixed + Valve makes some poor decisions with each update:
- random crits still exist and to me they have absolutely no purpose in this game
- the pyro flame spread is a mess and fighting vs 5 of them in the enemy team is annoying as ♥♥♥♥
- the shotgun bullet spread isn't consistent with every shot leading to some unfair situation
- there is little to no balance in the casual matchmaking
- the game is horrendous for begginers. There is basically a very minimal tutorial for just 4 classes in the game, where they teach you almost nothing. Then you go into a regular server, get killed 20 times(without knowing actually why) and probably never touch the game again. That's where TF2 is losing a lot of the player base.
- competitive is a bad joke, the only way to really play competitive is through UGC and ETF2L, both being quite elitist and non-enjoyable without a proper team
- hackers are still quite common
- weapon balance is a joke
- the levels you get in matchmaking games are useless, they don't give you any sense of progression, you just get an ugly badge that doesn't do anything at all. Having a high level doesn't queue you up with better players and the points you receive aren't skill based.
And the list can go on...
I know the TF2 team is dedicated and trying to do their very best at improving whatever remained from TF2, but I feel their effort is irrelevant, the age of TF2 is dead.
I really feel the next step in the evolution of this genre is Overwatch. And I know my review will get plenty of hate for saying that, but it's the raw truth.
I just can't recommend this game for new players. Go and play a game with a community that's thriving, with real youtube and twitch coverage, with a proper learning curve for begginers. TF2 did some of these things for a while (except the last part), but now it is slowly dying. Play Overwatch, play Paladins, play a MOBA, play a TCG, but I don't recommend you TF2.

It was first released as part of the video game compilation The Orange Box on October 10, 2007 for Windows and the Xbox 360. A PlayStation 3 version then followed on November 22, 2007. The game was later released as a standalone package for Windows on April 9, 2008, and for Mac OS X two years later. Team Fortress 2 is distributed online through the Steam system, while retail distribution was handled by Electronic Arts. On June 23, 2011, the Windows version of the game became a free-to-play title, supported by micro-transactions for unique in-game equipment through Steam. The development of Team Fortress 2 is led by John Cook and Robin Walker, who originally created the Team Fortress modification for Quake in 1996.

The only problem is that you have to earn these weapons or trade for them - and by the time you've done all that (which is, again, repetitive and boring), you are tired of playing the game anyway because all you've done is sit around and trade or do the exact same thing over and over.
Then there are the people that you may encounter in the servers:
Mic-spammers.
High-pitched annoying people (raging or asking to trade mostly).
Spawn Campers.
Etc.
(But that stuff is usually on all games with a mic or whatever)
I would recommend this game if I felt that you didn't  have to earn the fun rather than just get into the game and have fun right away.

It used to be THE BEST free game a few years ago. FREAKING AMAZING FUN Team Fortress 2 !!!!!!
I loved the game, I loved the whole concept of playing classes with different roles, strenghts and downsides, all of it combined into a shooter. And to some extent it's still the same game it was a few years ago, with some changes regarding the matchmaking.
However this is the exact problem with TF2. IT'S THE SAME ♥♥♥♥ING GAME. It was fun for a while, I love the game at its very core, but the issues it had weren't ever fixed + Valve makes some poor decisions with each update:
- random crits still exist and to me they have absolutely no purpose in this game
- the pyro flame spread is a mess and fighting vs 5 of them in the enemy team is annoying as ♥♥♥♥
- the shotgun bullet spread isn't consistent with every shot leading to some unfair situation
- there is little to no balance in the casual matchmaking
- the game is horrendous for begginers. There is basically a very minimal tutorial for just 4 classes in the game, where they teach you almost nothing. Then you go into a regular server, get killed 20 times(without knowing actually why) and probably never touch the game again. That's where TF2 is losing a lot of the player base.
- competitive is a bad joke, the only way to really play competitive is through UGC and ETF2L, both being quite elitist and non-enjoyable without a proper team
- hackers are still quite common
- weapon balance is a joke
- the levels you get in matchmaking games are useless, they don't give you any sense of progression, you just get an ugly badge that doesn't do anything at all. Having a high level doesn't queue you up with better players and the points you receive aren't skill based.
And the list can go on...
I know the TF2 team is dedicated and trying to do their very best at improving whatever remained from TF2, but I feel their effort is irrelevant, the age of TF2 is dead.
I really feel the next step in the evolution of this genre is Overwatch. And I know my review will get plenty of hate for saying that, but it's the raw truth.
I just can't recommend this game for new players. Go and play a game with a community that's thriving, with real youtube and twitch coverage, with a proper learning curve for begginers. TF2 did some of these things for a while (except the last part), but now it is slowly dying. Play Overwatch, play Paladins, play a MOBA, play a TCG, but I don't recommend you TF2.

Not too sure what to write here so heres a recipe for Pancakes instead
Ingredients:
1 1/2 cups all-purpose flour
3 tablespoons sugar
1 tablespoon baking powder
1/4 teaspoon salt
1/8 teaspoon freshly ground nutmeg
2 large eggs, at room temperature
1 1/4 cups milk, at room temperature
1/2 teaspoon pure vanilla extract
3 tablespoons unsalted butter, plus more as needed
Now to make it
1. In a large bowl, whisk together the flour, sugar, baking powder, salt, and nutmeg.
2. In another bowl, beat the eggs and then whisk in the milk and vanilla.
3. Melt the butter in a large cast iron skillet or griddle over medium heat.
4. Whisk the butter into the milk mixture. Add the wet ingredients to the flour mixture, and whisk until a thick batter is just formed
5. Keeping the skillet at medium heat, ladle about 1/4 cup of the batter onto the skillet, to make a pancake. Make 1 or 2 more pancakes, taking care to keep them evenly spaced apart. Cook, until bubbles break the surface of the pancakes, and the undersides are golden brown, about 2 minutes. Flip with a spatula and cook about 1 minute more on the second side. Serve immediately or transfer to a platter and cover loosely with foil to keep warm. Repeat with the remaining batter, adding more butter to the skillet as needed.
6. Procedure for adding fruit to pancakes: Once the bubbles break the surface of the pancakes, scatter the surface with sliced or diced fruit, or chocolate chips, nuts, etc. Flip with a spatula and cook for 1 minute more, being careful not to burn toppings.

I'll preface this by saying that most of my hours in this were before this became (or just when it just started being) the war-themed hat simulator.
The gameplay in this was just fantastic - balanced classes with completely different playstyles means you can play however you feel.  Personally, I tended to play Soldier.  Nothing beats rocket-jumping across the map, shooting down on your enemies as you fly, then landing behind their lines and destroying their defence.
That being said, all of the new weapons that have been released over the last few years have really made it a very different game to how it used to be.  Valve originally gave the characters very distinctive silhouettes so that you'd be able to easily identify what you were up against, but these days there are so many different weapons that you simply can't tell what the enemy will be using, and a lot of the weapons simply aren't as balanced as the originals.  All the new weapons, maps, and hats have added a significant amount of bloat to the game size as well - it was something like 4GB initially, and is now >20.

Ingredients:
1 1/2 cups all-purpose flour
3 tablespoons sugar
1 tablespoon baking powder
1/4 teaspoon salt
1/8 teaspoon freshly ground nutmeg
2 large eggs, at room temperature
1 1/4 cups milk, at room temperature
1/2 teaspoon pure vanilla extract
3 tablespoons unsalted butter, plus more as needed
Now to make it
1. In a large bowl, whisk together the flour, sugar, baking powder, salt, and nutmeg.
2. In another bowl, beat the eggs and then whisk in the milk and vanilla.
3. Melt the butter in a large cast iron skillet or griddle over medium heat.
4. Whisk the butter into the milk mixture. Add the wet ingredients to the flour mixture, and whisk until a thick batter is just formed
5. Keeping the skillet at medium heat, ladle about 1/4 cup of the batter onto the skillet, to make a pancake. Make 1 or 2 more pancakes, taking care to keep them evenly spaced apart. Cook, until bubbles break the surface of the pancakes, and the undersides are golden brown, about 2 minutes. Flip with a spatula and cook about 1 minute more on the second side. Serve immediately or transfer to a platter and cover loosely with foil to keep warm. Repeat with the remaining batter, adding more butter to the skillet as needed.
6. Procedure for adding fruit to pancakes: Once the bubbles break the surface of the pancakes, scatter the surface with sliced or diced fruit, or chocolate chips, nuts, etc. Flip with a spatula and cook for 1 minute more, being careful not to burn toppings.

Where do I even begin with this game. First off ive been playing this game for about 7 years now and every playthrough ive had of it was exellent. There is alot of variety when it comes to builds. There is the obvious Light/Dark or Grey option for the game but there is also Force user builds, Ranged builds, Pure combat focused guardian, etc. I find the combat to be enjoyable (In my opinion) since its tactical and you can really plan attacks and things of that sort. Take DA:0 for example. Its pretty much the same system. You can start with 3 beginning classes: Guardian (Combat focused), Sentinel (Better skill progression), and Consular (Force powers). You then later in the game get different set of prestige classes depending on your allignment. Now, lets get to the writing of the game. This game has one of the best stories I have ever seen. You'll see once you play it for yourself. The reason I prefer this game slightly over the first is just because I prefer the darker, philosophical, grey aspects of the atmosphere and story a bit better (Kotor 1 is also one of my favorite games). Anyways, this game presents the idea that Dark is not necessarily evil and Light isnt nessesary good and you really get to see the Flaws of both sides. For example, you play as the Jedi Exile, who was exiled from the Jedi order for rusing to war to protect innocents. The Jedi were lazy and waited to "evaluate the threat". The dialouge and voice acting in this game is absolutely fantastic (Especially Kreia). For this game, you dont even need to be a fan of Star Wars. A non Star Wars fan would look at this game and just play an RPG. However a Star Wars fan would look at this and play an amazing Star Wars RPG. The reason for this is because the game is set in an era wayyy before the Movies. One flaw however, would be the cut content presented this game. Obsidian (The developers) were rushed to release this game by lucasarts, resulting in them needing to cut out content for the game. Having over 400 hours on this game, i can tell you how life changing this game can be.
Here's my story of TF2 in a nutshell:
0-50 hours:"Oh boy, what a great game! I can't wait to headshot some spies and be credit to the entire team!" Is what i first said, and boy was i wrong. I just learned how to play a FPS, and i had no idea what i was doing.
50-100:"Woah, these guys have great hats! Hey! Maybe i can get their hats if i give them all my weapons and crates!" Little did i know that i was about to get kicked because of that. Another learning moment!
100-200:"Finally, i have premium...I can't wait for the hats to flood in!" They never came...leaving me wondering how everyone else got hats.
200-300:"Huh?
What's that? Let me check it out..." After finally not sucking at the game, i decided to check out a trading site, which introduced me to a HUGE economy, with rising and lowering prices, which was confusing at first.
300-400:"What's this? FPS configs? And custom huds? Lets see..." Yup, my laptop sucks, so FPS configs were a lifesaver for me. And with the FrankenHud installed i finally have a better grasp of everything on my screen.
400+:"Alright, if i sell my Botkiller Minigun for 7.66 Ref, i can buy that 5th key for 16 ref, and i'l wait for it to go 18 ref, so i can make profit...I also don't like this hat anymore, so i'l sell it for 2.33 ref..." That's right, i buy low, sell high for profit, and search trade sites for skins/hats i want.
Fun fact: I got this game because it's free.
To this day i've spend about 200 bucks on it.
Thanks GabeN, it really was worth the wait.

Team Fortress 2 is probably one of the better games I've played.
The mechanics and variety in TF2 make it stand out in its class. From a deranged Pyro and Soviet Heavy to a crazy German Medic and an Aussie Sniper with parent issues you are never short of something new to try out.
The controls are simple to get the hang of, however each of the nine classes have very different attributes and styles of play. You can rush into battle brandishing a sword and shield as Demoman or creep around the corner for a sneaky backstab as Spy.
The gamemodes themselves are also wide in variety. There's everything from pushing a bomb along a track in Payload, capturing the enemy's territory in Control Points or Attack/Defence and delivering the Australium to the rocket for Mann Co's very own Monkey Space Program.
The maps vary greatly in complexity as well as having something for all classes. In 2Fort, you can barge through the central bridge to return the stolen Intelligence to your base as Heavy or trudge through the the sewers as Spy (slightly less elegant, but it gets the job done).
The classes themselves are customiseable by unlocking new weapons and items for each class. These are randomised and can be equipped to alter your game completely. You can go from a modern day, grenade-chucking Demoman to a Medieval Scottish Swordsman with the click of a mouse. There is really no end to your options in this game.
This review only touches on what you can do in Team Fortress 2. I haven't even covered buying and selling items, Crafting, Trading or Co-Op defence against a horde of evil robots.

Where do I even begin with this game. First off ive been playing this game for about 7 years now and every playthrough ive had of it was exellent. There is alot of variety when it comes to builds. There is the obvious Light/Dark or Grey option for the game but there is also Force user builds, Ranged builds, Pure combat focused guardian, etc. I find the combat to be enjoyable (In my opinion) since its tactical and you can really plan attacks and things of that sort. Take DA:0 for example. Its pretty much the same system. You can start with 3 beginning classes: Guardian (Combat focused), Sentinel (Better skill progression), and Consular (Force powers). You then later in the game get different set of prestige classes depending on your allignment. Now, lets get to the writing of the game. This game has one of the best stories I have ever seen. You'll see once you play it for yourself. The reason I prefer this game slightly over the first is just because I prefer the darker, philosophical, grey aspects of the atmosphere and story a bit better (Kotor 1 is also one of my favorite games). Anyways, this game presents the idea that Dark is not necessarily evil and Light isnt nessesary good and you really get to see the Flaws of both sides. For example, you play as the Jedi Exile, who was exiled from the Jedi order for rusing to war to protect innocents. The Jedi were lazy and waited to "evaluate the threat". The dialouge and voice acting in this game is absolutely fantastic (Especially Kreia). For this game, you dont even need to be a fan of Star Wars. A non Star Wars fan would look at this game and just play an RPG. However a Star Wars fan would look at this and play an amazing Star Wars RPG. The reason for this is because the game is set in an era wayyy before the Movies. One flaw however, would be the cut content presented this game. Obsidian (The developers) were rushed to release this game by lucasarts, resulting in them needing to cut out content for the game. Luckily, a group of community modders managed to get into the games files and restore alot of the content that was cut. You can find the mod on the steam workshop. Anyways, hurry up and buy the game! You wont be dissapointed.

A game, simple, elegant yet sophisticated. Lots of support if you start running into troubles. The intergration of custom images, both animated and non-animated (AKA sprays) is a very good feature that Valve has intergrated into this game.
The limited use of weapons in multiplayer and Co-Op (AKA MvM) combat tests the players skills, with other people, forcing theirselves to improve their skills, or face defeat from the enemy.
At times, the lack of weapons and options is fustrating, like when one team is overpowered in their spawn by the opposing team, and the opposing team is spawn-camping.
The visuals are fine. When the computer lags, it returns to the players position sort-of gracefully, instead of the display jerking like other games.
For audio/music, I would of personally liked if the audio effects, such as the players shouting, or guns firing, could be turned off in the settings, so that one person could use the voice chat effectively.
Getting new weapons is quite easy using the Steam trading system. Just invite, drag the items to trade, ask for a specific item(/s) and click make trade. New weapons and cosmetics from the workshop is being added every year, to keep users enjoying the game.
Generally, a very good game for a gamer who wants to improve their skills, or  a 'noob' of FPS gaming to start with, before buying the 'big guns' of FPS gaming, like Call of Duty, Battlefield and Advanced Warfare.

A game, simple, elegant yet sophisticated. Lots of support if you start running into troubles. The intergration of custom images, both animated and non-animated (AKA sprays) is a very good feature that Valve has intergrated into this game.
The limited use of weapons in multiplayer and Co-Op (AKA MvM) combat tests the players skills, with other people, forcing theirselves to improve their skills, or face defeat from the enemy.
At times, the lack of weapons and options is fustrating, like when one team is overpowered in their spawn by the opposing team, and the opposing team is spawn-camping.
The visuals are fine. When the computer lags, it returns to the players position sort-of gracefully, instead of the display jerking like other games.
For audio/music, I would of personally liked if the audio effects, such as the players shouting, or guns firing, could be turned off in the settings, so that one person could use the voice chat effectively.
Getting new weapons is quite easy using the Steam trading system. Just invite, drag the items to trade, ask for a specific item(/s) and click make trade. New weapons and cosmetics from the workshop is being added every year, to keep users enjoying the game.
Generally, a very good game for a gamer who wants to improve their skills, or  a 'noob' of FPS gaming to start with, before buying the 'big guns' of FPS gaming, like Call of Duty, Battlefield and Advanced Warfare.

When I was younger, maybe around 13, I lived on a small farm in the middle of nowhere. I really like it there; my sister and I had a lot of space to run around and play. We also had horses, sometimes as many as nine. My sister loved them, but I did not, because I had to help feed them.
But I digress. I remember a lot of strange things that happened at and around that house. Perhaps the most terrifying was this one night when I was sleeping without my shirt on. Y'know, because that was a thug thing for a kid to do, apparently. Anyways, I was rather restless, spending a lot of time looking up into the darkness, toward my ceiling. I felt a very uncanny presence, though: a chill through my body, a lump in my stomach. I turned to look toward the other side of my room, and that's when I saw her. A woman, glowing, looking to be an adult, with blond hair and flatly colored clothes. I think her shirt was red, and her pants were blue. Oh, and she had no face. Like, at all.
It reminded me of a nightmare I had as a kid. My father had shown me a picture (which I assume was CG) back when I was around four years old of some old man without a face. He told me that's what happens to people who smoke cigarettes and pick their noses. Of course it terrified me as a kid. And of course, so did this apparition of sorts.
I quickly covered myself with my blankets in terror, my ears ringing. As I did, I felt a tingling numbness all across my back, and I couldn't help but picture her pouring spiders onto my body. That's how it felt.
When I eventually gathered the bravery to look back, she was gone. It was just an illusion. The tingling had just been from me being without a shirt. But needless to say, I wore a shirt to bed for years after.

Let me prep this review by saying one thing: I usually don't like multiplayer games. That is, until Team Fortress 2. Before this, the realm of my multiplayer experience lied solely on Smash Bros (and even then, I was the "Fox only final Destination no items" sort of guy). So what was it about Tf2 that changed my mind? Well, let's start with the obvious first; the aesthetics. It's a gorgeous game, with a 20th century cartoonish art style, and a personality Fallout hopes it can achieve. Every class is commically over-exaggerated, leading to a really pleasant experience for my eyes and ears. With that, let's talk about the core gameplay, shall we? The game is a team-based FPS, with a boat-load of modes, ranging from the familiar capture the flag to control points, to odder modes such as pushing the carts. The game has nine classes, each with their own strengths and weaknesses to contribute to the team. Every half hour of playing or so, you'll get a random item via a dropping system. Items are organized into primary, secondary, and melee, which is self-explanatory. What I like about the items is that they aren't clear upgrades, they have their own strengths and weaknesses. While their are a lot of modes, offline is limited to playing with bots, and it's boring, especially considering you're items are saved via cloud, so during offline you can't even use your items. That said, online is a great experience, especially with a team of nice players. A mode I've neglected to mention is man vs machine, which has a team of 6 players going against hundreds of bots, collecting money to buy upgrades along the way. While this mode costs a dollar to play, you can reap a good amount of rewards, ranging from robot parts, to the coveted australium weapons, which do nothing except look pretty. These items can be sold on the market, and the aforementioned australiums can charge upwards of 80 bucks! that aside, it's a living and breathing market a la W.O.W., and I think it's cool that real world concepts such as supply, demand, and inflation apply to the in-game market.
All in all, I give the game a 9 out of 10, a great time as long as you have friends to play with.

Team Fortress 2 is a fairly good game, very fun, definitely better than most generic shooters. I really only have three complaints. But dont get me wrong I do like the game.
1. No assault rifles. I mean really what kind of shooter doesnt have even 1 assault rifle. seriously WHAT THE HELL!
2. You cant aim down sights (with the exception of the sniper rifles). of course with most the combat being close to mid range and many of the weapons being shotguns and AoE weapons this can be overlooked.
3. Pay To Win. the guns they start you out with arent terrible, they arent great either. a few hours in I decided to buy two guns to see if I was a bad player and needed more practice; or if it was the default guns holding me back. It was. I purchased a new Sniper and a Revolver; immedietly I started doing better. My kills trippled at the very least.
now, with this being such a good game, I cant just give cons. so here are a few things I liked about TF2.
1. Well defined class roles. the classes are set up very well, to where as long as everyone does their part you will almost always suceed.
2. Fun maps. all the maps are well thought out with good positions for all the classes to do their jobs. (though I wish there were more places to snipe from.)
3. Tagging. for those of you who dont know tagging is placing a custom image (that you upload) on walls in the maps. Not enough games do this. And come on who wouldnt wanna do it, nothing like mocing your enemy by tagging the wall at the entrance of their base, or painting a pic of you favorite Animé/Game characters, or what ever.
anyway this game if pretty fun, definitely worth a try.

Let me prep this review by saying one thing: I usually don't like multiplayer games. That is, until Team Fortress 2. Before this, the realm of my multiplayer experience lied solely on Smash Bros (and even then, I was the "Fox only final Destination no items" sort of guy). So what was it about Tf2 that changed my mind? Well, let's start with the obvious first; the aesthetics. It's a gorgeous game, with a 20th century cartoonish art style, and a personality Fallout hopes it can achieve. Every class is commically over-exaggerated, leading to a really pleasant experience for my eyes and ears. With that, let's talk about the core gameplay, shall we? The game is a team-based FPS, with a boat-load of modes, ranging from the familiar capture the flag to control points, to odder modes such as pushing the carts. The game has nine classes, each with their own strengths and weaknesses to contribute to the team. Every half hour of playing or so, you'll get a random item via a dropping system. Items are organized into primary, secondary, and melee, which is self-explanatory. What I like about the items is that they aren't clear upgrades, they have their own strengths and weaknesses. While their are a lot of modes, offline is limited to playing with bots, and it's boring, especially considering you're items are saved via cloud, so during offline you can't even use your items. That said, online is a great experience, especially with a team of nice players. A mode I've neglected to mention is man vs machine, which has a team of 6 players going against hundreds of bots, collecting money to buy upgrades along the way. While this mode costs a dollar to play, you can reap a good amount of rewards, ranging from robot parts, to the coveted australium weapons, which do nothing except look pretty. These items can be sold on the market, and the aforementioned australiums can charge upwards of 80 bucks! that aside, it's a living and breathing market a la W.O.W., and I think it's cool that real world concepts such as supply, demand, and inflation apply to the in-game market.
All in all, I give the game a 9 out of 10, a great time as long as you have friends to play with.

Team Fortress 2 is a fairly good game, very fun, definitely better than most generic shooters. I really only have three complaints. But dont get me wrong I do like the game.
1. No assault rifles. I mean really what kind of shooter doesnt have even 1 assault rifle. seriously WHAT THE HELL!
2. You cant aim down sights (with the exception of the sniper rifles). of course with most the combat being close to mid range and many of the weapons being shotguns and AoE weapons this can be overlooked.
3. Pay To Win. the guns they start you out with arent terrible, they arent great either. a few hours in I decided to buy two guns to see if I was a bad player and needed more practice; or if it was the default guns holding me back. It was. I purchased a new Sniper and a Revolver; immedietly I started doing better. My kills trippled at the very least.
now, with this being such a good game, I cant just give cons. so here are a few things I liked about TF2.
1. Well defined class roles. the classes are set up very well, to where as long as everyone does their part you will almost always suceed.
2. Fun maps. all the maps are well thought out with good positions for all the classes to do their jobs. (though I wish there were more places to snipe from.)
3. Tagging. for those of you who dont know tagging is placing a custom image (that you upload) on walls in the maps. Not enough games do this. And come on who wouldnt wanna do it, nothing like mocing your enemy by tagging the wall at the entrance of their base, or painting a pic of you favorite Animé/Game characters, or what ever.
anyway this game if pretty fun, definitely worth a try.

Team Fortress 2 is a fairly good game, very fun, definitely better than most generic shooters. I really only have three complaints. But dont get me wrong I do like the game.
1. No assault rifles. I mean really what kind of shooter doesnt have even 1 assault rifle. seriously WHAT THE HELL!
2. You cant aim down sights (with the exception of the sniper rifles). of course with most the combat being close to mid range and many of the weapons being shotguns and AoE weapons this can be overlooked.
3. Pay To Win. the guns they start you out with arent terrible, they arent great either. a few hours in I decided to buy two guns to see if I was a bad player and needed more practice; or if it was the default guns holding me back. It was. I purchased a new Sniper and a Revolver; immedietly I started doing better. My kills trippled at the very least.
now, with this being such a good game, I cant just give cons. so here are a few things I liked about TF2.
1. Well defined class roles. the classes are set up very well, to where as long as everyone does their part you will almost always suceed.
2. Fun maps. all the maps are well thought out with good positions for all the classes to do their jobs. (though I wish there were more places to snipe from.)
3. Tagging. for those of you who dont know tagging is placing a custom image (that you upload) on walls in the maps. Not enough games do this. And come on who wouldnt wanna do it, nothing like mocing your enemy by tagging the wall at the entrance of their base, or painting a pic of you favorite Animé/Game characters, or what ever.
anyway this game if pretty fun, definitely worth a try.

"Team Fortress 2" Every time i hear this i get happy. Team Fortress 2 is a outstanding PC first person shoot with insane combat action. Choosing from 9 classes (How i say the classes are not in order like in the game) Scout, Sniper, Soldier, Heavy, Pyro, Spy, Engineer, Demoman, and Medic, you can have so much fun. You can get gear, weapons, and most importantly, hats for the classes. You can also get paint and dye your gear, hats, but sadly not weapons. Crafting is something also in Team Fortress 2, and no not like Minecraft, exactly. You get metal and other things to craft weapons and sometimes if you want to craft a weapon you need a other weapon that you collected while playing to create the weapon you desire. But if you have a hard time finding the weapon or crafting items, theres something called "The Mann-Co Store" Here you can buy almost ALL of the items in Team Fortress 2 with real life money. You can buy extremely expensive packs for a couple grand but sometimes theres sales to get items for less charge. But if your not sure if that weapon is great, you can test it for a week and while you testing the item you can buy it 20% off. Graphics are okay for a 2007 release. Theres graphic settings if the game lags at all so you can decrease the graphic quality. Theres a couple modes like Payload, King of the Hill, Etc You select from 2 teams, Red or Blu. And theres a mode where Red and Blu team up in "Mann vs Machine" this is a mode where you fight robot versions of classes to unlock new items and more. Story: how this all started is when 2 brothers created there own company. But there father left them some money before his death. But the 2 brothers fought over it and they both hired 9 mercenarys to fight each other. The fight was happening ever then. Mann vs Machine Story: Some how there was a 3rd brother who was lost and created a company and became extremely rich. He heard about his 2 brothers and there war. The lost brother created robots that run on money and sent them out to kill his brothers and the mercenarys they hired. The 2 brothers teamed up and made the mercenarys team up to kill the robots. I give this whole game 1000/10. This game puts the popular franchise "Call of Duty" in the dust.
