This game did not age well. I am an extremely biased reviewer for this purpose, owing to my large hour count (even larger than shown because of alts), years of seeing different stages of development and stagnation and plain embitterment.
Disclaimer : This does not apply to everyone but if you consider yourself good at fps games you most likely aren't interested in this game anyway.
I got into TF2 through a friend i played cs:s pugs with at a really low level and it seemed like a pretty fun game, so i had minimal fps game experience.
PROS:
-Huge mechanical depth to multiple classes, including the breadth of aiming capabilities
-Has a very good movement system, a lot of depth in itself
-Basic gameplay still is fun 10 years later
-""""can"""" be run with lower tier hardware with extensive graphic changes
-Can be fun at a very casual level.
CONS:
-Hands down the single WORST community of an fps game I have ever played
-Yes I know counter strike is full of toxic open players but the TF2 community is far worse
-Valve encourages the personality cult of popular players by adding "taunts" that encourage you to stop playing the game and not shoot people
-The votekicking system is used, the majority of the time, to kick players doing too well, or who are killing "friendlies", the aforementioned taunting players.
-Pro but also a con, a massive amount of player made maps. Sure some of them are funny a couple times but the vast majority are poorly made (because hammer is bad) and unfun to play.
-A massive amount of pointless cosmetics that take up 18 GB of my harddrive and eat my fps unless I use a third-party mod to disable them
-A ridicuously bad dev team
-In my opinion this is one of the worst issues with the game
-Most updates add trivial status effects or useless mechanics that seem to add more complexities for no reason.
-For a multimillion dollar company valve only has about 4 programmers for this game and sometimes they don't actually change gameplay whatsoever in more than a year.
-Balance is horribly skewed based on whatever awful idea a dev came up with before crunch time
If you want to play this game, play it casually and with as much brevity as possible. If you are good at fps games, be prepared to be hated and kicked from many servers for "cheating".

The tomato is the edible, often red fruit/berry of the nightshade Solanum lycopersicum,[1][2] commonly known as a tomato plant. The species originated in the South American Andes[2] and its use as a food originated in Mexico, and spread throughout the world following the Spanish colonization of the Americas. Its many varieties are now widely grown, sometimes in greenhouses in cooler climates.
The tomato is consumed in diverse ways, including raw, as an ingredient in many dishes, sauces, salads, and drinks. While it is botanically a fruit, it is considered a vegetable for culinary purposes (as well as under U.S. customs regulations, see Nix v. Hedden), which has caused some confusion. The fruit is rich in lycopene, which may have beneficial health effects.
The tomato belongs to the nightshade family, Solanaceae.[1][3] The plants typically grow to 1–3 meters (3–10 ft) in height and have a weak stem that often sprawls over the ground and vines over other plants. It is a perennial in its native habitat, although often grown outdoors in temperate climates as an annual. An average common tomato weighs approximately 100 grams (4 oz).[4][5]Etymology
The word "tomato" comes from the Spanish tomate, which in turn comes from the Nahuatl word tomatotl /aːˈtomatl͡ɬ/.[6] It first appeared in print in 1595. A member of the deadly nightshade family, tomatoes were erroneously thought to be poisonous (although the leaves are) by Europeans who were suspicious of their bright, shiny fruit. Native versions were small, like cherry tomatoes, and most likely yellow rather than red. The tomato is native to western South America and Central America.[6]
Mesoamerica
Aztecs and other peoples in Mesoamerica used the fruit in their cooking. The exact date of domestication is unknown: by 500 BC, it was already being cultivated in southern Mexico and probably other areas.[7]:13 The Pueblo people are thought to have believed that those who witnessed the ingestion of tomato seeds were blessed with powers of divination.[8] The large, lumpy variety of tomato, a mutation from a smoother, smaller fruit, originated in Mesoamerica, and may be the direct ancestor of some modern cultivated tomatoes.[7]
Spanish distribution
Spanish conquistador Hernán Cortés may have been the first to transfer the small yellow tomato to Europe after he captured the Aztec city of Tenochtitlan, now Mexico City, in 1521, although Christopher Columbus, a Genoese working for the Spanish monarchy, may have taken them back as early as 1493. The earliest discussion of the tomato in European literature appeared in an herbal written in 1544 by Pietro Andrea Mattioli, an Italian physician and botanist, who suggested that a new type of eggplant had been brought to Italy that was blood red or golden color when mature and could be divided into segments and eaten like an eggplant—that is, cooked and seasoned with salt, black pepper, and oil. However it wasn't until ten years later that tomatoes were named in print by Mattioli as pomi d’oro, or "golden apple".[7]:13
After the Spanish colonization of the Americas, the Spanish distributed the tomato throughout their colonies in the Caribbean. They also took it to the Philippines, from where it spread to southeast Asia and then the entire Asian continent. The Spanish also brought the tomato to Europe. It grew easily in Mediterranean climates, and cultivation began in the 1540s. It was probably eaten shortly after it was introduced, and was certainly being used as food by the early 17th century in Spain. The earliest discovered cookbook with tomato recipes was published in Naples in 1692, though the author had apparently obtained these recipes from Spanish sources.[7]:17 In certain areas of Italy, such as Florence, however, the fruit was used solely as a tabletop decoration before it was incorporated into the local cuisine in the late 17th or early 18th century.

Team Fortress 2 is very solid, fun fps (first person shooter) game. Unlike a modern fps game, TF2 has 9 unique classes: Scout, Soldier, Pryo, Demoman, Heavy, Engineer, Medic, Sniper and Spy. All the classes play very differently to each other, meaning that there's a class for everyone; want to go in guns blazing? Chose scout, want to stay back but still get kills? Chose sniper. All the classes are well balanced with none being much better than ay others but, with some cases like sniper or spy, you have to be could with some classes to get anywhere with them. Weapons wise they're all good, each class starts out with a default primary, secondary and melee weapon but you can find weapons via the game's item drop system or by them in the store or, if that wasn't enough, you can craft them or borrow them for a time. I myself rarely use crafting, only do so if you really want some items and have loads of scrap items that you want to get rid of. There are 8 game modes: Payload. King of the Hill, Attack/Defend, Paylaod Race, Control Points, Capture the Flag, Special Delivery and Random. I love payload, mainly because matches get frantic in the late stages, it's so fun to be attacking and at the last minute, get an uber and push and win. I also feel I should touch on the competitive side of TF2. The game hasn't got match making (as of now) but there are websites for those who want to play. The best I know is TF2 Centre, if you have only a background of public servers and matches, it's a good place to start. The main modes are: 6's, 4v4 and Highlander. 6's has 6 players to a team and play on Koth and CP maps, the normal set up is 2 scouts, 2 soldiers, 1 demoman and a medic. There are a lot of items that are banned in 6's, and it's seen as more of a serious side of competitive TF2 as well. 4v4 is very similar to 6's, only with, normally, only 1 scout and 1 soldier. Now to Highlander. In Highlander there can be only one of each class, and it's a 9v9 game. In addition to Koth and CP maps, Highlander plays Playoad maps as well. Highlander has less weapon restrictions too, and can be good for those newer players. Overall, TF2 is an amazing game and you must, I repeat- MUST have this game installed on your computer. It is free to play now too, but F2P's won't be able to craft, to become premium- just by an item from the Mann Co. store. From then on, only get items from the Mann Co. store if you're wanting hats. I recommend you use the community market for anything else, as those items will often be strange, vintage or killstreaked. TF2 is a wonderful experience that has lasted 8 years of updates, and is still going strong. Of all the FPS's I've played, this game has enjoyed me the most. And a last tip, if you're just starting out- don't worry if you're not to good, you'll learn. Find you favourite class, and make sure it isn't sniper! Seriously, all beginners go sniper, if you're starting- play soldier. A well balanced class. Now go out there, and MOVE THAT GEAR UP! (BEST ENGIE LINE EVER!)

The species originated in the South American Andes[2] and its use as a food originated in Mexico, and spread throughout the world following the Spanish colonization of the Americas. Its many varieties are now widely grown, sometimes in greenhouses in cooler climates.
The tomato is consumed in diverse ways, including raw, as an ingredient in many dishes, sauces, salads, and drinks. While it is botanically a fruit, it is considered a vegetable for culinary purposes (as well as under U.S. customs regulations, see Nix v. Hedden), which has caused some confusion. The fruit is rich in lycopene, which may have beneficial health effects.
The tomato belongs to the nightshade family, Solanaceae.[1][3] The plants typically grow to 1–3 meters (3–10 ft) in height and have a weak stem that often sprawls over the ground and vines over other plants. It is a perennial in its native habitat, although often grown outdoors in temperate climates as an annual. An average common tomato weighs approximately 100 grams (4 oz).[4][5]Etymology
The word "tomato" comes from the Spanish tomate, which in turn comes from the Nahuatl word tomatotl /aːˈtomatl͡ɬ/.[6] It first appeared in print in 1595. A member of the deadly nightshade family, tomatoes were erroneously thought to be poisonous (although the leaves are) by Europeans who were suspicious of their bright, shiny fruit. Native versions were small, like cherry tomatoes, and most likely yellow rather than red. The tomato is native to western South America and Central America.[6]
Mesoamerica
Aztecs and other peoples in Mesoamerica used the fruit in their cooking. The exact date of domestication is unknown: by 500 BC, it was already being cultivated in southern Mexico and probably other areas.[7]:13 The Pueblo people are thought to have believed that those who witnessed the ingestion of tomato seeds were blessed with powers of divination.[8] The large, lumpy variety of tomato, a mutation from a smoother, smaller fruit, originated in Mesoamerica, and may be the direct ancestor of some modern cultivated tomatoes.[7]
Spanish distribution
Spanish conquistador Hernán Cortés may have been the first to transfer the small yellow tomato to Europe after he captured the Aztec city of Tenochtitlan, now Mexico City, in 1521, although Christopher Columbus, a Genoese working for the Spanish monarchy, may have taken them back as early as 1493. The earliest discussion of the tomato in European literature appeared in an herbal written in 1544 by Pietro Andrea Mattioli, an Italian physician and botanist, who suggested that a new type of eggplant had been brought to Italy that was blood red or golden color when mature and could be divided into segments and eaten like an eggplant—that is, cooked and seasoned with salt, black pepper, and oil. However it wasn't until ten years later that tomatoes were named in print by Mattioli as pomi d’oro, or "golden apple".[7]:13
After the Spanish colonization of the Americas, the Spanish distributed the tomato throughout their colonies in the Caribbean. They also took it to the Philippines, from where it spread to southeast Asia and then the entire Asian continent. The Spanish also brought the tomato to Europe. It grew easily in Mediterranean climates, and cultivation began in the 1540s. It was probably eaten shortly after it was introduced, and was certainly being used as food by the early 17th century in Spain. The earliest discovered cookbook with tomato recipes was published in Naples in 1692, though the author had apparently obtained these recipes from Spanish sources.[7]:17 In certain areas of Italy, such as Florence, however, the fruit was used solely as a tabletop decoration before it was incorporated into the local cuisine in the late 17th or early 18th century.

Since the Meet your Match update has come about, and with PASS time and Competitive out of beta, Here I am, re-writing this. Team Fortress 2 (TF2) is my most played game. I have played it for hours and hours (OVER 5000000000000000000) and I still find myself going back to it.

Recently I bought Overwatch, and I very hyped for it. When I bought it, it was super laggy (as I expected) with 5-15 FPS, which my insanity calls playable. Even though I have this epic new game, im still playing TF2. Why? Because I love it. Team fortress 2 is by far the most enjoyable game I have played. I've been playing Team fortress 2 (TF2) since July 27, 2014. over 2 years now. I have a reputation for not only playing tf2 all the time, but I like to think im pretty good at it as well. As I said, I love TF2. Why? I love TF2 because the game manages to stay fresh. With different maps, weapons, loadouts, cosmetics, and friends to play with, it rarely ever gets boring. The community are the ones who love this game, and they are the ones who keep it going. Without a fan base as huge as TF2's, this game may have crumbled to dust years ago. Luckily, it hasn't. It still has it's annual updates with some more here and there, theres always something new just as you decide "I'll stop for now" unless you plain dislike the game, there really isn't any reason to stop playing. The new casual mode and competitive modes, I find absolutely amazing. wait times aside, the actual gameplay mechanics of these casual and competitive modes are just like the old valve servers, with some minor changes that dont effect the gameplay at all, if not for the better. most of the issues lie within the organization of them such as wait times and other issues that were fixed. If you dont like the official gameplay then maybe you will like the community servers. There are dedicated servers to the old pubbing experience, such as 24/7 servers. The othes include but are not limited to: cp_orange, 100% crits, randomizer, x10, and new weapons. One of my favorite things in tf2 is you can turn a profit, completely free. its easier if you spend just about 49 cents or so on a sticky jumper, or anything to get premium, so you can trade easier. its a complete arbitrage of trading. You can always make the most of trading in this game for absolutely free, or under a dollar to be more convenient.
Tf2 is my favorite game -obviously, because theres no reason not to. Its free, and even if it wants you to buy something, you can spend under a dollar. (just dont start out buying cheap weapons for like 3$ like I did) I really recommend you to try it, it cant hurt since it's free. If your new to TF2, you wont regret playing it, and have fun on your new experience!

Greetings, Meatbags.
I have 154 hours logged. I spent 99 cents on a key. I got a hat.
As most of you know, this is the kind of game that has no story, and gameplay is the key element.
However, this is not a game. This is mindless shooting, and hoping that you hit something... not that I was terrible at this game, but I spent waaay more time playing than was necessary to write this review.
+ Gameplay mechanics are great, balancing was pretty good.
+ F2P, but the desire for different guns keep you playing
+ Not pay to win. The weapons, both found and purchased are very well balanced
+ Co-op mode is fun, and challenging
+ Holiday themed maps and events
+ Crafting is available but...
+/- Very Addicting. Can be good for some, but will consume your time like there is no tomorrow.
- The economy in the game and steam market place - $10 and up for "collector's edition" weapons (which happen to have the same stats as the random finds)
- Hats. So. Many. Hats. (great for customization, but entirely pointless)
- No gratification outside of victory. There is no sense of fulfillment after playing a couple of matches.
- Completing co-op mode on harder difficulties just gives you robot heads to slap on to your weapons. (just more customization, showing others how large your brass balls/ovaries are)
- Any customization options you unlock during the aforementioned holiday events can not be used after the event ends. Meaning it just takes up space in your inventory -unused- until next year
- Crafting is random. If you want a specific weapon to complete a set, you might end up making a replica of something you already have, just making the game more tedious if you wanted to 100% sets... Unless you buy it of course.
I was especially annoyed by the Steam workshop for this game. Lots of the items were amazing and belonged in this game, but steam refused to add many of the items. Of course, this is only my opinion, and Steam can make up their own mind on what belongs to a game that they created.
I can't truly rate the game, as it does have some really great gameplay elements, but I found the whole game meaningless and unsatisfying... outside of it being a caricature of sensless violence of course.
****
Don't waste your life playing this. I mean, come on, Steam produced a comic portraying the TF2 team to give the game some sense of a story. I personally never read it, but how much more sensless violence do you need? Just watch the news.

There are 9 classes in the game, and each one completes another one (although the classic pyro you will encounter is W+M1). I'll show the pros and cons of the classes next. 1. Scout. The pistol works nice with pyros and generally it's a really cool gun. The bat is not something i use cause i just forget about it. Same thing with the Sandman. As a scout you always have to think ahead and know the layouts of every map cause you're an ambush class not an assault one. 2. Soldier. A patriotic american that fights for Liberty and also one of the easiest classes in the game. Your rocket launcher does amazing damage at close range, and not from afar (I saw soldiers doing that) Aim for the ground when you aim a target it will do the same damage. That's all about it, you don't need the rest too much (the shotgun is simply a reskin of the scattergun).3. Pyro. Unknown identity and nationality.  One of the classes i hate because how can you rezist raging when you see that he killed you and a second later he's blown up? Anyway the flamethrower is cool but dont just press W and mouse 1, there's so much more about this class. a tactic i reccomend is flame your target and pull out your flare gun and get a crit on him ( airblasting is optional) and then just fall back and let the fire do the rest. 4. Demoman. This guy is from Scotland and you can just get your bottle of scotch and not go driving (not safe) and go in combat (more safe). One of the most versatile classes of the game. The grenade launcher is for self defence and assaulting and the sticky bomb launcher for defence (although some demomen use that only with great effects i can't do that) that's pretty much all about it. a direct hit with the grenade launcher does 100+ dmg no matter the range so.. or you can go demoknighting and chop some heads (the best sword is the Persian Persuader but dont use it for classic demo) and get yourself a shield charge to your enemies with mouse 2 (also for falling back) and get the crit swing on them.5. He is from Russia and has a very russian accent. The heavy is the slowest class of the game but once you get the hang of the minigun (that does 50 dmg at close range lol) it becomes a fun class to play with (paired with a medic I got 63 kills in one life and it ended because the round was over also back then my name was Trololol best name ever for that situation :).6. Have you watched the good ol' westerns? Well it makes no difference cause this cowboy is very far from that. Engineer. With his classic loadout he's just for defence or putting up a teleporter somewhere hidden and protecting it with a sentry gun (that rips the shreds out of your dying enemies at lv 3) Other than that (unless you're a combat engineer) the dispenser will only be used by yourself while you are bored waiting for enemies at the flag (intelligence). now the combat engineer is an engineer that gave away the big sentry for a mini sentry and a life of action and fun  (yeeehaaaaa). The mini sentry fires faster than a lv 1 sentry and although it has less health it's harder to hit. Phiu, almost done. 7. Medic! this guy is from Germany, Stuttgard. the class that nobody plays with its also the class that it's the most round-changing because that uber can change everything if timed correctly. I really don't play as a medic so i cant give tips on How to...(don't play as a combat medic because you will look like an idiot and you'll die almost instantly). 8. Ahh the sniper. This australian bushman has a big mouth and an amazing laughter im sorry he laughs so rare(huhuhuhuhhuhuhuhuhuhuh...). one of the best classes in the game for me. Its easier to get headshots without any effort than desperately going for the back as a spy (talking about newbie spies) Also, the SMG IS THE WORST GUN IN THE GAME, I SEE TO MANY NOOB SNIPERS THAT GO ASSAULT AND DISGRACE THEIR PURPOSE (i was on spectator, and i saw a sniper in the enemy base with an SMG, he battle cried (nobody around him), a soldier came down the stairs, the sniper said : HELP! he didn't even shoot the SMG as he was falling back looking like an idiot while the soldier blew him up. PRO tip: Just aim for the head while scoped and you'll get a couple of headshots.9. SPY round' here! SPY! Hey boys there's a SPY! The spy is the hardest class to master in the game and watching youtube videos and seeing OMG! look! it's so easy! No it's not. Most of them were playing with very unexperienced players and I'm not saying that they don't have skill, they do, but they luckily picked a nice server to show that spectacularly. So if you don't want to be like: "Spois, bloody useless"(Sniper) in the minds of everyone keep in mind:  Your revolver is meant to be used in case of emergency and last resort not as your primary. Your knife. Use it wisely and dont go desperately stabbing a guy in the front. Use your cloak for infiltrating and escaping (prefferably after a corner cause you will be visible for one more second after you take your watch out. Your disguise kit. Despite general thinking, the effect of the disguise does not break your cloak (it won't be visible unless you diguise before you get hit with the Dead ringer)

TF2 is a 10(?) year old game, and personally, I've enjoyed it for the couple years I've played it, but recently, many problems have been plaguing it.
Main problems:
1) Hard to get into. There's quite a bit of veterans that still play this game, so, at first, you would have to learn to tolerate to die (a skill some higher-level players lack).
2) Performance. Over the years, the now-outdated Source engine has been modified heavily as to allow many elements. However, there are elements that Source just can't handle, leading to a lot of performance issues. Even with a good computer, you'll experience a few hiccups.
3) Community. TF2 is hard to explain community-wise. Rude players are constantly thrown in with kind players, and it just seems like a huge moshpit of immaturity, terrible memes, and all-around cancer.
Verdict: The game can be quite fun when experienced, although beginners beware: this game can be quite punishing at times.

TF2 used to be a great game. I clocked over a thousand hours on it.
With the matchmaking update, it often:
- Takes 5-30 minutes to play a map of your choice despite an ample amount of "compatible players" searching for it. I wrote this entire review while waiting for a game to start with 34 compatible players in my country, which according to the map selection screen, was green, meaning many players were available to play with.
- Matches you against teams with less players than yours, making it no challenge at all, or impossible if you're on the other side of that equation. This is because they removed autobalance, which wasn't the best system, but at least worked "well enough".
- Makes it very difficult to play with and/or invite friends to your game. In order to invite and play with a friend, neither of you can actively be in a game. Invites don't pop up like messages do, so you can easily miss such an invite, because it won't show up in a game. If you're in a game and invited to another game, tough luck for you. No more hopping into your friend's game partway through, even if there are 4 more players on red than blue.
It also makes it impossible to play against a friend (on opposite teams). No more grudge matches with your peers. The update destroyed the world of "community servers" that made TF2 so casual and fun. We're 6 months into this update, and subsequent updates, and it's still broken.
They could've left TF2 as it was for years. It was an excellent game for years and years. New games with better graphics and features came out, but TF2 survived with a healthy community of players. Valve ignored a huge user outcry against the update, and unfortunately TF2 will be one of those games we "used to play" and "used to be so much fun". We could have just gotten some more useless crates, hats, or weapons, but instead they broke it. They could have left it exactly as it was, and people would have kept buying $2 crate keys, spending thousands of dollars on hats, and donating to community servers, but instead they tried to make it "better" to compete with Overwatch. It's awful. Now I only login occasionally, at the insistence of my steam friends. What a shame,
RIP TF2 2016.

All the way from 2007 and still going strong. When I say ''going strong'' I usually like to think so in the community workshop and hat section. But on a serious note, this game is absolutely sensational and what's the best of it now? Well, it's totally free and definitely deserves the quote ''the most fun you can have online.'' - PC Gamer.
The game has a wide and diverse selection of 9 different classes, ranging from their own unique abilities and strategies that can be performed against each class, kind of like a ''rock, paper, scissors'' thing. The fast Boston talking and even more fast running Scout, to the towering, minigun-wielding hulk of a Russian man, Known as Heavy. Though every character class usually represents a soldier in a common FPS' of some sort, what I love about this is the fact that Valve has openly breathed life, vibrant personalities, characteristics and nationalities into this rag-tag bunch. I also enjoyed the customization of weapons and accessories, named after the witty puns, possibly the slight descrimination and referenced culture of that said character. Really brings out the comedic flare of the game and shows that humour can mix amusement in with entertainment.
Another great thing to note in this game is the fact that it's holiday themed. Either new campaigns modeled after a specific holiday, down to the newly cashed in, fan made hats are launched to the public to bring in funds for both Valve and the original creator at hand. Halloween, Christmas, Easter just to name a few are a great example and addition to the game's growing campaign and community.
I definitely recommend this game. Not just down to the fact that it's free, but because it still remains fun to this day and constant updates on campaigns and official hat accessories keep this game alive, making the game overall timeless.

Is this where I insert the hat simulator joke?
As someone with a little over 1,000 hours in TF2 (around 860 on this account at time of review and more on an alt I've completely forgotten about), I can safely say I have a pretty good idea of how the game plays.
Let's start with the negative stuff, though. Yes, there's negative stuff. For one thing, the most obvious downside is the community. It's... all right, all things considering. Better than some other FPS communities, but that doesn't necessarily mean it's any good. As a matter of fact, that doesn't even mean it's remotely CLOSE to being any good. It's better to have friends that play in the first place than it is to hop on and try to make friends, since you'll more than likely be called a noob/hacker/some other slur upon stepping foot into a populated server. This isn't to say it's impossible, but just... not likely.
As for other downsides, it's pretty obvious that, despite all the hat simulator jokes, yes, there ARE hats in the game. They look good, but they're EXPENSIVE if you decide to buy them with money, impossible to get unless you give them money in the first place, and you're generally considered a noob if you don't wear them (Some people even automatically assume I suck because I don't generally wear hats). Also, the economy is ridiculous. Not bad, but ridiculous. Starting from the ground up is getting more and more impossible as people keep relying on sites such as backpack.tf for pricing their precious items, and not so much on item function, or simply what they enjoy; if they aren't making a profit, you're probably not getting it. I suppose that's how all economies work though, which is why I don't call it 'bad,' just bad to get in to.
But honestly, I... I don't know what other negative things to say about this game. I could always complain about the Gunslinger or something equally stupid, but I won't. Let's move on to the positive stuff instead.
Let's just start with the most obvious thing: the customization is awesome in this game. In fact, it's beyond awesome. With 9 classes to play, each with a number of unique weapon options, you can play almost any role with any class. Want a more supportive Scout, rather than an offensive one? Just get yourself a Shortstop, Mad Milk, and a Candy Cane, and keep feeding your team that health. Want a defensive Pyro? An airblast capable Flamethrower, Scorch Shot, and Third Degree might be right up your alley. With so many options, you could experiment for HOURS straight and still have things you haven't tried. And to get even further into it, if you find a weapon set you like, the customization doesn't end there: HATS, HATS, HATS. Just trick out your look if that's what you want! A number of taunts keeps things going even further than they've already gone.
Now, the diversity, which I'm keeping in a whole other category from customization, just because there's so much more to cover. If you're just going to talk about what Valve gives you, straight out of the box, you'll STILL have plenty to choose from. Payload, King of the Hill, Control Points, Capture the Flag, Arena... get bored with one thing, go straight to the next. But that's not even scratching the SURFACE. Team Fortress 2 is, by definition, a community driven game. Even though Valve releases regular updates to the game, the community puts in so much more than they have already. Jump maps, VS Saxton Hale, just plain trade servers where you can goof around... there's so much stuff, I'd probably kill myself just trying to list it all. Just play, just... just explore. Do it. Do it for me.
But ultimately, what else is there to say about the game? Addicting, I guess? It's incredible fun, and it's never hard to find something to do when you start it up. Each character is lovable, the game is constantly getting new content added (though admittedly, mostly hats), and everything's just great. Not to mention, a TF2 Youtube channel and online comic only add to the experience. If you haven't tried this game yet, TRY IT (I mean seriously, it's free. Even if you don't like it, what'd you lose?).

This game used to be fun. Team Fortress 2 used to have the friendliest community, where people would help eachother learn how to rocket jump and give an Engineer tips on Sentry placement. Now its got hordes of lime green and pink Scouts running in, killing everything that moves, and putting "git gud scrub" in chat with a keybind.
This game used to be fun. For some it may still be fun to play, for others its a way to pass the time, and some people only still play because it has become routine to do so. And for many the in-game economy has actually become a job, a business, even if they don't work for Valve or any other software developer. If Valve were to remove metal and cosmetics entirely, many people would lose hundreds or thousands of dollars. This isn't even a game anymore.
People who play TF2 say that many aspects of this game need fixing. "Why would you nerf the Heavy and not the Demman?" I would say that the whole thing needs fixing. Specifically the community.
This game used to be fun. The community used to be fun to be a part of. A few months ago it has become just as bad as the Call of Duty fanbase and community.
You may still find it fun to play this game. You may somehow find the patience to deal with another toxic community. My patience is shot, I can deal with no more.
If any of you need me, I'll be playing a single player game. I can actually play those without being told "git gud, noob" or "get rekt, scrub" after every death. The NPCs of a Singleplayer game like Fallout or Metro are certainly friendlier than the real people who play Team Fortress 2.

Well, hello there. If you're reading this you're probably wondering if you should download this game or not. So, here's my personal opinion on the game after 1600 hourst that I've spent in it.
The game itself is cartoonish, but yet beautiful. The community is huge and amazing to this day! Of course the game has lost most of its biggest YouTubers, but it's not the game, it's how Valve does things.
Valve has a policy for their employees to work on whatever project they want, making the updating of this game long, but yet exciting.
This game is a 9 class Team based shooter with many unique weapons and cosmetic items that can make the game more fun! The game runs smoothly and is guarantted fun for your friends and most importantly, YOU!
The game has 5 main game modes: Payload, Attack/Defense, Control Points, King of the Hill and Capture Flag.
The 9 classes that I mentioned before are: Scout, Soldier, Pyro, Demoman, Heavy, Engineer, Sniper, Medic and the Spy. Every class comes with its own play style, which makes the game hard to master. At times spending hundred or even more hours into one class, just to master that class! Personally the Spy is my favorite class, even if the Inferno Update made Spy a lot harder. However, I love the challenge.
The game also has a story, which is told in comics at TF2's offcial Website, and SFM's, which can be found at TF2's Website or YouTube page. The story is actually good, every time we get a continuation of the story, it's worth it!
Well, this wraps up my review of the game. I hope you found this review helpful! Cya in the next review!

TF2 was the first game I really got into. It was relaxed and casual, the large teams and casual atmosphere gave me plenty of room to learn the ropes without being a burden. I spent hundreds of hours building defense grids, learning basic rocket jumps, and watching the world burn.
For a while I got bored of TF2, and went to play other games. When the matchmaking update came out I didn't believe the doomsyers, those who would declare TF2 to be 'dead'. Recently, I came back to TF2 to see just how much things had changed.
It turns out the doomsayers were right. The TF2 I fell in love with is dead and gone. When the matchmaking system came around and 'replaced' valve servers, a large portion of the playerbase dropped out. In my rusty state I simply can't find any good matchups. Half the time I get placed with players who are so far beneath me It's not even a competition, and the rest of the time It's me who's going under the steamroller. There's no push and pull anymore, and no room for failure.
TF2 isn't a bad game, and never has been, but it's not for people like me any more, and certainly no good for new players. I recommend finding something newer to sink your time into.

I have been play for a extremely long time and I have to say, you should get this game.
If you are reading this and have never played here are some tips for starting people.
-Spend around $5 on Backpack Expansions, trust me you will need it.
-Start with the class you think would be fun, I would recommend Soldier or Heavy and avoid Spy and Pyro until a few hours of learning the game.
-The "training" is bull jump onto CP Turbine, PL Upward, PLR Hightower, or CP Two Fort to learn what this game is.
-Never trash Achievement items like the L4D2 hat... I wish I never did....
-Keep the Frying Pan
-Don't be afriad to use you Revolver as spy, it is better than you may think.
-Use your shotgun every now and then.
-As medic stay behind your heal target.
-TF2 has an odd learning curve, you wil be♥♥♥♥♥♥for a while but you will quickly learn, then level off until you learn the fine tuning of the game.
-The Sticky and Rocket jumpers do no damage.
-Stock weapons are better all around weapons, unlocks have a time and place but I have found that Scout's best option is the Stock, same with Engi, Medic, and maybe Demoman.
-When Spy changing to a scout does not make you faster.
-The right click on pyro is an air-blast the reflects projectiles like rockets and grenades. (I couldn't figure that out at the start, I thought it was a gas thing where if you used it on a flaming target they would explode.)
-You will be made fun of for being a F2P, but oddly you wont be made fun of if you lack hats.
-Check out the settings, there are some class specific toggles you may want to look into.
-Again in the settings turn on hit noises, they help, along with hit numbers.
-You can bump into spys or get a pyro friend (Pybro) to help you.
-Watch some tutorial videos. Arrayseven (medic), Uncle Dane (engi), and a bunch more tubers have made very helpful videos on starting and leaning a class...
I hope these points helped... If you have any more questions just ask around.
Also side note while these videos are comedic, they are acually helpful.

Many years ago, some men were concerned about our safety, and so they tried to teach us a dance, and assured us we could leave our friends behind.  Unfortunately, the message was lost for one simple, horrible reason.  They had no hats.  Fast forward to the 21st century, and those who longed for safety and danced remained hatless, with the exception of Prince, who had a thing for certain berets.  Then came TF2, which restored hats and dancing to the world.  Unfortunately, it might have forgotten the safety part.
The impetus for this culture shift that is Team Fortress 2 was found in the cryptic writings of a large cat with a hearing impairment in ages past.  Buried among those ancient words was "No serenade, no fire brigade, just pyromania."  So it was clear that people should not sing, but rather attack each other with flamethrowers and play air guitar with weapons.  It made perfect sense.  Meanwhile, while listening to the radio, Mann Co. came to remember that they built this city, and when it was finished the engineers grew restless and bored, and began to struggle with the pyromaniacs.  As the arms race escalated, people had to come to terms that in fact this minigun-wielding man, he was not their brother, and that he was, in fact, heavy.
Because of these events, a group of private eyes were hired.  They were watching and saw every move.  They assured the world "I'm a spy, but I'm on your side."  When they cried out "hit me with your best shot, fire away!" in mockery, they were suprised to find sharpshooters from Australia eager to take them up on the offer.  The military was called in, to attempt a peaceful resolution.  The soldiers called out "come off your battlefield, lay down your arms and surrender", but  the combatants saw their rocket launchers were loaded and aimed, and attacked.
Interestly, some talent scouts for Major League Baseball were on hand, and mistook the melee for a sporting event.  Eagerly, one of the scouts shouted "put me in coach, I'm ready to play", only to be hit in the head with a frying pan.  So he called out to the nearest medic.  "Doctor, Mr. MD, won't you tell me what's ailing me?"  And he said "Yeah", before a spy snuck up on him, stabbing him in the back, and the doctor swore eternal revenge.
By then it was clear something needed to be done.  So scientists in a remote location in Scotland prepared a weapon against this madness.  They spliced the genes of Syvester Stallone and Wesley Snipes together to create a new superhero.  His name was The Demolition Man.  But this was only  a prototype, the Demolition Man Demo, and Taco Bell wasn't sure about the sponsorship.
But then there were the hats.  And people stopped fighting amongst themselves to trade these many hats that they wore.  Just kidding, they kept killing each other endlessly.  But then they questioned the conflict, and it became Mann vs Machine for a time.
The world is a safer place.  We can go where we want to.  A place that they will never find.  We could even act like we're from out of this world, and leave the real one far behind.  Because of the wonderful hats, which have brought world peace.  Although it looks an awful lot like war.

Tonight I racked up my 1000th hour in TF2. I started playing this game three years ago as a college freshman, and played off and on until now, my senior year. This game's given me sore wrists, headaches, reduced me to tears of frustration, cost me nearly a hundred dollars worth of cosmetics and most recently broken my laptop's keyboard so I have to type this on a replacement.
And I love it.
Team Fortress 2 is great. It's got all the stuff you love to see in a game- entertaining characters, fun and varied gameplay between nine brilliantly balanced characters, and a great rotation of cool maps (except Mountain Lab). But what amazes me so much about this game is how many ways there are to play it. I've done tons of regular game types, but that's only part of TF2. You want to listen to fourteen year olds claim they're big wigs on a trade server complain as you stop them from spawncamping? We got that. You want to run around on a Mario Kart map with Gmod screenshots covered in Impact font plastered everywhere? We got that. You want to play a Smash Bros. or zombie mod for stupid gimmick kicks? We got that. And heck yeah you do, those modes are awesome.
This game is some of the weirdest and stupidest fun I've ever had with a video game, and I've spent far too much time in it and all the modes above. I've grown a lot as a person with this game (i.e. I don't get so into it I have tantrums anymore, thank Christ), and met a ton of friends I've gotten to play it with too. But come on, dude, the game is free. Tons of people still play it. Download it, jump into a game, and get started!

Ok sooo TF2... where do i begin?
Gameplay: The 9 different classes add a lot of varity to the game. Example: Say You are a Pyro, (I main Pyro.) A Pyro's job is to be on the front lines and scortching the enemy team, you also are the Spy-Checker-3000, your flamethrower is the best way to check for spies, all you need to do is approach a "Teammate" and hold down the shoot button for half a second and if they catch on fire they are a spy. But if they are a good spy they will stay far away from any Pyro on your team. Here is another example: Engineers: If you are an Engineer, also known as an Engie, your job is to be not as close to the warzone as a Pyro or Scout should be, but you should be placing a teleporter in your base so then your teammates can teleport into battle. You should also be guarding a control point, you should be placing down sentry turrets to defend, and also a dispenser so if you run out of metal to upgrade your buildings with.
I have only scratched the tip of the TF2 iceberg.

Ok sooo TF2... where do i begin?
Gameplay: The 9 different classes add a lot of varity to the game. Example: Say You are a Pyro, (I main Pyro.) But if they are a good spy they will stay far away from any Pyro on your team. Here is another example: Engineers: If you are an Engineer, also known as an Engie, your job is to be not as close to the warzone as a Pyro or Scout should be, but you should be placing a teleporter in your base so then your teammates can teleport into battle. You should also be guarding a control point, you should be placing down sentry turrets to defend, and also a dispenser so if you run out of metal to upgrade your buildings with.
I have only scratched the tip of the TF2 iceberg.

Let me get this out of the way for anyone who doesn't understand what is going on. Recently, Valve totally eliminated their public servers in favour for a 'casual' feature which doesn't grant users the option to join their favourite public servers anymore. Instead, it puts users into an auto-queue, you get to decide the gamemode and map but that's about it, a large portion of the playerbase have lost the ability to play on the servers that they may have put 100's of hours into prior to the update. They are mad, which is understandable.
But ignore the toxicity of the community that has been affected by this change, Team Fortress 2 is still a fantastic game. It had a rough start but for any new players getting into the game the casual system is ideal and very well refined.
Team Fortress 2 is a game about skill and good aim. You will win games by working in unison with your team mates in order to secure an objective. There are nine playable characters each with their own unique playstyles and boundless skill ceilings. The advanced movement in TF2 is what makes it such an exceptional game, in order to become a better player you must utilise advanced movement, such as propelling your movement with your rockets as the soldier character, or with your sticky bombs as the demoman, or even something as simple as dodging as the scout class. The fact of the matter is that you will encounter players who are hundreds of times better than you and you will need to develop your gamesense and skilled movement so that you can overcome them.
The competetive gamemode is still rather undeveloped as of yet and you shouldn't try it out anytime soon.
Like many other huge PC platform games, TF2 has its own economy centred around hats, but I don't need to talk about that.
Comparing this game to Overwatch:
Team Fortress 2 is undeniably a more skill based game than Overwatched, but Overwatch is a more relaxed experience. Both games rely on team gameplay, calling out enemy strategies and planning attacks, but Overwatch lacks the skilled movement that TF2 has, staying in favour of a generic left, right, forward, backwards and jump formula, with few characters having vertical versatility. TF2 in comparison has vertical versaility with almost all of the nine characters, air strafing, rocket jumping, stickyjumping, wrangler jumping, airblast jumping, surfing rockets and trickstabbing are amongst the many things you can master in this game.
Overwatch is oriented around the ultimate abilities and basic abilities that are used to elmininate players and secure objectives whilst TF2 is always about the raw power and skill of the players pushing the objective, if you're good enough, you will in the game.
I recommend TF2.

Let's talk about one of my favorite games on Steam, TF2.
I know it's kinda strange to review a game that is free, since pretty much anybody can play it, but I really want to share my thoughts on it, since I think it's awesome.
Also, this is my first review on Steam, so please let me know what you think.
Let's talk about the graphics first.
Usually, First Person Shooter games consist of realistic graphics with a military theme.
All of these games look almost the same, with very minor differences, that you can barely tell them apart from each other.
TF2 however, went for a very cartoonish artsytle, making it stand out from the crowd.
The graphics are also over the top, with tons of explosions, blood and body parts flying all over the area, but at the same time it feels lighthearted because of the artsyle, adding to the humor of the game.
To sum it up, the graphics are very unique and add to the charm of the game.
Next let's talk about the most important part of the game, the gameplay.
For anyone who is a fan of singleplayer only games, you might be disappointed, since the game is online only (there is a practice mode where you can battle against bots, but they obviously feel very artificial).
There's also no story, well sort of. All of the story of the game is told through comics that you can read on the TF2 website, but are not available in game.
So yeah, this game is pure multiplayer, but that's not a bad thing at all.
I am a person that usually tends to dislike FPS games where the focus of the game is multiplayer like Call of Duty, since it doesn't require too much skill in my opinion, only fast reactions which causes tons of rage.
TF2 however , is different in that regard too.
This game requires a TON of skill, and because of that it might be offputting for new players, but if you stick for a while, you will see how satisfying pulling off an awesome trick is.
Also, unlike many FPS games where you can pretty much do everything on your own , in TF2 you HAVE to work as a team, after all, It's called Team Fortress, not Me Fortress.
Trying to fight three enemies, or more at a time WILL NOT work for you AT ALL.
Instead, you have to rely on your team, which also adds to the strategy of the game.
Believe me, there's a lot of strategy in this game, a lot more than you might think, one of those being the classes which I will talk about right now.
The classes are one of the things that really make this game unique.
There are nine classes, each having their own stats and playstyle.
The thing is, they are very well balanced.
Each of the classes completely change the way that you play the game, so if you get bored of playing a certain class, no problem, because you can change into another class at any given time.
I'm not going to talk about each one, but believe me, the things that each of the classes does well, they do the best, but each also has their lowpoints, which is why the classes are very well balanced.
There are also many game modes, adding even more to the variety of the game.
All of that was before the game became Free to Play, so what was added since then, and is it a Pay to Win kind of game?
The answer: alot, and not at all,
In fact, TF2 is one of the most complete F2P games I have ever played.
So what do you get in advantage of being a paid player?
Hats.
Seriously, hats.
Do they add you some sort of an extraordinary power that makes you completly overpowered, making it that nobody can beat you?
No, just hats and other cosmetics that don't change a darn thing, other than making you look fancy.
For most of the community, hats are some the most important things in TF2, leading to tons of trades and paying actual money in order to become the fanciest of them all.
I personally don't really care for the hats, only about the gameplay, but many players enjoy that, so if trading's your thing, go ahead.
Other than what I've said, what else you can buy with actual money?
Weapons.
The weapons however, can be found randomly by each player and a lot of these completely change your playstyle, adding even more to the variety.
I really like the weapons system in the game, mostly because a lot of the times, you don't put yourself in an advantage for using them, heck, sometimes it's even better to use your stock weapons that each class starts with.
So why use them?
Simply because they are fun.
They are also very well balanced (well, most of them...), so again, you don't put yourself too much in an advantage for using them.
So, basically you really don't need to become a paid player in order to enjoy the game.
The thing is, becoming a paid player is as cheap as you want it to be.
You decide how much you want to pay in order to become a paid player, and that's pretty cool.
Another thing, the game keeps being updated, despite being 7 years old, making it feel fresh.
Next, I'll talk in a brief about the game's charm.
I've already talked about the graphics, but what other things make the game charming?
Well, the characters.
Besides playing differently, they all have their own personality and in game quotes.
Some of the quotes are really funny, and the characters' personalities really shine in that regard.
Also, TF2 has some of the most clever advertising I have ever seen:the "Meet the..." videos, where the characters' personalities shine even more.
I really recommend you watching them since they are awesome.
So these are all the positives, are there any negatives?
Yes there are.
First, the auto balancing in this game can become EXTREMLY annoying.
At some points you will score many points for the team, almost close to a victory, to then be moved to the other team, resulting in a loss, which is obviously very frustrating.
Next, there are many bugs and glitches, but that to be expected from a big game as this.
And third... THE RANDOM CRITICAL HITS!!! I HATE THEM!!!
Two other negatives that I have aren't really Valve's fault but I will say them anyways.
First, the community can be extremly annoying at times.
How? By making fun of Free to Play players.
They think that just because they don't pay, it makes them bad at the game.
That logic annoys me, since I've seen F2P players that are better than some that just like to brag about their hats, but if that does happen to you, just ignore them and enjoy the game.
Second, is that because the game has been out for quite a while, there are many skilled players here, which can really frustrate newcomers, but as I've said before, stick for a while, and it will get much better.
In conclusion, I think TF2 is a fantastic game, possibly the best free game I've ever played.
If you haven't already, please play it, it's free, so you have nothing to lose.
For those asking for a score, I'll give it somewhere between 9 and 9.5 out of ten.
The reason for that score is that I think no game is perfect, but there many great games out there and this is one of them.
Highly recommended for everyone, even for those who dislike the genre, like me.

Sadly, I CANNOT recommend this game. Team Fortress 2 may be the best shooter I played so far, but there are things that will ruin any fun.
First of, matches are completely unbalanced most of the time (at least mine were). One team is full of newcomers to TF2 or people who are even trying their first ever FPS. On the other team, you got the elite of TF2 just waiting to make any enemy's life a living hell. And now take a guess in which team you will land most of the time, that's right, in the newcomer team. In the end, you'll find yourself jumping from server to server, in hopes of finding a match where everything is balanced.
Secondly, the auto-balance. It may be a good thing, it can even be disabled with a vote, but it will screw you up most of the time. You carry your team to victory, you mow down every enemy on the way to the final point or you build up an epic defense, one that seems unbreakable. Now there is a slight imbalance in the enemy team, the teams are about to be auto-balanced. It works in this way that only players who have died during the rebalance phase are switched. Suddenly, spy or sniper got you with a lucky shot or stab. Now you must defend from your former team or break the defense you helped built up. Time runs out, your team lost. I think you get the idea.
Thirdly, the class balance. This is really a major game breaker for me. More than often I wandered into spy or sniper town. Then, you got the newcomers who see you're doing good with a certain class, scout for example, suddenly you got 5 more scouts on your team, while you desperately need a medic or soldiers and demomen to break the enemy defense, but your actions as scout contribute a lot, so you can't switch without losing an important advantage. In short, more than often you'll walk into teams where there is a lot of one class, most of the time snipers and spies.
And lastly, one thing that really ruins my fun while playing Team Fortress 2, the other players. I'm not saying all players are just out for ruining your fun, but the ones who are, will make you wish you never installed the game. They spawncamp, use cheap tactics and some will belittle you in chat. It's even worse if you are new to the game, your first impression will be that the TF2 community is full of trolls, idiots and other trash of the gaming community and decide this awesome game is not worth your time.
Team Fortress 2 is awesome, I don't doubt that but these 3 points, are stressing my fun out and constantly make me think this game was better off as it was before, not free to play. For a free to play game, it's balanced, only a few weapons are ridiculously powerful but are counterable, unless people refuse to work as a TEAM in TEAM Fortess 2.
Give this game a try, if you dare. You might think I'm exaggerating with my words, but believe me I'm not. Maybe you'll be awesome at it, maybe you'll get into the most unfair matches ever. But please, give it a try, test yourself in the training mode first so you can see how most of the game works, then try multiplayer. If you like it, stay if you want. If you don't like it, leave, this game can be addicting, no matter how much it screws over your fun.

Now, I'm going to be straightforward with you, this is likely one of the most fun games I have ever played, which really says something being the avid gamer I am.
The thing is, this game is unlike any first-person shooter out there. The combination of all the classes' hilarious backgrounds and the ridiculous chaos that can go on makes this game worthy of praise. Another thing that makes this game so wonderful though is it's not too hard to learn. Whether you prefer standing in high places picking off your enemies one by one as a sniper, or just want to cause as much damage as you can as a heavy, Team Fortress 2 allows you to use your own fighting style in battle.
Another great feature of the game is that Valve works on it constantly. The game is very seasonal, whether you're in Halloween or Christmas, Team Fortress 2 adapts to all of it, whether you're facing The Horseless Headless Horsemann (yes that's its actual name) and Merasmus The Wizard in Halloween season or enjoying the festivities of Christmas, Team Fortress 2 has it all.
Something else that makes this game unique is you can make money, yes, money off of it. If you are a skilled 3D Model maker, this game allows for workshop submissions that Valve might add to the game if they like it. If you're more of a Co-op guy or girl, Team Fortress 2 accomodates that too. Mann Vs. Machine is a great way to take your anger out on vast numbers of robots. Now, I could go on and on about this game, but I'm going to cut myself short.
My final words about it, Get this game. You won't regret it.

Team Fortress 2 has been in my library for 2 years now, and I have not stopped enjoying the fast-paced, team-based, tactical battles. Team Fortress 2 offers a wide variety of different gamemodes, maps, and guns. The game is very user-friendly as you can click through the manu, customize your classes, and find a match with ease. The actual gameplay though is different then you ever thought it would be. The battles usually range between 5-20 minute matches with 10-30 players playing. You can choose between Offensive, Defensive, and Supportive classes offering different perks to the team. But these class types all have to work in unison to destroy the other team. Almost every gamemode in Team Fortress is team based from Attack/Defend, Payload, Special Delivery, Etc. I would recomend this game to all casual and competitive gamers and always will.

With well over a 1,000 hours into this game, I thought I would give my final opinions before I quit. Despite the vast amount of playtime i've accumulated, I do not still fully recommend this game to everyone. It has some major flaws especially in its player base that are irreversably cancerous.
+Fun, fast paced gameplay
+Free to play
+Unitrusive microtransactions
+Cool misc gear to hoard
+Co-op is great fun
+Cool weapons
+Almost every class is fun to play, however not all as effective as the others and easy to pick up on.
-Free to play also means an ABSOLUTE CANCER fanbase. That is the ultimate killer for this game. Nearly every player you cross is a child. Though some may not care and simply mute voice chat; it's far worse than just their spam and voices. This game heavily relies on multiplayer interactions, and because everyone is an idiot those interactions mostly consists of people running around taunting, attempting trick shots, and making no actual attempt to play the game. Without any dedicated ranked mode this also means more experienced players have to deal with this frequently, and new players either get absolutely♥♥♥♥♥♥on, or annoyed enough by the idiots around them to up and quit just hours into the game. This really can't be fixed, but it should be noted for anyone going into this game. About 90% of the people who play this game are just ♥♥♥♥ing stupid.
-Some weapons encourage previously mentioned autistic behavior. There are multiple weapons that are absolutely useless in competitve play like the rocket jumper or the sticky jumper, yet people still sport these weapons and aimlessly launch themselves around the map, being of no actual benefit to the game. With how the weapons are designed this almost seems intentional.
-Each class has it's own quirky character. Some people find their dialogue funny, I found it pretty annoying, especially with children constantly repeating their lines in my ear.
-No real balancing. While each class does have its way to counter another there are some more unfortunate than others. The spy for example is near-useless for competitve play. Sure, he can take out "key targets" if he gets close enough without getting absolutely destroyed, but doing so is a death sentence. When at the same time the sniper can do the exact same far more efficiently. Sure he can sap a sentry gun, which again will most likely get him killed, the sapper removed, and a demoman can just as easily get it done, while being a lot more helpful to his team. Pyro and engineer are super easy to play and render the classes that actually require skill useless. Taking the time to get skilled in the game is honestly a fruitless effort.

With well over a 1,000 hours into this game, I thought I would give my final opinions before I quit. Despite the vast amount of playtime i've accumulated, I do not still fully recommend this game to everyone. It has some major flaws especially in its player base that are irreversably cancerous.
+Fun, fast paced gameplay
+Free to play
+Unitrusive microtransactions
+Cool misc gear to hoard
+Co-op is great fun
+Cool weapons
+Almost every class is fun to play, however not all as effective as the others and easy to pick up on.
-Free to play also means an ABSOLUTE CANCER fanbase. That is the ultimate killer for this game. Nearly every player you cross is a child. Though some may not care and simply mute voice chat; it's far worse than just their spam and voices. This game heavily relies on multiplayer interactions, and because everyone is an idiot those interactions mostly consists of people running around taunting, attempting trick shots, and making no actual attempt to play the game. Without any dedicated ranked mode this also means more experienced players have to deal with this frequently, and new players either get absolutely♥♥♥♥♥♥on, or annoyed enough by the idiots around them to up and quit just hours into the game. This really can't be fixed, but it should be noted for anyone going into this game. About 90% of the people who play this game are just ♥♥♥♥ing stupid.
-Some weapons encourage previously mentioned autistic behavior. There are multiple weapons that are absolutely useless in competitve play like the rocket jumper or the sticky jumper, yet people still sport these weapons and aimlessly launch themselves around the map, being of no actual benefit to the game. With how the weapons are designed this almost seems intentional.
-Each class has it's own quirky character. Some people find their dialogue funny, I found it pretty annoying, especially with children constantly repeating their lines in my ear.
-No real balancing. While each class does have its way to counter another there are some more unfortunate than others. The spy for example is near-useless for competitve play. Sure, he can take out "key targets" if he gets close enough without getting absolutely destroyed, but doing so is a death sentence. When at the same time the sniper can do the exact same far more efficiently. Sure he can sap a sentry gun, which again will most likely get him killed, the sapper removed, and a demoman can just as easily get it done, while being a lot more helpful to his team. Pyro and engineer are super easy to play and render the classes that actually require skill useless. Taking the time to get skilled in the game is honestly a fruitless effort.
-$1,000 virtual hats is ♥♥♥♥ing stupid
It's a solid shooter with some minor design flaws and a really ♥♥♥♥♥♥ fanbase, but it's done its job for several years, and will hold me over until Overwatch comes out. 6/10

All the way from 2007 and still going strong. When I quote, ''going strong'' I usually tend to think so in the community workshop and hat section of this game. Although they aren't the main aspects of this game, but on a serious note, this game is excellent, fun and arguably flawless. So, what's the best of it now? Well, it's totally free and definitely worthy of the quote; ''The most fun you can have online.'' coming from the humble editors of PC Gamer magazine.
The game has a wide and diverse selection of 9 different classes, ranging from their own unique abilities and strategies that can be performed against the opposing team. Similiar to a ''rock, paper, scissors'' scenario, where everything is fair and there are no ''over-powered'' classes. The fast, Boston-talking and even more fast running Scout, to the towering, minigun-wielding hulk of a Russian man, known as the Heavy. Every character class usually represents a soldier in a common FPS' of some sort. What I truly love about these characters is the fact that Valve has openly breathed life, vibrant personalities, characteristics and nationalities into this rag-tag bunch. I also enjoyed the customization of weapons and accessories, named after the witty puns, along with the slight ethnic slur and referenced culture of that said character. This really brings out the comedic flare within the game and shows that humour can mix amusement in along with entertainment the players from around the globe can express and relate to, depending on the gamer's nationality.
When it comes to the plot of the game, the elements of storytelling isn't entirely shown into clear perception. It mainly focuses on the two, competitive industries of RED (Reliable Excavation Demolition) and BLU. (Builders League United) Who both subsequently conquer half of the world, known as the Badlands. Each corporation administers its half of the world with a multi-disciplined army of paper pushers. One of those ''paper pushers'' is you and your whole team, when playing this game.
A fantastic thing to note in this game is the fact that it's holiday themed. Either new campaigns modeled after a specific holiday, down to the newly cashed in, fan made hats are launched to the public to bring in funds for both Valve and the original creator at hand. Halloween, Christmas, Easter just to name a few are a great example and addition to the game's growing campaign and community. It's also important to note that the game is getting updated at a steady pace, with the occasional UI updates and other fun concepts, such as poses and character interactions being frequently implemented to wet the appetites of the individual player's preference.
I don't have much to complain about this game, other than the fact that majority of the servers you connect to, you'll most likely encounter 13-year-olds who constantly nag and try their luck to command the rest of the whole team, which sometimes resorts to foreign/eastern european person nagging about the 13-year-old's nagging, so it's not rare to see a big kick off between young kids and ignorant foreign kids going absolute bonkers on a connected match. It's more fun to not say a word at this point in time and just watch the ultimate climax between the raging two forces.
I definitely recommend this game. Not just down to the fact that it's free, but because it still remains fun to this day and constant updates on campaigns and official hat accessories keep this game alive, making the game overall timeless...which, doesn't affect the game's mechanics at all but, only along the lines of taunts and so on and so forth.

11/23/2016 update: I nominated this game for the "You Either Die A Hero, Or You Live Long Enough To See Yourself Become The Villain" award for the Steam Awards of 2016.
11/22/2017 update: I nominated this game for the “Labor of Love” award for the Steam Awards of 2017.
========================================
Absolutely recommended, regardless of whether or not you enjoy FPS games or even games in general. As it is free-to-play, it only costs your time to investigate if this is a game for you. This is the only game that brings a smile to my face and for which I laugh out loud every single time I play it.
PROS:
-Hilarious team-centered gameplay that can consistently make you laugh out loud even if you're losing a match
-Distinct and memorable character classes that suit different play styles
-Unique and pleasant graphical fidelity that suits the game's intentions well
-Excellent and constantly improving level design
-Variety of classic and newer game play modes provide fun for all types of players
-Good bots included for offline practice
-Wealth of options readily available in-game to ensure the game looks and handles the way you want
-Many (emphasis) hats, other cosmetic items, and item modifiers available for customizing your look
-Free item drops, with an average 1 random drop per hour
-Many free updates that have added weapons, maps, production value, improved performance, story, play modes, and by extension new ways to play the game. All of this has made the game more fun over the years and helped to grow its diverse and largely vibrant community
CONS:
-The addition of so much content over the years has had some impact on game stability, though this is often fixed eventually via free updates
-Some nasty exploits available that can ruin the game for some players, though these are usually eventually fixed via free updates
-No obvious classic 'team deathmatch' play mode. The CTF map 2Fort is often used as a team deathmatch map as a result
-A lot of the story is explained outside the game via entertaining comics and high quality videos. I am fine with this, though this could frustrate players more interested in storytelling within games
-The game is free-to-play, however a minimal monetary investment is required to begin unlocking more than 50 items. Veterans used to learn the game mecanics by themselves since there is no other way of learning to play this game. The game's clear and prime purpose is to let the player taste all the different kinds of FPS modes possibly open in the gaming industry.
How?
-You are able to chose between 9 Classes that have individual personalities,background and lore.
*Characters do not only have individual personalities that will slightly but surely enhance your gameplay, but they also have different styles of play which are keen in order to win the game (NO I'M NOT TALKING ABOUT 9 SNIPERS IN EACH MAP!)
-Different Modes, which will enhance your experience of the game and you will understand different aspects of each map which is linked in different gaming mode.
The game also offers alot of materialistic features such as: Hats,Miscs,Weapons,Taunts and others..
Why are they included in the FPS game?
-Well,let's say these materialistic features that I have mentioned above, are the addons to the game that will let the player customize his class in his own unique way, meaning that the enlightened purpose of these miscs and hats is to make the player feel comfortable with his own style and surely to allow the player to show his uniqueness.
I played this game alot in the past through different use of accounts, but I am surely recommending this game as it has got a high popularity, the game's authority is at the toppest (which is clearly seen in the game ranking ladder on Steam).

This is a well made, stylized, team based first person shooter. Teamwork is needed to win at higher levels of play, though lone wolfing is fine on lower skill levels such as on most public servers. There are 9 classes to choose from. Each class has unique weapons and abilities that allow each to fulfill a unique roll as part of a larger team. This provides for a challenging and rewarding experience when faced against opponents of similar or better skill levels. The game has an active dev team that continues to release updates to the game that add new content such as weapons or game modes.
At the time of this review, there are two official modes of play: player versus player and 'Mann Versus Machine'.
Player versus player is a mode where one team of players battles against another team of players. Within this mode, there are different types of maps. Each type of map has it's own objective or objectives for each team to achieve.
'Mann Versus Machine' is a mode where a team of up to 6 players battles against waves of bots. Players collect money from destroyed bots. The money is divided equally among players in the team and can be used to purchase upgrades and abilities for the next wave of bots. The pay to play sub-mode, "Mann Up", gives rewards upon completing a "tour".
In addition to the official modes of play, there are several player made mods that introduce other modes of play such as 'Versus Saxton Hale', where a team of players battles against a player playing as a character named Saxton Hale; 'Dodge Ball', where two teams of players playing as Pyros must airblast rockets and other projectiles back and forth in order to stay alive; 'Zombie Mod', where a team of players must make it to the end of the map without dying to zombies that are played by other players; to name just a few of the many player made mods available.
In addition to game play, players will randomly receive free items from the game. Some of the free items given out are weapons, hats and crates. Hats can be worn by a class to change the appearance of that class. Crates can be opened with a key. Keys can be purchased from the Mann Co Store or from the Steam Community Market or traded for from another player. Most crates will list which items can be found within them.
The game has several communities for a player to choose from if a community is what you are looking for. The game is easy to pick up and play, either alone or with friends, yet has a depth of play that will keep you from becoming bored too quickly. The dynamics between the different classes, weapons, play styles, skill levels, modes and maps provides content for many hours of play.

As a sniper i always tend to find my self in the worst place possible being chased by a heavy, shot at by a soldier, and getting hit by a scout with a bat. When i join a server i love to hear the squeal of the squeakers who play this graphic game. Here is the list of people i always meet on servers.
Camper= Sits at spawn or at a distance (Sniper class) and waits until someone walks out of spawn.
Rager= Continue calling every one names when his team looses the round and says "YOU GUYS SUCK AT PLAY TF2!" when he has 0 points and 9 deaths.
Squeaker= Sound's like a seven year old throwing the f bomb when ever he kills someone.
Try hard= Always at the front and trys to kill as many people as possible in one life.
That one person who takes the game seriouse= Back stab him and he turns into a pyro and yells at you when he kills you.
The troll= Acts like he dosent know how to play and messes up every thing for every one.
#YoloSwag= The person who spams the chat with #Yolo, #SWAG. And spams the chat with bad words when there is squeakers playing the game.
Last of all: The dude who brags about his hats: The guy who brags about his hats is the dude that you know played for 7 years straight of team fortress and has earned all the collectables and all the guns in the whole entire game.
Lets talk about the servers now:
Some servers are all right. But the ones  that really get me are the ones with high pings, annyoing adds in the loading screen that causes lags and plays music or a movie trailer. Some server have just horrible admins. I was searching around in team fortress and found that and Admin on a "Server i shall not name" banned someone because they killed them with a backstab. Servers that actually are good are worth playing but the thing that ruins is the power hungry admins that if you do something wrong they ban you for life.
Charactor hats and weapons:
We all like dressing our team fortress charactors up. I myself do. But when it comes to get stuff the prices can be high. I mean you can buy a pink tu-tu if you wanted to for 1.00. But in the team fortress store or called Mann-Co, The price for a pink tu-tu can be up to 7.49. I mean buying a hat for 7.00 even if its a tie for the spy is a little over priced. The other day i came across three hats stacked on each other. Their price was a whopping 7.49. I was also looking for things for the Engineer. I came across this Triple chin i really liked. 10.00. I don't know what valves trying to do. But i know its prices are not worth the hat.
Game Overall: I personally would rate the game a 8/10. Just because its a fun first shooter dispite all its down's. The upside of the game is that you can make friends and trade weapons for more usefull things. It has an offline practice mode that you can train yourself. So after looking at all these things its worth playing. I would recomend to friends who don't have this game.. Plus its FREE!
