Team Fortress 2 has allot to offer, and delivers on it's expectations for it's fans.
About two years ago I started playing this game out of pure curiousity, and found myself in admiration of what the core feature of this game was. I kept playing it and finding more items to the point that I need to stop being f2p. The item system in this game is truly fascinating, and is worth holding a conversation about. I found myself playing this game allot and over the past two years I've punched in over 900 hours on it (and I'm still really bad). I find the system of weapons and cosmetics was a truly unique one. The way people make fun of cosmetics is a rather stupid decision. The cosmetics, name tags, weapons, etc. Make you able to stand out from everyone else. I find myself playing this game quite often, and loving it even more every time. I love the other forms of intertainment that Valve (The Producers) update quite often (The Web-Comic, SFM Series, Etc.). I feel as if just talking about this game isn't doing it any justice. Go and play it and see for yourself if you enjoy it.
I give this game a solid 8.6/10.0

It's unique take on a genre of gaming that has otherwise become dull.
An active community that is only growing and becoming for friendly torwards eachother.
An item system that allows you and your class loadout to stand out.
A truly fun experience that keeps you coming back for more.

Team Fortress 2 is one of those games that you find yourself coming back to over and over again. Not because its intense gameplay, its unique industrialesque Norman Rockwell artstyle, its hundreds of playstyles and customization, or even its free pricetag. Team Fortress 2 is the kind of game that leaves a lasting impression because its massive community of friendly and sometimes not so friendly players and it's heavy involvement with the community (such as community driven items and as of this review the upcoming community update End of the Line). People that play a game for casual relaxation or intense combat. Those who make longlasting friendships and sometimes shortterm rivalry. Those who invest themselve in a virtual marketplace finding themselves learning economics based of rising and lowering prices of metal and keys. Team Fortress 2 is an experience well past the boundaries of just gaming, it has a well planned and written lore that has made itself into movie quality animation and comics that bring a multitude of emotion through their art and captions. Never before have I seen a game that has made a holiday like Halloween into an event more for teamwork and community than scares and candy. Never before have I seen a game with such impressive ARG's that make people hyped for robots and bread. Valve has blessed the world with a gift that I am sure will go down with the ages amongst other great titles and so I say to you, If you've never tried this game sit down one evening and play it. It's free and goes long beyond the boundaries of a standard first person shooting hat simulator.
Felt the need to update this review now that the game has celebrated its tenth anniversary. Even after ten years the creators still show compassion and support towards it's community by creating animations, new features, and new content. At times it may seem drawn out and far between but this is a company who still cares about it's dear creation and a franchise that has turned 21. I think that Valve earns some mad respect for that. It has been a wild ride, here's to the next 10 years!

Team Fortress 2 is a  Class Based FPS game (First person shooter). In the game there are 9 classes: Scout, Soldier, Pyro, Demoman,Heavy,Engineer,Medic,Sniper,Spy. Each of theese classes have their own powers. For sample: Scout can double jump. The graphics are great. In the newest update "Inferno Update" the menu layout is changed a bit, but it is still easy to navigate. There are 520 Achievements. Not all Achievements are hard but some Achievements are hard.
Here are the basics of the game:
After you downloaded the game, i recommend to go on the training menu. You will have hard times if you miss it.
Make sure you join VAC secured servers. Is it a bad time when somebody is hacking, don't worry if you are in VAC secured servers. I should introduce the 9 classes. Scout: The fastest in the game. Has the ability to double jump. I'm recommending this class to first play with it. Soldier: An American mercenary with a giant Rocket launcher. If you have some experience you can learn rocket jumping. Pyro: A guy who has a Flame Thrower. He/She has a gas mask. Nobody knows if it is a Boy or Girl. Demoman: An Alcoholic guy with a Grenade Launcher. He has a Stickybomb Launcher too. Heavy: a "Fat" Russian man with a giant Minigun. His favourite food is the legendary "SANDWICH". Engineer: He is an Engineer with a shotgun,pistol and a wrench. He has a very helpful device: Construction PDA. He can build Sentry guns, Dispesners, Teleporters with it. (One at a time) He has a: Destruction PDA too. He can destroy his buildings. Medic: He has a syringe gun, medigun, bonesaw. The syringe gun is not strong at all, i dont recommend it. The Medigun is a "gun" but you can heal your teammates with it. The bonesaw is his primary weapon, it's a bit stronger than the syringe gun. Sniper: A Sniper with a Sniper Rifle,SMG,Kukri. With the Sniper Rifle you can zoom and unzoom with right click. SMG:just hold Left Mouse button. The kukri is a machete thingy. Spy is a super class. He has a Pistol, Disguise kit, Electro-Sapper, Invisibility Cloak, The Pistol is a single pistol. The Disguise kit, you can disguise as your enemies (they can spot you easily) Electro sapper: You can ZAP the enemy engineers buildings. If you press right mouse button you can be invisivble for a short time (if you touch an enemy or you get damaged you will lost your invisibility).

Ah, Good ol' Tee Eff Too. This game is really what started Steam, and gaming other than Minecraft, for me. After many hours of playing this game, I can't actually remember how I discovered it, but whenever I get on I enjoy myself a lot. I'll start of by listing some highs and lows of this game:
Pros:
-Longevity. This game was made in 2007 (correct me if I'm wrong,) and it has only been improved on since, and it has such good replay value as well.
-Items. Tf2 is known for the customizations, both cosmetic and involving choice of weapons. I don't think that there are way too many items, but it is just at a perfect amount. More cosmetics are constantly being added, and that most of them come from the community makes it even better. There could be some more items added, but if more and more were put in, the game would definitely become cluttered with unneccessary and gimmicky items that would detract from the Tf2 experience.
-F2P. Team Fortress 2, although a free to play game, is not a pay to win. Yes, money will get you hats, but they don't directly affect the gameplay.
-Choice of classes. Tf2 allows for the player to choose a class that each has different attributes to play as. They are all balanced, and they all play differently, and require some mastery to get quite good. Personally, I like to play as the Scout, Soldier, and Spy.
Cons:
-Crates. In Team Fortess 2, there are crates that can be unlocked with Mann Co. Supply Crate Keys. Each series of crate has a different set of items, but they are usually worth next to nothing unless you get lucky and end out getting a super-rare unusual. Another thing is that keys cost money and you can't find them in the standard drop system.
-Trading. The actual aspect of trading in this game, and games in general is almost always a good thing. It's even fairly good in this game, but in order to get some high value items, you basically NEED to pay for them on the market, or get keys to trade for them. I just think that this whole system is flawed. I guess that you can just craft items together to get metal, but that process takes FOREVER. I've kind of done it, but it takes numerous hours to at least get a hat. ._.
Aside from those two cons, Team Fortress 2 is very good. Nothing about the physical gameplay is flawed, which is really good for a game. Overall, tf2 is a great game. It is fun for any level of gamer, whether you be a professional or someone who just started. It does require some practice to do well on multiplayer, but the practicing is actually fun! Team Fortress 2 is one of those games that you find yourself coming back to over and over again. Not because its intense gameplay, its unique industrialesque Norman Rockwell artstyle, its hundreds of playstyles and customization, or even its free pricetag. Team Fortress 2 is the kind of game that leaves a lasting impression because its massive community of friendly and sometimes not so friendly players and it's heavy involvement with the community (such as community driven items and as of this review the upcoming community update End of the Line). People that play a game for casual relaxation or intense combat. Those who make longlasting friendships and sometimes shortterm rivalry. Those who invest themselve in a virtual marketplace finding themselves learning economics based of rising and lowering prices of metal and keys. Team Fortress 2 is an experience well past the boundaries of just gaming, it has a well planned and written lore that has made itself into movie quality animation and comics that bring a multitude of emotion through their art and captions. Never before have I seen a game that has made a holiday like Halloween into an event more for teamwork and community than scares and candy. Never before have I seen a game with such impressive ARG's that make people hyped for robots and bread. Valve has blessed the world with a gift that I am sure will go down with the ages amongst other great titles and so I say to you, If you've never tried this game sit down one evening and play it. It's free and goes long beyond the boundaries of a standard first person shooting hat simulator.
Felt the need to update this review now that the game has celebrated its tenth anniversary. Even after ten years the creators still show compassion and support towards it's community by creating animations, new features, and new content. At times it may seem drawn out and far between but this is a company who still cares about it's dear creation and a franchise that has turned 21. I think that Valve earns some mad respect for that. It has been a wild ride, here's to the next 10 years!

Team Fortress 2 is a  Class Based FPS game (First person shooter). In the game there are 9 classes: Scout, Soldier, Pyro, Demoman,Heavy,Engineer,Medic,Sniper,Spy. Each of theese classes have their own powers. For sample: Scout can double jump. The graphics are great. In the newest update "Inferno Update" the menu layout is changed a bit, but it is still easy to navigate. There are 520 Achievements. Not all Achievements are hard but some Achievements are hard.
Here are the basics of the game:
After you downloaded the game, i recommend to go on the training menu. You will have hard times if you miss it.
Make sure you join VAC secured servers. Is it a bad time when somebody is hacking, don't worry if you are in VAC secured servers. I should introduce the 9 classes. Scout: The fastest in the game. Has the ability to double jump. I'm recommending this class to first play with it. Soldier: An American mercenary with a giant Rocket launcher. If you have some experience you can learn rocket jumping. Pyro: A guy who has a Flame Thrower. He/She has a gas mask. Nobody knows if it is a Boy or Girl. Demoman: An Alcoholic guy with a Grenade Launcher. He has a Stickybomb Launcher too. Heavy: a "Fat" Russian man with a giant Minigun. His favourite food is the legendary "SANDWICH". Engineer: He is an Engineer with a shotgun,pistol and a wrench. He has a very helpful device: Construction PDA. He can build Sentry guns, Dispesners, Teleporters with it. (One at a time) He has a: Destruction PDA too. He can destroy his buildings. Medic: He has a syringe gun, medigun, bonesaw. The syringe gun is not strong at all, i dont recommend it. The Medigun is a "gun" but you can heal your teammates with it. The bonesaw is his primary weapon, it's a bit stronger than the syringe gun. Sniper: A Sniper with a Sniper Rifle,SMG,Kukri. With the Sniper Rifle you can zoom and unzoom with right click. SMG:just hold Left Mouse button. The kukri is a machete thingy. Spy is a super class. He has a Pistol, Disguise kit, Electro-Sapper, Invisibility Cloak, The Pistol is a single pistol. The Disguise kit, you can disguise as your enemies (they can spot you easily) Electro sapper: You can ZAP the enemy engineers buildings. If you press right mouse button you can be invisivble for a short time (if you touch an enemy or you get damaged you will lost your invisibility).

Team Fortress 2 is a  Class Based FPS game (First person shooter). In the game there are 9 classes: Scout, Soldier, Pyro, Demoman,Heavy,Engineer,Medic,Sniper,Spy. Each of theese classes have their own powers. For sample: Scout can double jump. The graphics are great. In the newest update "Inferno Update" the menu layout is changed a bit, but it is still easy to navigate. There are 520 Achievements. Not all Achievements are hard but some Achievements are hard.
Here are the basics of the game:
After you downloaded the game, i recommend to go on the training menu. You will have hard times if you miss it.
Make sure you join VAC secured servers. Is it a bad time when somebody is hacking, don't worry if you are in VAC secured servers. I should introduce the 9 classes. Scout: The fastest in the game. Has the ability to double jump. I'm recommending this class to first play with it. Soldier: An American mercenary with a giant Rocket launcher. If you have some experience you can learn rocket jumping. Pyro: A guy who has a Flame Thrower. He/She has a gas mask. Nobody knows if it is a Boy or Girl. Demoman: An Alcoholic guy with a Grenade Launcher. He has a Stickybomb Launcher too. Heavy: a "Fat" Russian man with a giant Minigun. His favourite food is the legendary "SANDWICH". Engineer: He is an Engineer with a shotgun,pistol and a wrench. He has a very helpful device: Construction PDA. He can build Sentry guns, Dispesners, Teleporters with it. (One at a time) He has a: Destruction PDA too. He can destroy his buildings. Medic: He has a syringe gun, medigun, bonesaw. The syringe gun is not strong at all, i dont recommend it. The Medigun is a "gun" but you can heal your teammates with it. The bonesaw is his primary weapon, it's a bit stronger than the syringe gun. Sniper: A Sniper with a Sniper Rifle,SMG,Kukri. With the Sniper Rifle you can zoom and unzoom with right click. SMG:just hold Left Mouse button. The kukri is a machete thingy. Spy is a super class. He has a Pistol, Disguise kit, Electro-Sapper, Invisibility Cloak, The Pistol is a single pistol. The Disguise kit, you can disguise as your enemies (they can spot you easily) Electro sapper: You can ZAP the enemy engineers buildings. If you press right mouse button you can be invisivble for a short time (if you touch an enemy or you get damaged you will lost your invisibility).

Team Fortress 2
The short answer is, it's holding up very well. The core action pits two teams of players against each other in a battle to capture points, move a cart, or steal a briefcase. The objective is always very straightforward; it's the interplay between the nine playable classes that makes things so varied and interesting. The speedy scout, the militant heavy, the diligent engineer, the conniving medic, the pesky sniper, the sneaky spy, the feisty pyro, the explosive soldier, and the even-more-explosive demoman all have unique weapons, attributes, and abilities that complement each other and clash in myriad ways. Encounters can vary widely depending on the match type and the makeup of each team, and this unpredictability is crucial to TF2's long-standing appeal.

Team Fortress 2, where do I even start... THIS GAME IS FREAKING AWESOME! I have played Team Fortress 2 for 2 years now (love the irony), and I have just yet to stop loving this game. It is constantly updated with new gamemodes, weapons, maps, and of course HATS! This game has got to be one of the finest free to play First Person Shooters out there, and heck it might be one of the best first person shooters out there period. It has nine different classes to choose from all with unique weapons, abilities, and playstyles (my personal favorite is the soldier). It is wonderfully balanced and takes a lot of skill to master many of the classes. It has random drops so if you don't want to pay to get new things you can just have items drop (I suggest spending money on something say for example a hat because it then allows you to trade).
Overall, Team Fortress 2 is probally my favorite game of all time so far and gets my first 10 out of 10 on any of my reviews.

This is a well thought out team based first person shooter. The game encourages teamwork to win against players of higher skill or well-organized teams. Lone wolfing can still be done on lower levels, especially on public game servers.
There are 9 classes to choose from, each one offering unique skill sets and abilities that allow them to fill in a unique role as part of the team as a whole. Because of this, the player is rewarded with a challenging and fun-filled experience, especially when faced against opponents or teams with similar or greater skill.
Even though this game was released way back in 2007, the game continues to have an active development team that continues to release updates to the game that add new content, such as new unique weapons or game modes. At the time of this review, the Team Fortress community is preparing for the upcoming Halloween update, which has been an annual event in the game since 2009.
While this game is extremely fun and rewarding to play, I have noticed how complex the game has become in regards to new items and game mechanics. I became introduced to this game in 2011, and gradually learned the ropes of the game over time. However, I have noticed how newer players have reported having a hard time grasping how all of the items work and in general feeling a sense of information overload. In order for them to not be considered a "noob" at this game, they must experiment and test with all of the items in the game to have a full understanding of what weapon(s) should be used in certain situations.
All of this, however, is a small issue amidst the big picture. This game is fantastic and, being a free-to-play game, allows players to have loads of fun without having to make a big down payment to enjoy it. I continue to return to the game on a daily basis.

After 300 plus hours of tf2 I think it's time I have this game a review.
Team Fortress 2, a pay to play game that has found success as a free to play title. Tf2 is a class based, team based first person shooter developed by none other than Valve. Being a team based class based shooter is one of the few aspects that differentiates Tf2 from other shooter. With 9 different classes and tons of different maps anf game modes , this game will surely keep you hooked for a while.
The visuals of the game are pretty unique, with a more cartoony and humourous art style rather than a grim serious one. The game is a source engine game so it doesn't look too stunning but it runs perfectly fine and is not very graphically demanding.
The gameplay in this game is pretty interesting. Being that there is 9 different classes means that there is different play styles and even then each class has a different play style to them. You can be a pyro and mw1 your way to victory or you can be a degreaser pyro, air blasting damage and being more skillful. Or even a pybro which is a play style designed to aid engineers and help defend their buildings. Honestly the possibilitys are endless and each class has a unique role to play.
Since this is a f2p title I'll have to assess it's business model. Out of all the free 2 play models this one is by far the best. All weapons in the game are free to use and can be received in drops that occur a few times per day. The only time you would have to fork over money is to buy cosmetics and cosmetics only. Bottom line the business model is quite generous and I like it and judging From the games success, it works.
Now with the recent emerge of class based team based  shooters such as overwatch, you may ask what is to happen to tf2? Would it die off? Well my an to that question is no. Although tf2 is nearly 10 years old it still stands strong as a f2p shooter and from what I've seen over watch is completely different, and favours a more CoD style mechanic as the fame is going to be released I  consoles as well. There was also a recent interest by valve in this game and tf2 is soon to have a competitive match making system, similar to that of csgo.
To conclude this is undoubtedly one of the best f2p titles out there and I would encourage everone to try it at least once. It doesn't matter if your bad at shooters or you don't like how the game looks, the is something for everyone to try out in this game.

A unique thing that Team Fortress 2 offers, unlike most First Person Shooters, is a system of trading. You give items to another player worth a specific value, they do the same back. Overall,  any new person looking for a top notch game to get into, Team Fortress 2 is for sure one of the best.

Team Fortress 2, or TF2, is a good game in all, give a wide variety between all the classes. It makes the players focus on working together more than being a long wolf. The game is very much like its own genre, being focused on offnece and defence. With nine classes to chose from, three for; offence, defence, and support it is easy to find a class that best suits your play style.
The multiplayer is nice and the community is good and responsive with many features on it.
The games features two different multiplayer mode, being co-op and competitive.
1-The co-op is like a horde vs the group defending a point of interest, killing robots with many buy-able upgrades to help
2-The competitive is two teams trying to get one objective done, in some instances one might be defending will the other attacks.

This game is SO awesome! Unlike most shooting games, you have a goal to accomplish, either one, capture control points before time runs out (similar to capture the flag), play king of the hill, and keep a single control point safe from the other team, or, push a cart with a bomb to the other team's base. I will, right now, list pros and cons of this game.
Pros: Smooth controls, and a HUGE variety of ways to customize your character.
Each character suits for a person's liking.
Many details of the game such as the characters can be humorous.
This game is FREE
Cons: If your computer is old, prepare for a "lagfest."
The item drop system can be really hard to activate and it takes a while to get new items.
Score 9/10: This game will bring joy to anybody who likes FPS games, or people who just want to have fun!

The number one thing you need to have for TF2 is; 1. Online Connection (obviously) and 2. Friends (which shouldn't be hard because almost everyone that has Steam plays this game!). The reason you need your friends is so you can do teamwork easily (but you can work with complete strangers if you want to). There is also a Practice mode, this can help you become a better player without the hassel of other people. Overall, this is a really good game. It's fun, it's quick, it's exciting. I'm giving it 9/10!

Team Fortress 2, or TF2, is a good game in all, give a wide variety between all the classes. It makes the players focus on working together more than being a long wolf. The game is very much like its own genre, being focused on offnece and defence. With nine classes to chose from, three for; offence, defence, and support it is easy to find a class that best suits your play style.
The multiplayer is nice and the community is good and responsive with many features on it.
The games features two different multiplayer mode, being co-op and competitive.
1-The co-op is like a horde vs the group defending a point of interest, killing robots with many buy-able upgrades to help
2-The competitive is two teams trying to get one objective done, in some instances one might be defending will the other attacks.

This game is SO awesome! Unlike most shooting games, you have a goal to accomplish, either one, capture control points before time runs out (similar to capture the flag), play king of the hill, and keep a single control point safe from the other team, or, push a cart with a bomb to the other team's base. I will, right now, list pros and cons of this game.
Pros: Smooth controls, and a HUGE variety of ways to customize your character.
Each character suits for a person's liking.
Many details of the game such as the characters can be humorous.
This game is FREE
Cons: If your computer is old, prepare for a "lagfest."
The item drop system can be really hard to activate and it takes a while to get new items.
Score 9/10: This game will bring joy to anybody who likes FPS games, or people who just want to have fun!

Team Fortress 2-----> a free cartoonish action/shooting game.
"Why should I play it?" BECAUSE IT'S A FRIKIN' HILARIOUS, AWESOME AND CHALLENGING GAME!
"Why is it challenging?" You can always try to get some items to use in-game, sell or trade or you can try to unlock some achievements to  show how MLG you are. But the main point is that you want to shoot the living hell out of everyone you play against.
"I'm getting bored of this game." Something is wrong with you. But don't worry, they made some mods in the game like Deathrun or Slender to keep bored people like you amused.
"How are the graphics and sound aspects?" Just try to play and you'll experience it. If the game doesn't work on your computer, then buy a new one...
"What's the best way to play this game, with friends or on your own?" Try to play with some friends because I think it's more amusing when you work together to destroy the enemy, but it's also funny to dominate your friends when you're playing against them. Playing alone is an option, it's still nice to play. But if you want to play TF2 with other people you like, try to get some friends...
EDIT: I'm sorry if I insulted someone with this review, but TF2 is still fun to play (at least, that's my opinion). :D

Probably the best free-to-play on steam. Its got a little something for everyone. Want to run around burning stuff? Done. Want to blast away your enemies? Done. Maybe sit back and snipe? Got it. Stealthily dodging enemies and tricking them? Can do it. Build sentries and teleporters? Easy. Or maybe heal your teammates and keep them in the fray? My favorite. And if you absolutely must kill everything in front of you, we've got a man and a minigun. I say again, the best f2p on steam!

Ah... yes! Team Fortress 2! One of my favorite FPS games out there since I played it on the Xbox 360 version of the Orange Box. Needless to say is that the art style of this game is amazing and appealing. Also the gameplay is well balanced, competitive team play, and a very nice selection of maps. An awesome selection of weapons available as unlocks, drops, purchases, uncrates, and craft for 9 classes. The voice acting of 9 classes, and other characters like The Administrator, Meresmus, and Saxton Hale is always appealing to hear. They also have a crafting and trading system for crafting any duplicates or unwanted items to scrap metal, scraps to reclaimed, and reclaimed to refined, use weapons, tokens, cosmetics, scraps, and others to craft what item you wanted to have. And at the trading system, you can trade for someone or a friend give the items that they don't have or wanted to trade a quality item for how much scraps or weapons.
There's also a very large variety of cosmetics for 9 playable classes that you can wear in-game and change styles or color it with a paint bucket. And crates, crates opens and uncrates a random item when opened with a key purchased from the Mann Co. Store, it has an extremly rare chance to uncrate an unusual cosmetic hat or a taunt. That means an unusual item has a particle effect on the hat or when taunting, and it usually has an high value, depending on the item.

The Mann vs. Machine mode is one of my favorite game modes to play in TF2. Mann vs. Machine mode is an 6-player co-op mode when you have to defend and protect the possesions of Mann Co. from endless waves on lethal robots created by Gray Mann to stop Mann Co. What I like about this game mode is you can pick up the money and use them to buy the upgrades for one of the 9 classes, and at the very end when you complete all waves depending on the difficulty level, you are rewarded for an random item. In some cases, an rare cosmetic or an Australium weapon.
And we have the humor, my goodness! I can't stop laughing at the funny jokes around TF2, especially the fan-made machinimas of TF2. And some community fads like the scout face, nope.avi, spycrab, and Heavy's misheard quote Pootis.
And overall, Team Fortress 2 is a very great FPS game.

These gamemodes can be done with alot of different accesseries. To get these you must play the game and it give them to you randomly or on a special day. Items can be traded to gain higher grade items. When playing you'll see players in fancy clothes, most likely they have pain for these with real money,
There are 9 different classes who all have different roles in battle. The Pyro is used to burn the enemy which will keep damaging the enemy for a time while not being hit. The Engineer makes Turrets/Sentries, Teleporters, Dispensers which aid to aid the team and try and hold an area. The Spy can discuise and turn themselves invisable to try and flank enemy lines to; 'Zap' Sentries, dispensers and/or Teleporters, also to try and 'assassinate' the enemy players. The Heavy weilding a Minigun or sorts, kills well and soaks a good amount of damage but is slow and a big target. The Sniper usally one to camp or 'Spawn Kill', will use his sniper rifle to kill his enemy from a distance, staying in scope will give more damage, if fully charged and a head shot he can kill a heavy in one hit. The Scout is used as a hard to hit target, does he uses a shotgun to get his enemies close range, also can double jump. The Soildier will shoot a rocket launcher of sorts to either kill or 'Rocket Jump'. The Demoman uses grenade launchers to kill his enemies, either laying down a trap or hiting their enemy dirrectly. Also please note there is a sub class of the Demoman called Demo-Knight where the Demoman uses meleweapons and most of the time a sword and shield instead of his grenade launchers, this sub class can only be fully used when owning a pair of shoes, a shield and a meleweapon for the Demoman. The Medic he heals his teammates and doesn't normally just go into combat, he has an ubercharge ability when healing teammates for a certian amount of time.

I love Team Fortress 2.
It's a first person shooter master piece where teamwork is key, instead of in usual FPS's where having one perticular modifaction and set of perks leave all the others at a disadvantage, this game's classes work with a sort of rock, paper, scissors kind of gameplay with other classes being effective against others but over time with practice you will learn to counter act these disadvantages. it also has multiple game modes and maps, both made by the community and the people at valve to keep the game fresh.
The game also rewards you for playing giving you randomised weapon and item drops, which allows you to customize your class to what you wish. However in order to buy special items and a larger inventory to carry more items and weapons you must actually buy an item which turns your copy of the game into a bought copy which allows you to unlock these unique items.
The only real problem is the community which can be filled with you raging or annoying children, players of other FPS games like Call of Duty or Battlefield expecting it to be the same and find out it isn't and start hating the game because it's not how they like it, or just terrible people who insult players who have less experience or who haven't got the bought version of the game. But don't get me wrong there are many who are kind and there to help you get better if you struggle.

First let me preface this by saying this will be an
long review. This is because I have been playing since Beta, and have clocked over 14,000 hours. You can take off a few hundred or so for accidentally leaving the computer on overnight but I assure you they are otherwise legit. I have no life whatsoever. I am not trying to brag by with these, I am just trying to give some perspective.
When TF2 was first announced, and the initial trailer was released, I jumped right on it. I had been playing TFC for years and was a huge fan. From the moment I saw the Minigun muzzle flash, and the hilarious soldier rocket jump sequence, I knew there was something special. Somewhere along the way TF2 has strayed from its roots.
One of my favorite aspects since the beginning, the art style, has now gone to♥♥♥♥♥♥and frankly has been that way for years. What was once a beautiful, unique, purposeful, sophisticated visual style is reduced to random♥♥♥♥♥♥on top of people's heads painted obnoxious colors and gaudy BS rotating around their hats. The color palette used to be neutral and low-saturation. Every visual aspect was simple where it needed to be, complex where it needed to be. These decisions were made for a reason and looked damn good because of it. Seriously why are planets rotating around your head? Are you the sun? People have no taste whatsoever in this game. Bright pink and lime green is an eyesore and yet every dumbass paints 3 of their cosmetic items that to stand out. No one knows anything about complimentary colors or contrast, that's why the damn art department of this game should have stuck to the art direction. Some of the cosmetics are stupid/terrible-looking in and of themselves. The X-Com hair, the Bolgan. They look terrible, they should never have been put in the game. This all brings me to another point:
Item names. Item names & descriptions are often times cringeworthy, made from the same uncreative people who slap together a Frankenstein head, a sweater and flip flops and call it a day. "aimbot.exe" for your Sniper Rifle, wow, real original there! Stupid internet memes like "problem?" or "boom headshot." If you want to have a cringefest, search "tf2 unoriginal item names" w/o quotes on Google and go to the pastebin link, it should be the 5th result. Someone scanned 3 million backpacks and that's the result. These are the people you are playing the game with (if you do play). Speaking of the community:
One of my least favorite aspects of gaming is often times the terrible communities that spawn from it and the gaming community in general. What once was a general positive atmosphere among the game has now been reduced to constant whining about pointless things like class choices. "OMG 3 SNIPERS" is the eternal cry of the TF2 tryhard, who never seem to understand that it's a video game at the end of the day and to let people play what they want. These people believe that a switch is somehow flicked that makes it impossible to win once you exceed x of y class, and it is then necessary to ♥♥♥♥♥ about it. I've seen teams of 3 spies, 3 snipers win, 6 snipers, all spies, you name it. It doesn't matter.
Speaking of the TF2 playerbase, the TF2 playerbase has grown to be a bunch of idiots apparently, because the servers I see populated are terrible 32 player 2fort Instant Respawn servers where the map becomes an even worse stalemate than it already is, and tastelessly over-modded MarioKart servers. In addition, a lot of servers have ads, that not only play when you join, but when you SPAWN. Also there are Pay2Win servers that are actually populated. It boggles my mind.
To sum it up, this game is not what it used to be. It is a bloated, tacky shadow of its former self. The only reason I play it is because I have endless mods to for instance, disable terrible unusual effects, and I turn both voice chat and text chat off. This should not be necessary to enjoy a game. Screw what TF2 has become.

I love Team Fortress 2.
It's a first person shooter master piece where teamwork is key, instead of in usual FPS's where having one perticular modifaction and set of perks leave all the others at a disadvantage, this game's classes work with a sort of rock, paper, scissors kind of gameplay with other classes being effective against others but over time with practice you will learn to counter act these disadvantages. it also has multiple game modes and maps, both made by the community and the people at valve to keep the game fresh.
The game also rewards you for playing giving you randomised weapon and item drops, which allows you to customize your class to what you wish. However in order to buy special items and a larger inventory to carry more items and weapons you must actually buy an item which turns your copy of the game into a bought copy which allows you to unlock these unique items.
The only real problem is the community which can be filled with you raging or annoying children, players of other FPS games like Call of Duty or Battlefield expecting it to be the same and find out it isn't and start hating the game because it's not how they like it, or just terrible people who insult players who have less experience or who haven't got the bought version of the game. These hours are legit, I played this game a lot in the past to avoid some tragic stuff in real life. I was young and didn't really have my gaming consoles anymore because of my brothers and I had a really bad pc, which i still own. TF2 was one of the games i could play pretty well on this pc but with horrid graphics, but it was one of the more fun games I installed. I met some real cool and nice people on this game as well as people who i plan to keep by my side. The community back then was more humble compared to nowadays. You have competitive gamers who spam their bind keys with unfunny/gross jokes and very obnoxious people who are either yelling at you or telling you to do specific things to win the game. When really, it doesn't even matter if you win or lose.  However, you also have those people who are really awesome and you may meet some nice friends along the way! Although you never know what kinda person you're going to meet on this game. In my honest opinion, if you want to have a game to just waste time on (and money) or just mess around with people you know (which is what I do now), this is perfect. Esspecially the mann vs. machine co-op. I mainly play that now. Although to me, the game lost its touch, update wise, and I moved onto other games.
I believe it's worth a shot to try it out but other than that, I'd keep it as a casual game. I don't think the competitive scene is worth getting into anymore because it's being flooded by crude people. Atleast from my experiance after over about 4+ years of playing it just got worse and worse. You will eventually be tied into drama even if you try to avoid it. You'll be more stressed than actually having fun, I'll tell you that!
Although in all seriousness, this game is losing its touch and probably isn't worth making it your main game MAINLY because the updates they've been releasing are becoming very dull and not as great as they used to be. BUT, it's a great game to just play to pass the time and have fun! All you'll really notice nowdays is...people really love to trade more than actually play. Living off as a free to play would be very tough and you'd need to be patient with items you would want, unless you got that MONEY! Hope this helps.
One last thing, I am not saying this game is bad in any way. I am saying that it's worth trying and playing with friends, or even meeting people! Although there are some downsides that you won't like, such as some stuff I pointed out above. Strictly towards the community. I personally think you should have this game as a side game rather than your come home to play sorta thing. Have it as a once in a while game, because it's nothing to be big about, unless you really do not like most of the millions of other games out there.
Just give it a shot and see what you think! Have fun <3

A lot of hours, a lot of time. God forbid that my life becomes anymore than this game. TF2 is a fun, action-packed multiplayer only FPS. It was made F2P a couple of years back, and it started a grand war about whether or not it was worth it. This is my honest review, and I will only state matters that are important to me. Beware, for this will be a long revies.
First of all: people who are free to play. There are many different people in TF2, and F2P is a common one. This people have not bought anything in the game, whether key, hat, or weapons. These people usually fall under 3 categories: complete noob, 10 yr. old kid/someothershooterplayer, and actually skilled player. The noobs are people who have just started and don't quite know how to play. It is better to educate them than to berate them, since they could become very skilled players and P2P. Do not insult someone for not knowing how the games work unless the refuse the listen, and most of the time I found many noobs willing to listen so they can get better at the game. The second type, kids and othershooter noobs, tend to not know anything... at all. After playing Halo a long time, I decided to see what else was on the shooter market. When I heard about this great game, I decided to try it. I realized very quickly how different it was from other shooters I had played, both in gameplay and in graphics. So, for TF2, I had to adjust, and it has been hard and long but I feel used to it now. Other othershooternoobs, however, are not like me. Often referred to as COD kids, these guys expect this game to be like the others. Big mistake. It's better to kill and troll them out of existence than to talk to or put up with them. As for the 10 yr. olds, well, that goes without saying. There are skilled F2P players out there, allbeit very uncommon. These guys dominate the enemy team while wearing their gibus and are accused of hacking. If you see a gibus dominating people left and right, that probably means their good at the game, instead of being a hat-hoarding moron (pardon my French). It takes dedication and skill to learn the ins and outs, and these people have done it.
Next are P2P, which, in my opinion, are actually worst than most F2P. They usually are under these categories: silent and deadly, hat-hoarder, and friendly. Silent ones I have found to be the most deadly, as they kill people, but never utter a word, nor type a text in chat. Their there to play, and do no more. A sub-group of them, called try-hards, can't deal with people who want to conga or be friendly instead of capture a point. These people need to calm down, because its the player's choice to conga or to kill. Then there are the hat-hoarders. This guys have got unusuals and stranges like there is no tommorow, They think anyone who doesn't have a strange or unusual sucks, and often accuse people of hacking or using noob weps and combos when they are dominated. I dominated one of these people on a server, and I just kept killing them with the degreaser-flare-axtinguisher combo (pyro is the class I'm best at #airblastftw). So, they pay for god-mode (usually a fair amount of money/metal), but then I do !friendly so I can't be hurt. I think he may have had a anuerism or heart attack. I was promptly kicked off the server after trolling him more with the fortified compound's taunt (which I didn't know I wasn't suppose to do lol). This people need to worry less about appearance and more about skill. Lastly, we have friendlies. They tend to not ne that good at the game, so they decide to just conga or spy-crab around. If you see a friendly, please don't kill them. Their just being friendly. To learn more signs of friendlies, go look up a guide on them in the community discussions.
Next, trading. Trading has become part of TF2, but is not necesarry despite what some people think. Most people could care less about Australium-unusual-strange-prokillstreak Black Box. If people want an item, most are buyable, and the achievement ones do not really matter since they are mostly reskins. For those interested in actually joining the manneconomy, you should buy some keys from the Mann Co. Store first, and start unboxing crates. Get some unusuals, see what their worth, then see if you can make a profit. If you can't, well, that unusual is yours until you decide to sell it. Most of time you can just wait for the prices to go up so you can make a profit. If you want achievement items, it is most of the time easier just to get the game its from than to get it from trade or crafting. If you think the Awper hand is cool, then go get CS:GO and get the achievement for it in that game. Want the sharp dresser? Go get Assassin's Creed (I can't remember which one though). It saves a lot of time and hassle.
Finally, we get to the important part: gameplay. Valve has worked for a long time to get TF2 where it is, and people still complain. "OMG degreaser combos are so OP and this game should nerf it!" Really man? I have beaten combo pyros with scout. I've beat demoknights with pyro. I have beaten rocket jumper soldiers as sniper. I have destroyed an engi nest once with me, as a medic, with another medic. I have capped the point with engi with the help of my minisentries. I have ran the intelligence as heavy. I have defended the point as demo and spy. You have to learn how to get around the noobs and the OP loadout users. Dead ringer spycicle spy? No problem for this pyro. Engi nest? Bonk's away! MLG sniper? Fists of steel shall protect me. While I do admit some weapons are useless, like the Dalokah's Bar and Vitasaw, some of the weapons people call useless, like the Air Strike, Wrap Assassin, Big Earner, etc. are actually really useful. While I can't do much as Big Earner spy, probably from the fact I stink as a spy (#deadringerforever), I have made progress with the Wrap Assassin and the Air Strike, while a little gimmicky, takes full advantage of the BASE Jumper.
In the end, is TF2 worth playing? Well, it depends on why you're playing. Interested in taking over the manneconomy? Go buy some keys and get those buds! Want to kill people while looking awesome? Go buy/trade for a cosmetic and hat. Want to become a pro player? Train, find a mge server, train some more, and look for a pro match or tournament online. TF2 is a lot of things, and the second you step in, YOU decide who you want to be. That is what really matters. The rest is up to you.

A first-person shooter game (mainly), orginated as a bunch of merchants killing other for unknown reasons, but since then has been transformed into a game with a huge community following. The game used to sell for quite a bit of money until Valve (producing company, etc) decided that making TF2 free to play (f2p) might attract more following. Which it did, and the main pay in the game now is an in-game store with weapons, taunts, cosmetics (mostly hats), and so on.
I would recommend this game, however just as a warning, it gets a little addicting! Even if you don't think you'd like a first-person shooter type of game, there are so many little specifics to the game that you might become interested in just the community. Like... why does the spy date scout's mom, and the scout doesn't do anything about it? Or, why is aulstralium (a futuristic element that for some reason makes anyone who is in contact with it for a period of time extremely strong and "intelligent") a thing? Or prehapts, why does this game even have such a big following?!
You can begin to join the 'underlying' community by most simply going onto your favorite newly posted video site, and type in TF2 "Meet the..." animations, and (of course) most the other recommended video responses.  Hopefully, if you are willing to take both this review and the game seriously, you will give Team Fortress 2 a shot. Or atleast mention it to someone...

Just amazing. This is the best FPS game that is currently "active" (as in not outdated, too old or unobtainable) IMO. I hear lots of complaints about how thing were "better before" and such, but...I don't really see it.
"Hat Simulator 2014" both is and isn't a good name for this game. The gameplay has nothing to do with hats and if you're smart you shouldn't give a single f*** about if your teammates/opponents wear hats or not. Unfortunately this is harder than it seems (sometimes you get the urge to get a hat just so you feel more pro and get noticed. I usually shrug off that feeling but it still comes up often). Don't get me wrong: i have a couple of hats myself and I appreciate them.
As for money: BE WARNED! This game WILL make you spend money on it if you're actively gonna play this (and thus get addicted). While the 0,75$ is a hilariously cheap price for Premium Membership, I've bought a few Crate Keys as wel as Tour of Duty Tickets (things you can ONLY get via buying with cash). However here's a tip: NEVER buy hats or weps.
Anyway back to the gameplay. It's very fluid, smooth and there are no such things as "Quickscopers" or random grenades. Sure there are some pro snipers who can headshot you insanely fast but they're pretty rare on normal servers. Classes are well balanced iMO. Sometimes people will complain about a class being OP (Scout, Soldier and Demo come to mind) but just shrug it off. It mostly depends on skill (that doesn't maen the game's 100% fair and EVERYTHING is perfectly balanced).

A first-person shooter game (mainly), orginated as a bunch of merchants killing other for unknown reasons, but since then has been transformed into a game with a huge community following. The game used to sell for quite a bit of money until Valve (producing company, etc) decided that making TF2 free to play (f2p) might attract more following. Which it did, and the main pay in the game now is an in-game store with weapons, taunts, cosmetics (mostly hats), and so on.
I would recommend this game, however just as a warning, it gets a little addicting! Even if you don't think you'd like a first-person shooter type of game, there are so many little specifics to the game that you might become interested in just the community. Like... why does the spy date scout's mom, and the scout doesn't do anything about it? Or, why is aulstralium (a futuristic element that for some reason makes anyone who is in contact with it for a period of time extremely strong and "intelligent") a thing? Or prehapts, why does this game even have such a big following?!
You can begin to join the 'underlying' community by most simply going onto your favorite newly posted video site, and type in TF2 "Meet the..." animations, and (of course) most the other recommended video responses.  Hopefully, if you are willing to take both this review and the game seriously, you will give Team Fortress 2 a shot. Or atleast mention it to someone...
...I don't think you'll regret it... or atleast I hope not. :)

Team Fortress 2, lovingly referred to as "Hat Fortress 2", is the definitive MMOFPS. If you don't know about it, you must have been living under a rock AND a hard place at the same time. I have a hard time writing reviews about games that mean something to me. It's not too complicated that you can't learn it in a few hours, but it isn't self-explanatory either. All in all, TF2 is probably my all-time favorite Steam game in existence. The community is also amazing and very active in the game. Valve themselves takes some of the top-rated Workshop items and adds them in occasionally. It isn't played like the traditional FPS, however. Most FPS games put you in the role of "Expendable Scrub #2258," but in TF2, you take the role of one of NINE Expendable Scrubs! Each one drastically different from the last. From the fleet-footed Scout, to the walking Russian tank, the Heavy, to the Not-a-Nazi mad German doctor, the Medic, to the♥♥♥♥♥♥lobbing Sniper. Your years of CoD and Halo won't help you here, friend. I gladly give this game a 10/10. A massively enjoyable experience for the most hardcore and adaptable FPS players out there! But wait, I'm not done yet! It... has hats. Yeah, that's right. HATS! Possibly the greatest addition to a game ever, and until you have one, you will NEVER understand! And with that, I give it a final score of 10/10, and a personal score of 11/10 because hats push it one step further.

TF2 has received some serious love, there's heaps of new maps and weapons that has been added since release, but even though the game has past its prime, the core gameplay remains the same. It's still an amazing multiplayer FPS that puts the yearly-released-FPS crowd to shame.

Team Fortress 2 is the most realistic hat simulator created to date. There is absolutely no other simulator quite like this one. The first time you start the simulator, you join a server where you can play a minigame where you show off your hats and items. If you kill a person three times in a row in the minigame, you get your very first hat: the Gibus. I, I am a soldier. I don't know what my name is. All I know, is that Mann Co has taken me in and raised me to fight for them. They told me that my parents are dead and that the town I was born in was destroyed a long time ago. Their training has born fruit, as I ended a substantial amount of lives in the past three decades.
Currently, I am stationed in Badwater which has been under siege by the BLU, our sworn enemies, for a week now. Civilian unrest is rising, and riots are imminent. While I understand their concerns and anger, we must still win this war, so we are forced to quell them by any means necessary, whether it'd be peaceful or violent. Morale is at an all time low. This whole battle has gone to♥♥♥♥♥♥ Our sergeant still has his hopes up, though, and we are ordered to follow our superiors to hell and back on their command.
But I feel peaceful, like I'm in an empty field where you don't hear gunfire and explosions, but the chirping birds and the trees in the wind. Wait, there's someone over there, I should go and...
"Wake up, you useless MAGGOT!"
I fell out of my bunk bed, but still had the (will)power to address him (thank god). SIR, YES SIR!
I got up (by myself, of course. Sgt. Morris would've laughed his♥♥♥♥♥off if I asked for help, but not in the good fun way, if you know what I mean). I packed my gear and went outside to scout the area and see what the rioters and BLU are planning.
And then, a loud bang was heard. I immediatly jumped to cover, and after a few seconds of hiding, I looked back at the base. It has been entirely demolished. I ran back (although while under cover) and saw that everyone had perished due to either the blast, the rubble or the fire. I hear a faint call for help, and I rushed there to see Sergeant Morris, legs blown off, covered in blood and rubble, and ran to him.
"Soldier", he said. "Please, Soldier... run! Get out of this war! Make sure you can start over! The war hasn't... been... lost". He died immediatly after he spoke his final words. Start over, he said. But... I have nowhere to go. What the hell do I need to do now? I tried to think, but I was thrown out of thought by a blue blur. Is that.... An engineer? What is he doing on the battlefield? I ran after him while firing rockets at the scouts trying to stop me. I almost had him, but I was hit by a tranquilizing dart. I fell on the ground, barely concsious, and a BLU sniper stood next to me. A few of their Heavies held me up. "Good night, ♥♥♥♥♥♥" was the last thing I heard before he knocked me unconcsious.
"Ja, zis patient is ze optimal test subject!" I opened my eyes and tried to get up, but my limbs were bound to a table. "Easy zere, schweinhund. Zere's nowhere you can go". A medic looked at me with an unnerving grin and pulled a syringe out of a box. "You feelthy REDs have opposed us for long enough, you know zat? We always had ze optimal ideas for zis welt, you know? But you dreckschweinhunde always tried to stop us! Do you know how MAD zat makes me?" I tried to reply, but I didn't know what to say. "Zis medicine right here, will cure you from ze programming the REDs have knocked into you. How does zat sound? A free life in a welt run by ze BLUs would be in your best eenterests, nein? Eef not, take zis!" He stabbed me with the needle, but I didn't feel brainwashed, I felt stronger. "SHEIßE! Zat was the wrong syringe! Zose were my experimental steroids!" I ripped the binds off, and punched the medic in the face, which threw him against the wall. "Wait, nein! no! Please, don't hurt me!" I grabbed him and snapped his neck. "hil...fe" were his final words, as he fell on the ground lifelessly.
An alarm went off, and shortly after, soldiers were already swarming the room. "Hands up, maggot!" one of them screamed. I saw a teleported labeled as "?". I ran for it while they shot at me, and strangely enough, my body reflected the bullets without any pain. One of them jumped in my way, but I knocked him over effortlessly. I jumped in the teleporter, and it teleported me right before it broke down. I saw nothing but light as I floated down, and then I hit the ground.
I woke up, but I felt very different. I raised my palm in front of my face. The first thing I noticed, is that my arm has a strong brown tan, not unlike our Demomen. I was white all of my life, so how could this happen? The next thing I noticed is that I was... female? Due to my upbringing, I barely saw any women at all, let alone with my own eyes. But yet I knew that I switched genders. I got up, and I hear a faint voice behind me. "Fareeha?"
It sounded very german, so I thought it was the medic. I raised my differently looking rocket launcher at the figure. "Wait, what are you doing? It's me! Angela!". Suddenly, I saw her more clearly. She was a slim figure with white clothes, technological wings, blonde hair and she had golden halo-like headwear. When I saw her, the memories of my previous life faded, and were filled with new ones. I felt like I actually was this "Fareeha". "You were unconscious for about an hour! What happened?" I replied with that I was knocked out of the sky by a brownish figure with flamboyant blond but burned hair, what was his name, Trashmouse or something? "It's okay, love. we're still together", Angela replied. Love, I thought? Suddenly, the questions I had were replaced by the romantic feelings I had for her. Before I could reply, a serious looking old man came in the med ward. "What are you jokers doing now? Stop wasting time!" Another old man in a knight outfit entered the room as well, and replied with "Let them be, Morrison! You know how ze so called sky lesbians can be when zey're alone!"
"Morrison". That name reminds me of my old sergeant, but I know this man way better. He is Jack Morrison. And it all became clear now. The teleporter teleported me from the second realm of Team Fortress to the land of... Overwatch? I used to be a soldier, and the teleporter turned me into Pharah. Yes, I know who I am now. I feel way happier knowing these people and fighting for them instead of Mann Co and its corrupt leaders. I am still a soldier, but under a different, better banner. I just hope that my mom Ana doesn't find out about my relationship ;)
The End.

TL;DR: We don't need drill sargents on a casual game
Salty and toxic (Yes, I'm going to use that term) players started invading this game recently, and I'm not talking about F2Ps. It's the competitive 'scene' where everything has to work, everything has to follow their own little rule book, everything has to be over in 5 minutes or less. It's fine in CS:GO, where angry russians are the least of the worries or Overwatch; both of which were built for competitive play. In TF2? Doesn't work. 'Professionals' need to use a heavily limited selection of weapons, routes and graphics settings which just limit what the game could be. Unfortunately Valve is complying to these people, or seem to at least which means I might end up quitting along with a lot of other people who just want a game; you know that thing you play for fun?
I'm still upvoting because its an excellent game, though I'm not happy with the current player base. The majority are good, the rest just incite hot-headed and voice/chat warrior behavior, which ruins it for everybody else.
Game wise it needs some tlc, Source 2 is a future idea for this which is great (All products ultimately want to see Source 2 ~ Valve interview 2017), and that can bring many more updates, features and maybe a proper competitive gamemode without the need of drill sargents. Until then the experience is bittersweet.

At first this game may just seem like a not serious, cartoony mess. But if you actually download and play it for a while, youll start to realize how much there is to this game. TF2 really isnt like any other fps you find out there. May it be Battlefield, Call of Duty or Counterstrike. There are 9 different classes to choose from here (Scout, Soldier, Pyro, Demoman, Heavy, Engineer, Medic, Sniper and Spy), each one with completely different weapons and playstyles. Yes, even W+M1 is a playstyle (youll start to figure out this part if you play the game).
The Scout has high mobility due to his runspeed of 133% and ability of doing doublejumps, can dish out high damage really quickly (if played correctly) but doesnt have a lot of health. The Spy can disguise as enemy players and get a one-hit-kill with his backstab if they arent paying attention (or the pings of the other players are in their favour). His revolver is very powerful if aimed right and works just fine if you missed your backstab. The engineer can build 3 different buildings: The sentry gun, which is a very strong aimbot turret; the dispenser which gives health and ammunition to teammates, and the teleporter which, as you could imagine, teleports teammates from one place to another. His biggest concerns are spies (who can sap his buildings), demomen (who can blow up his buildings), and medics (who can charge the so called "über", that gives 10 seconds of invulnerability to him and whoever he's healing). But if your teammates are helping you and you can aim somewhat well, these classes wont be to much of a problem.
The last point is about the f2p-model and the leveling. In Tf2, every single weapon has a downside and an upside (actually: there are a few weapons which dont have any stats and there are some weapons which have one minor upside). There arent any direct upgrades to weapons, like in call of duty (or 65% of all first person shooters for that matter). The only bonus that a player who has played longer than a beginner have is experience. So there arent any "booster packs" for real money or stuff like that. "Well then how does valve make money with this game????" you might ask. Yeah, there are crates that contain cosmetics.
One key to open one crate is around 2,50. sometimes more i suppose. And that is how valve makes money off of the players. So, after this freaking long review, you better download Team Fortress 2 right now... or ill be using minisentries.

+ You get 9 choices of hat modelers from different ethnicities. (The Russian and German models are probably the worst models, because they don’t wear a default hat)
+ You get a lot of different locational maps to model you hat in. (Best with western hat modeling)
+ You can team up with others in what I assume are competitive hat modeling competitions, like Capture the Hat, Control Hat, king of the Hat, Mann vs. Hatted Robots, Hatload, and Hatted Delivery.
+ Super cheap hats in the games hat store. $12.99 for a “Bubble Pipe Hat” What a steal! (I think they should increase these prices, or they might run out items. I already bought this item 26 times in case they ever do run out of hats)
Some things I did not like about the simulator.
- You get these weird metal hats drops called “weapons”, which you can’t even wear on your head! They only go in your hands! I didn't think I would be so addicted to this game! I love it! It has made me realize that I have sold my soul to Valve, seeing as how I have been playing Team Fortress 2 on the daily almost every day from the moment I wake up to before I sleep at night. The co-ops are fun and the server settings are awesome! The quality of the weaponry is amazing. If I could stick with one game I could play for the rest of my life, this would be it.
The only thing I could make do without it, would be the players that happen to make rude and racial slurs along with the loud, obnoxious pre-teens and children who happen to mic spam on some occasions. But overall, it's a highly enjoyable game that is free to play and great for fast-paced loving gamers looking for first-person shooters. The one thing you need to remember, though, you aren't playing by yourself but with other gamers around the world with different strengths and weaknesses, where you gotta learn to work together. Hence, the word "TEAM" in the title. Team work makes the dream work, as they say.
P.S. Conga is the best thing to see in a server. EVER! xD

The one thing you need to remember, though, you aren't playing by yourself but with other gamers around the world with different strengths and weaknesses, where you gotta learn to work together. Where do I begin. Being someone who came from a game like Battlefield, a game I ended up getting great at. This was a totally new playing field for me. I was used to like 4 classes, their are 9 in this game. All with their own strengths, weaknesses, and amazingly well written personalities. This game very quickly became the most fun I've had in a virtual world. Even if you don't win you're gonna have fun, because honestly what other game has american vets shooting rockets at their feet and landing on people's faces while at the same time smacking them with a frying pan!? It's highly entertaining!
Pros-
All the classes are useful, and highly situational
A fun loving community, that is all about goofing off
Hats to give your classes a hint of your own personality and taste
Several weapons that take time to learn how to use correctly
Each class has an entertaining personality, and something funny to say
While this game is goofy as can be, it can be highly intense
Graphics that are very art inspired, thus making them fun to look at
Multiple gamemodes so that the fun never stops
It never gets repetitive, something new will happen everytime you jump into a match
A great soundtrack
A very cool secret agent kind of feel, this game takes place in 1972, but has technology that we don't even have to this day, which makes for a really sci-fi-ish feel.
Cons-
Occasional bugs, but every game has these
Some community members can be very hateful, like telling free to plays that they are worthless, or telling members of fandom groups that they need to kill themselves, however you can't find any perfect community
Two cons? That's it yeah. I honestly can't find anything else negative to say. I got this game way back in January 31st, 2014. I had always wanted it since 2010 but wasn't able to get myself a computer (Mac OSX Air) once I did I played the crap out of this game, and I still play it an insane amount of time, I wanna be a writer, but everytime I get on here to write something I end up starting up Team Fortress 2. Regardless I'll write my book at some point. In closing, thanks to Law Abiding Engineer for giving me tips back when I had only 10 hours logged. GG Valve, your games are legendary.

Where do I begin. Being someone who came from a game like Battlefield, a game I ended up getting great at. This was a totally new playing field for me. I was used to like 4 classes, their are 9 in this game. All with their own strengths, weaknesses, and amazingly well written personalities. This game very quickly became the most fun I've had in a virtual world. Even if you don't win you're gonna have fun, because honestly what other game has american vets shooting rockets at their feet and landing on people's faces while at the same time smacking them with a frying pan!? It's highly entertaining!
Pros-
All the classes are useful, and highly situational
A fun loving community, that is all about goofing off
Hats to give your classes a hint of your own personality and taste
Several weapons that take time to learn how to use correctly
Each class has an entertaining personality, and something funny to say
While this game is goofy as can be, it can be highly intense
Graphics that are very art inspired, thus making them fun to look at
Multiple gamemodes so that the fun never stops
It never gets repetitive, something new will happen everytime you jump into a match
A great soundtrack
A very cool secret agent kind of feel, this game takes place in 1972, but has technology that we don't even have to this day, which makes for a really sci-fi-ish feel.
Cons-
Occasional bugs, but every game has these
Some community members can be very hateful, like telling free to plays that they are worthless, or telling members of fandom groups that they need to kill themselves, however you can't find any perfect community
Two cons? That's it yeah. I honestly can't find anything else negative to say. I got this game way back in January 31st, 2014. I had always wanted it since 2010 but wasn't able to get myself a computer (Mac OSX Air) once I did I played the crap out of this game, and I still play it an insane amount of time, I wanna be a writer, but everytime I get on here to write something I end up starting up Team Fortress 2. Regardless I'll write my book at some point. In closing, thanks to Law Abiding Engineer for giving me tips back when I had only 10 hours logged. GG Valve, your games are legendary.

Team Fortress 2 is one of very few free-to-play games left that does not incorporate the "pay-to-win" concept. I personally recommend this game because I've come to enjoy (most of) the TF2 community as well as the overall ridiculous atmosphere of gameplay. I honestly do not think you can get the full experience of this game staying on just a free-to-play account, despite you still being able to have a fun time at that. Being that a premium upgrade is a one time payment and can cost as little as $0.50 it is certainly worth the money. It allows access to a plethora of new items via trading which can become somewhat addicting. The weapons/equipment that are more easily obtainable through premium does not grant any leverage in game, each weapon besides the defaults have both positive and negative attributes that may be balanced in accordance to the player's preferred playing style. There is a heavy emphasis on player responsibility that, if you are the competitive type, may require you to play as classes you are not accustomed to in order to more effectively contribute to your team and have more favorable odds at winning. Even then this may not always be the case as it may not always be you that needs to be "carrying their weight." The game is easy to run with most modern computers and was the first game I had on Steam. Long story short if you're looking for a decent fast-paced, team-oriented first-person shooter that is *free* you will be hard pressed to find something more fitting than Team Fortress 2.

text: I may not be one of those guys whose into those Xbox shooting games such as, Call of Duty, Modern Warfare, Halo, etc. But TF2 is an awesome game that has extended the variety to what many of those other games provide. It has shown itself than more than just a killing game, it is a game that has humor, style, colorful characters and more. With nine main characters total (three offensive, three defensive and three supportive), there is a lot of variety and different ways of playing and stratigizing. All nine characters are unique in their very own way and they each have potential in mastering the field in their own way. It's proven that someone in any class can be the pure dominator of the game; but it takes a lot of speed, skill, and experience to get to that point. If TF2 is known for one thing, it would definatly be for its fair gameplay. In TF2, anythings possible. Even people who are pure newbies and have never heard of TF2 could possibly become potenial underdogs on the battlefield. Players have a lot of variety, not with just the characters they choose to play as, but with the weapons and cosmetics they choose for the characters. It's unlockable by achievement, buying them, or by a random drop rate. There's many ways to be good at TF2, so if you are new to playing battle games, this would be a great game for you. And if you're someone who loves fighting battle games with a sense of humor, I would deeply suggest this game.

Very fun team v.s. team game with multiple character classes that all have unique aspects to one another. Some being fast with several jumps, some being slow with gigantic miniguns. There are many gamemodes, one in particular that is often played the most; capture the flag. We all know what capture the flag is, both teams have a designated item that the other team must retrieve back to their base in order to gain a score. Different gamemodes have one team defend a bomb being rolled to the destruction point, the other team attempting to do so. There are quite a few more gamemodes, but I'm not going to go into detail about them, as I try to keep my reviews short and simple. Then there are servers. Servers can be hosted by different people and or companies, having seperate servers for assorted gamemodes. Some servers are specifically designed for trading Team Fortress 2 exclusive items, such as cosmetic items or weapons. Of course there are normal servers for the game's default gamemodes, but there are also custom gamemodes. For example, Versus Saxton Hale (Or Freak Fortress 2) has one team of however many people fighting against one person on the other team. The catch is, the lone player has a very large amount of health points, often reaching into the thousands. There's a ton of stuff to do in Team  Fortress 2. Having over one thousand hours in this game, I can say it can definitely get boring at times, but with Valve continually updating and the community constantly throwing out new gamemodes and custom mods for the game, you will always be able to enjoy playing.

Team Fortress 2 is quite unique in that the strategies diverge from most 1st person shooters. Instead of being solely about outgunning the opponent team, it introduces a need for communication between teammates and a heavy emphasis on location. No minimap is available, and the only clue you have about your team's status is a kill feed and a list of live players. In addition, each of the classes outputs a high amount of damage relative to all the classes' max health, even the Heavy's health. This further emphasizes the need for strategizing and location, and not simply holding down M1 the entire time. The amount of equipment customization and need for adapting both individually and as a team set this game apart from many others of its genre. Anyone who enjoys an offbeat RTS/FPS hybrid should thoroughly enjoy TF2.
