TL;DR You'd be surprised how good your game can be if you have more than 10 people working on it and actually listen to your playerbase, Valve. And stop trying to be like Overwatch. You're not Overwatch and that's okay. The more you try to be the more you alienate people.
If the question is "Would you recommend it?" my answer is "No." But it is more complicated than that.
If you've never played this before and don't have a friend to guide you or play with you, don't even bother. The game has a steep learning curve and makes no effort to teach you any of it. I have 1,000 hours plus 200 hours on my old Steam account, I played this game since 2010, and I JUST found out you can hold down left click to charge sticky bombs to throw them further. As a demo main. That's the levels of not bothering to teach we're talking about.
The development cycle is long and drawn out and it's clear the developers barely listen to the players. Weapon rebalances make no sense, take ages to come out, and make clear that they don't even play their own game. But don't worry, you have cosmetic cases and TIERED HATS! Because who doesn't love artificially inflated marketplace prices, am I right??? The community finds bugs VERY often, report them and make videos on them and Valve takes AGES to fix them, and even when they do often times people will easily find ways to replicate them again. This is the reason channels like Delfy are as successful as they are.
50,000 people. That's what SteamCharts insists the playerbase number is daily. Where ARE these 50,000 people? There are a small handful of community servers (with mostly the same people on them), but that's barely even 200 people. Quickplay/casual queues? Nope, queue times take ages and barely anybody plays maps that aren't 2CP and Payload. Competitive? PFFFT, NOBODY in this game is playing competitive. Because it sucks. But more on that later. MvM? Queues take about as much time as they used to. Which is a while.
The update everybody was hyped for. It released in 2016 (and it took them a year to release any rebalances, but they didn't even release rebalances, no, they released a list of IDEAS for rebalances. And not even the full list. HALF of it.) and has been there since then. So how is it? In my opinion, it f*cking killed this game, or got the closest to doing it. Quickplay/Casual queue replaced the super convenient Valve pub servers and it sucks. Bad. You have very little choice in terms of gamemodes because, again, barely anybody plays anything that isn't 2CP and Payload, and queues take ages. You can't even pick the map you want to play on. Well, you can, but expect an insanely long queue time when you do so. When you do get in, you will notice there is no team switching, there is no team scramble, and there is no AUTOBALANCE. Before any of you go "autobalance is cancer, huhuhuhuh", that's a f*cking meme and if you don't see why it was necessary then you're one of the reasons things are as they are now. Because now, if teams are unbalanced, they will stay that way. Sure, the winning team gets a "teams are unbalanced, wanna volunteer to switch?" prompt, but nobody will ever accept that. And that's also the only way to play against your friends in Quickplay. You can't even switch manually anymore. Hey, Valve, just because Overwatch does something one way doesn't mean it's automatically GOOD. I want to be able to play against my friends super easily in Overwatch too. But I can see why they can't do that. Because it's a 6v6 super fast paced game where team switching in the middle of a game wouldn't make sense. But they have a custom game maker just for that. And something like "put us on separate teams" would be a neat addition to the game.
Speaking of game maker, the quickplay/casual match queue is ripped straight out of the MvM mode with no changes made to it, and all the issues from before still staying there. You can't even do simple things like leave a match WITH your party, you have to reinvite them all over again. And what the F*CK is the point of tracking my casual match level if you're not gonna use it to pair me with people of similar levels? You know, like Overwatch.
This is what I'd argue MyM's main issue is. It tries TOO MUCH to be like Overwatch in places it shouldn't. In places it SHOULD, it doesn't. And that brings me to:
Let me put it simply: competitive mode in this game is garbage. It's pointless. It's years worth of hype for a new pet just to be presented with a blind rat who has turboAIDS. There are no placements. Barely anybody plays it because it sucks. Ranks don't matter, you'll still be paired up with and against new players and/or veterans no matter what skill rank you're at. And the format is 6s. So a 6v6 with no class locks, no weapon bans, nothing. And the game is still balanced around casual, which is a 9v9 or 12v12 format.
Gone are the days where even if I primarily play other games I'd still want to pop into a quick Valve pub to have some with my friends. I lost hope in Valve trying to salvage this game. Not because TF2 is unsalvageable. Because Valve doesn't give a sh*t anymore.
This game's hardcore fanbase is in denial. They refuse to see faults with this game and continue to insist that everybody who doesn't want to play it or stopped playing it is just not good enough or is too stupid to do so. They will also turn any criticism of this game into an insult towards Overwatch and its fanbase.  This ranges from people like UncleDane (as much as I like him, this statement is f*cking dumb) saying "TF2 is better and people only play Overwatch because it's new." to when FUNKe points out TF2's problematic learning curve, people in the comments going "So the argument is that Overwatch is for babies."
People who never played either game choose Overwatch over TF2 because Overwatch is easier to get into and play. Not because "hURRR DURR IT'S NEW AND THEY'RE BLIZZCUCKS". And yeah, veterans moving to Overwatch are playing Overwatch because it's new. Because TF2 fails to offer something new and refreshing while still fixing the broken sh*t that already exists. When's the last time we had new weapons? End of the Line (that was also a f*cking trainwreck)? I don't even remember anymore. And no, TF2 needing multitudes of outside sources and at least 20 hours of playtime to start understanding the basics of the game, is NOT a good thing.

text: I may not be one of those guys whose into those Xbox shooting games such as, Call of Duty, Modern Warfare, Halo, etc. But TF2 is an awesome game that has extended the variety to what many of those other games provide. It has shown itself than more than just a killing game, it is a game that has humor, style, colorful characters and more. With nine main characters total (three offensive, three defensive and three supportive), there is a lot of variety and different ways of playing and stratigizing. All nine characters are unique in their very own way and they each have potential in mastering the field in their own way. It's proven that someone in any class can be the pure dominator of the game; but it takes a lot of speed, skill, and experience to get to that point. If TF2 is known for one thing, it would definatly be for its fair gameplay. In TF2, anythings possible. And if you're someone who loves fighting battle games with a sense of humor, I would deeply suggest this game.

Team Fortress 2, though I am not fond of MOST FPS, this is one that stands out and tries to be different. Hats, miscs, halloween and other seasonal events, custom and normal game modes, and an overall nice soundtrack?
1. Story **SLIGHT SPOILERS***
The story is too long to summarize, so let me simplify it even more. Two brothers fought for gravel and their long lost third brother kills them both and makes robots to destroy Mann Co. THE END
2. Mechanics
The game has 9 different classes from you to choose from, The Scout, who is fast on his feet but can take a bit of a beating; The Soldier, who has an arsenal of rocket launchers and boots; The Pyro, a crazed and weird pyrotecknic; The Demoman, a scottish drunkie who can litearlly put your remaining body parts in a soup can; The Heavy, a popular meme with his POOTIS; The Engineer, what Texans would find a little bit racist; The Medic, a German who is bound can turn almost anyone in to a god in a short amount of time; The Sniper, not a crazed gunman, but a leathel assassin, next to DeadShot; and The Spy, a Frenchmanwho really like the Scout's mother. Anyway, At first, TF2 was supposed to be a command and attack game, which ended up being too stoopid for us, they decided to make is alot like the orignal Team Fortress, a class-based FPS. Containing game modes such as Capture the *cough* breifcase *cough* flag, Control Point, and the completly forgotten Territorial Control Points, (A.K.A. tc_hydro. Yea, remember that? I sure DON'T!) and the new and enjoyable, Mann vs. Machine.
3. Graphics
The game, at first, was trying to look like, at the time, a realistic command and attack game, then the graphics started to look a little more... cartoon-y, which ended up getting ALOT of people on TF2's purchase list, along with all the famous "Meet the Team" Videos, while at the same time, making the game more mature for the older audiences.
Overall, Team Fortress 2 is a great shooter for the person who is trying to look for a good FPS, with out having to be called a F2P all the time.

The short version is that this game is pretty good for what it is. You should get it and see if you get hooked and if you want to play more further, but as for me, i did get hooked and back in the day played it atleast 5 times a week,but unfortunately my ''hype'' has died off. I play this game SOMETIMES, but pretty much rarely, since Valve removed the good old pubs. Pubs were just these servers you could tune into through the game's server browser, but now they are gone. And there's no Quickplay. It used to be almost as easy as joining a valve server in the server browser. But what does that change? The game is still working. Well, the fun factor. Games in TF2 used to be alot more longer than they are now. AND they used to have alot more players aswell, which obiously doesnt make you want to play more. Nevertheless, the game is also pretty buggy in a few points. The hitboxes are either ridiculous or ♥♥♥♥ing stupid. In short, this FPS is uniquie.
What i mean by that?
Most of FPS avaliable to aquire are military shooters. They tend to be really serious one, where having a good killing spree or doing great at playing objective is main thing You focus on, but TF2 isn't that one. It places fun over those two, where in other situations fun was somewhere below. For example when You kill other player in some fancy way and other one from opposing team will see this, then there is good chance that except of trying to kill You, he might give You thumbs up and go his way (but don't start thinking that everyone will do this!). Sometimes players from opposing teams stop to shoot to each other just to walk around and have some fun with voice commands.
Yes, I have to agree that "friendliness" appears in many other FPS's but here it's most common.
Other than just having fun TF2 offers 9 classes. Hah, You may think its nothing new, but hell no.
Each of those classes are allmost completly different, and they allmost always have pretty much good counters (except snipers ofc. Those are always problem in every FPS) And same map and same players, but playing different class will change whole perspective of gameplay (just in this situations 9 games in 1).
I can say that TF2 isn't just a one game, It's combination of them! Those are things that will give You completly new experience while playing Team Fortress 2
- Rocket jumping
- Sticky jumping
- Sentry jumping
- Surf maps
- Zombie Fortress maps
- Dogdeball
- Smash bros maps
- Death run maps
- Trick stabs
- Shortcuts for each maps
- Even griefing
- And many more
If You don't know what any of those means, than You should get into Team Fortress 2 right now.
So If You are bored of those military shooters out there and want to try something new, than check it out!

you want a review? well even if you didn't I'm giving you one anyways.
TF2 is not like most FPS games, let alone one that is free to play. TF2 is the sequel to a game known as team fortress classic, a mod using the unreal tournament engine. blah blah blah historical stuff I prolly got wrong. ANYWAYS: TF2 is quite simply an amazing game, with 9 different classes, each with their own unique roles in a successful match.
1. scout: he runs fast, capping intel, capping control points, and pushing the bomb cart with the power of 2 people! warning, since he runs so fast and has a double jump, allowing for high evasiveness, hes also pretty squishy, having a measly 125 base health.
2. soldier: soldier is a powerhouse, holding 200 base health and a rocket launcher that deals splash damage to multiple enemies. his rocket jumping ability (though this takes a LOT of practice to fully master) can get him to the point even faster than a scout!
3. pyro: the most controversial class, having 175 base health, medium-paced walking speed, and a short-ranged based primary (the flamethrower), pyro can be seen as the weakest class. while most newbies would complain to him being an overpowered fire demon here to eat your babies, they really just don't know how easy it is to counter her. (ONE SECOND THOUGH: PYRO CAN AIRBLAST PROJECTILES AND EXTINGUISH BURNING TEAMMATES BY USING M2, OR MOUSE 2).
4. demoman: arguably the most powerful class in the game, demoman is here to bring diversity to the game. (y'know, because hes scottish). anyways, demoman, while having the same 175 health as pyro, has one distinct advantage: the stickybomb launcher. this bad boy does 60 damage per sticky, meaning that spamming it on a public game makes you a bad player that should go back to playing minecraft and the hundredth jumpscare game pewdiepie just played.
5. heavy: also considered one of the weakest in the game (especially without a medic latched onto him 24/7) heavy is the mascot for TF2. this bald, bear wrestling, russian giant shows none of his ruthlessness in the game, but rather the comics (which even then he realy kind of doesn't). heavy has 300 health! "wow!" you must think, until you learn his disadvantages. he is the slowest and has the largest hitbox in the game, making him easy to pick off from afar.
6. medic: oh boy. medic is the second fastest class in the game, just after scout. he also has 150 base health.your CoD-washed mind might think "hey wheres his souper smg ding?" well thats because TF2's medic is actually here for healing. sure, he has a syringe gun (which is basically a flamethrower without afterburn) but no sane medic would rush into a fight like that, as he'd die near instantly. (each class has their own way of dealing 100+ damage in one shot, though this is mostly up to crits/ actual skill). instead, medic uses his medigun, a long, black, healing device that can patch up your teammate's wounds in seconds! plus, when you have full "ubercharge" you can either have increased healing, full invincibility, 100% chance of everything your teammate does being a critical hit, or a tiny uber that increases your resistance to a certain type of attack, and gives you health for the damage the person you're healing recieves.
7. engineer: engineer builds sentries, dispencers, and teleporters. sentries will guard an area, sitting in place waiting for some unsuspecting scout to run in and get blasted away by tons of bullets (and rockets when your sentry reaches max level). dispencers health and provide ammo for you and your teammates. teleporters are capable of sending your teammates from one side of the map to the other, however, all these buildings require a lot of care, as they are susceptable to many attacks, and will do no damage to stock ubers (the kind that grants full invincibility). and since you'll probably be taking care of your buildings and aimbot, engineer only has 125 health.
8. sniper: sniper, if played right, can outdamage demoman! even though sniper only has 125 health, he has the longest range out of every class, what with a sniper rifle and all. sniper is the one of the only classes that can kill a fully overhealed heavy in less than 3 seconds. the sniper rifle isn't like most sniper rifles in other games. having good aim is essential to playing sniper, as his main source of damage is getting headshots, otherwise he'll normally do only 50 damage.
9. spy: spy is a real sneaky rat. he can diguise as any class, sap buildings (turning them off and eventually destroying them unless the engineer hits and breaks the sapper), his main "deal" is that he can "backstab" enemies. backstabbing someone is always an instant kill, with only for a few exceptions.
TF2 is a great game, and I suggest you look into it.

Your objective is to kill all the members on the other team and either control the control point for 120 seconds, capture all the control points, so forth. For newcomers, there is a training mode where you practice against bots, and for pros, there is multiplayer, where you (obviously) play other people worldwide. Well, thats TF2 in a nutshell. Enjoy!

In short, this FPS is uniquie.
What i mean by that?
Most of FPS avaliable to aquire are military shooters. They tend to be really serious one, where having a good killing spree or doing great at playing objective is main thing You focus on, but TF2 isn't that one. It places fun over those two, where in other situations fun was somewhere below. For example when You kill other player in some fancy way and other one from opposing team will see this, then there is good chance that except of trying to kill You, he might give You thumbs up and go his way (but don't start thinking that everyone will do this!). Sometimes players from opposing teams stop to shoot to each other just to walk around and have some fun with voice commands.
Yes, I have to agree that "friendliness" appears in many other FPS's but here it's most common.
Other than just having fun TF2 offers 9 classes. Hah, You may think its nothing new, but hell no.
Each of those classes are allmost completly different, and they allmost always have pretty much good counters (except snipers ofc. Those are always problem in every FPS) And same map and same players, but playing different class will change whole perspective of gameplay (just in this situations 9 games in 1).
I can say that TF2 isn't just a one game, It's combination of them! Those are things that will give You completly new experience while playing Team Fortress 2
- Rocket jumping
- Sticky jumping
- Sentry jumping
- Surf maps
- Zombie Fortress maps
- Dogdeball
- Smash bros maps
- Death run maps
- Trick stabs
- Shortcuts for each maps
- Even griefing
- And many more
If You don't know what any of those means, than You should get into Team Fortress 2 right now.
So If You are bored of those military shooters out there and want to try something new, than check it out!

Solid game that emphasises teamwork over a lone gunman being able to carry a team. It's true if you are really good you can heavily influence a game, but it isn't like CoD or Battlefield where one person can literally carry a team to victory. Your KDA isn't publicly displayed butw hat is displayed is the number of points you get. These can be gained by doing things that help the team (i.e pushing objectives, defending teammates, etc etc). There is a diverse number of classes  to choose from and each class has a specific role on the battle field. This can encourage players to be diverse instead of sticking to just one class. Some classes are arguably more important on the battlefield (i.e protect your medics!) but working together is the best way to win games. The gameplay is fluid and each class has their own unique style of play. There are basic level skills everyone should learn, but you can really take each class to a high level of play with time and patience. Overall I would recommend this game to anyone looking for a colorful and dynamic shooter which encourages teamwork.
P.S-it helps to find a server that has a great community. Most of the Valve servers are filled with people who just want to frag people. A server like lionsden is great because it has people that are really good at the game and the people there are more focused on pushing objectives and working together.

Ah, TF2, one of the most well-known and popular FPS games out there on Steam, especially since it became Free To Play on the Steam Store.  Ever since a friend got me into this game, I've been playing it non-stop for more than 200 play hours in total, and I would like to take the time to give my own thoughts on the game as a whole and some tips for newcomers to help them on their way to enjoy the game and not ragequit within the first 20 minutes of jumping right into it.
First off, gameplay-wise the game is a typical multiplayer-based FPS game where the core goal is very simplistic: Hop on either the red or blue team and kill the opposing team and secure victory, however, the methods of accomplishing this range per match type, and usually good teamwork and class diversity are required to win the match.
As for said class diversity, the game offers you 9 different playable class characters to choose from, all with their unique advantages and disadvantages, and it's a key requirement for any player to learn the limits and strengths of those classes in order to play the class effectively and to be of benefit to your team as a whole. Thankfully the game has a alright tutorial on a few classes, specifically the Demoman, Spy, Engineer and Soldier, but there are many tricks for a class that the game doesn't often directly tell you, but rather clues you in through the in-game loading screen tips section when you go to a match.
Picking a class that suits your playstyle is often the first thing many new players struggle with, but the classes all range from fairly easy to pick up and play decently with, to far more tricky and fragile ones that require the player to be familiar with the mechanics and overall gameplay before they can effectively use them in combat. Such examples are the Heavy, Soldier and Pyro which in my opinion are some of the more easily accessable classes for new players to experiment around with, and Engineer, Sniper and Spy for the more experienced players when they feel confident enough. It has something for every kind of FPS gamer regardless of skill level, which is what I really like about this game.
Atmosphere-wise, the game is very visually pleasing with alot of intricate map design accomodating the various matchtypes, and is designed so that players who are unfamiliar with the map and it's pathways are given visual cues on where to go, like if they're on the red team, a red arrow sign will point in the general direction where they need to head to, as well as various signs detailing a mission's objective and locations, like 'Intelligence' for the intel briefcase on capture the flag, 'Battlements' for the general middle area where most of the combat will take place, etc.
The classes all have dynamic personalities that make them a blast to play as and you'll often chuckle at their lines regarding the situation, which really gives this game alot of personality. I personally really enjoy the Pyro because the character itself wears a gas mask which makes most of his lines almost inaudiable, but if you listen carefully you can make out a few key lines that he screams out.
Besides the game's addictive core gameplay, there's alot of side content to it like customizable loadouts to your class' arsenal, cosmetic clothing and different taunts which you usually have to acquire through specific unlocking methods, crafting from metal which you get from turning additional weapons into metal which you obtain from random weapon drops during gameplay or trading with other players.
Trading is one of the key mechanics of interacting with other players, and interacting with other players is oftentimes a good way of getting to meet a nice friend on Steam wether it's someone on your team, or someone you encounter while on a specific trade server, and who might be able to trade or even gift you some stuff if you're friendly to the player and and he/she is friendly to you in return. Just be careful of annoying or pushy players who are out for your items and will offer either nothing or nearly worthless items in return, though, if you happen to encounter those, just ignore them.
There is also a Mann vs. Machine co-op game mode in where you get to work together with 5 other players being the limit against a horde of powerful robots trying to defend your area from a bomb they will attempt to deliver at all costs. This game mode is much more intense than regular multiplayer TF2 and you can earn nice cosmetic item rewards for your weapons in the Mann Up mode, but the Bootcamp mode is free to play and a good way for practice, but Mann vs. Machine is very tough and is not recommended for newcomers of TF2 to try out immediately.
With that all out of the way, here are a few tips I would recommend everybody who's going to try this game out to follow if they want to have a pleasant experience playing this game in the long run:
- Always stay friendly to other players and don't act obnoxious or self-righteous to others.  The name of the game is TEAM Fortress 2, meaning that in order to win, you need to work together as a team, and not go out there, thinking you can take the entire team on yourself, which will oftentimes lead to you getting killed over and over again. Communicate with your fellow team members over the situation and what you're planning to do, or regarding  plans or tactics that the enemy team is using through the default Y normal in-game chat and U team members-only chat window buttons. Your team members will appreciate it if you're friendly, and will be much more likely to co-operate alongside with you towards completing the objective if you do so. Sure the game can get very hectic and is easy to get annoyed over a supposed 'cheap kill' from a enemy player, but overall try to maintain a friendly atmosphere in the game.
- If nessecary, do offline training on maps that you're unfamiliar with, and explore the maps so you'll know the shortcuts and side routes into enemy territory. This is a key factor into becoming a more skilled player over time, as there are many side routes that are often easy to miss or not pay attention to that the developers of the maps implemented in order to balance the game and make it possible for a team to overcome the other if they're being pressured or having difficulty breaking through chokepoints. If the enemy team is spawncamping, try to take a different spawn exit and flank them from behind. If the main route into their base is heavily guarded, look for a alternate pathway to take and inform your teammates about it.
- Play classes that suit the current situation. This is a common mistake that I see occuring alot on many servers I play on, as quite alot of players seem to not grasp the limits of a class and oftentimes like to stick to one class only just because they like playing as that certain class and refuse to play anything else that the team might benefit more at that specific point during the match. Players need to observe the situation and pick classes whose advantages are required at the time. To give a good example, payload is a match type in where the red team needs to defend the bomb from being delivered by the blue team, and as such will be spawn-camping right off the bat during the start of the match. Yet alot of times there tend to be about 2 or 3 Spy and/or Sniper players in a team of roughly 9 to 12 players on blue. Those 2 classes can only take out 1 enemy at a time normally, and will be killed easily. You'll need a strong offensive class like Heavy or Soldier to pressure and kill the enemy team, and if your team doesn't have a Medic, be one. Medic isn't a easy class, but your team members will benefit from the healing so they won't have to retreat to the supply closet often. Class diversity and good communication about class choices mid-game can go a long way in winning the match.
Thanks for reading this, and hope it was insightful. I definetely recommend this game!

It is a very simple game that involves a feud between two companies working against eachother, BLU and RED. This game is very blunt when you first start playing it but as you get more immersed into it, you start to like it more and more. Team Fortress 2 is a weird game, and it is not only a FPS game anymore. I would describe it more as a social hub for people to hang out. This game have two teams that are supposed to fight each other, but only in Team Fortress 2 with two people of the opposite team giving each other high fives, stop fighting during the game and walk around crouching, or dance together!
There are nine classes divided into three groups; offense, defense and support. But Team Fortress 2 have changed so much since release that it does not really mean anything anymore. Pretty much every class can function as any of the three groups with the right loadout, but they are still very different from each other. You got a fast Scout with little health, and a slow Heavy with a lot of health, and anything inbetween that! There is no way you will not find a class you prefer sticking to.
Valve never added a new class, but they added tons of weapons! Some of them are really silly (punch an enemy in the back to make him stop and laugh, a great way to get silly taunt kills!), while others generally are a big improvement over the stock weapons (like the Degreaser). However most of the weapons are very situational and I prefer the stock weapons.
There are many game modes to play. Capture the point, capture the flag. Payload where you push a cart through the map while the other team try preventing you from doing it, and if you're a fan of tower defense, you will enjoy Mann Vs. Machine! You're a team of up to six people who are supposed to kill a huge army of robots before they move their bomb to your base. Some of them are small, others are big and really hurts, and others are big and runs fast. But what really makes this game mode different from the more traditional Team Fortress 2, is you can upgrade your weapons. Fire speed, damage, reload speed, damage resistances, running speed, jump speed and so on. It is really fun, and if you are lucky you can win a huge prize for completing a Tour!
Cosmetic items are a huge deal for many people. Hats! There are so many hats in this game, and they are all so different. There is no way you are not going to find one you like and will wear and be proud to wear every time you play. Many of the cosmetics can also be painted into your favourite colour!
Team Fortress 2 is free to play. Is it pay to win? No. All the weapons you see in the store, are weapons you can get simply by playing, or you can use items to craft the weapon you want. If you buy premium you will receive weapons faster, your backpack will be larger so you can keep more items, and you can trade with others. Trading is a good way to get the weapon you're looking for.
It is a lot of fun! It is fun to play the actual game, or just hanging out with people ingame like you can not do in any other game. This is the game where you make friends! ^____^

If you ignore some part of the toxic community including tryhards, crazy people who yell at your team for not doing a simple thing, and the occasional pro that kicks your♥♥♥♥♥ This game scores high on the field.
The many things of this game is relatively likeable, you're given new weapons to toy with from the drop system that changes how the game is played little by little, each and every weapon can alter the style of how you play, and as a result, makes you feel like you're kinda creating your own build. There are loads of cosmetic items and hats to customize with that when people get to that stage of getting those cosmetic items and paints, people can make an appearance of themselves in the game that distinguishes them. Even Free to Players can get a variety of hats for free and use them, but most of all, the majority of the game's community. But it's not the hats that make the player, it's the dedication and how the game works.
Every now and then, sure, you'll come across a squeaker or even an arrogant fool that brags about killing you every time, but most of all? What makes games fun is when the teams are both on balance beams, but you're capable of playing against up to thirty-two people on a server, usually, or, by Valve standard's, twenty-four. The characters, being suited for different roles in the game are comical, colorful, and fleshed out, given their own personality and having their own unique, lovable shine to them, where unlike other games with most classes, people sound like they have the same voice actor, or even the same two or three voice actors, where it this game, the voices for the characters are quite indistinguishable and marvelously done by the team in that sector, despite some classes sharing the same voice actor. The game is portrayed in a cartoonish art style in which the characters are represented well for it.
The game allows you to have Offline practice which even then can challenge you with what you're doing, Normal mode alone pits you up against multiple engineers, and occasionally a Sniper and Spy, and a normal team functions identically to that as an average team of people on Team Fortress 2 (Safe for the Medic, occasionally, where I died right in front of the AI when lit afire and calling for him with no medpack in sight.). Which Normal is the best difficulty to hone your skills, though Easy too, can be occasionally challenging. Every online game is not relatively geared to be the same, too. You're pit up with likely people you've never even met.
And what these people do is what makes that game feel different, you might make friends, you might make rivals, you might see new techniques, you might see something silly. Not every game in TF2 is the same compared to most team-based shooters, which is absolute rush down or too much centered upon simple quickscoping, and shooting. In order to get better at the game, you need to be more aware of your surroundings, what is happening, and not only this, but to counter the playstyle of players in the game, which you may or may not do.
The only bad points this game has had is some bugs, exploits, and occasionally, you may find a hacker if you're unlucky enough. But this game originally started as a Quake Mod, and then has went through nine years of development, and now, up to this point, we've got a masterpiece which all of it's years had paid off it's potential. 95%

I'm actually a big fan of Valve, but Team Fortress 2 seems more like a comedy writer with no gaming experience attemping to make a first-person shooter than a Valve game. The world and the characters are absolutely wonderful, so much so that I've wasted at least a hundred hours watching TF2 source videos and shorts on Youtube, and the idea of, to quote another review, "cartoon men running around shooting other cartoon men," seems brilliant on paper. But the game itself is poorly designed and poorly executed. Combat is dull, has almost no tactical depth, and is frustratingly chaotic, like poorly supervised fifth graders playing football on a Sunday afternoon. And given how horrid the community is, it might as well be poorly supervised fifth graders playing football on a Sunday afternoon. The rules and structure of combat are rather arbitrary, and internal regulations like balancing are almost non-existent. Also the obsession with hats really is ridiculous, not amusing like I was hoping.
Maybe I'd be more forgiving of these things if the community wasn't so awful. After all, the premise is so simple, I can almost understand why combat would be as well. And if I understand correcly, it originally was little more than a simple, casual game that was fun nevertheless. But now it's as if Valve is trying to pass it off as an in-depth, complex MMO, rather than what it was initially meant to be.
Overall, I give this game a "meh." It comes so close to being a glorious, if casual, game. But it's not.

Team Fortress 2 is a weird game, and it is not only a FPS game anymore. I would describe it more as a social hub for people to hang out. This game have two teams that are supposed to fight each other, but only in Team Fortress 2 with two people of the opposite team giving each other high fives, stop fighting during the game and walk around crouching, or dance together!
There are nine classes divided into three groups; offense, defense and support. But Team Fortress 2 have changed so much since release that it does not really mean anything anymore. Pretty much every class can function as any of the three groups with the right loadout, but they are still very different from each other. You got a fast Scout with little health, and a slow Heavy with a lot of health, and anything inbetween that! There is no way you will not find a class you prefer sticking to.
Valve never added a new class, but they added tons of weapons! Some of them are really silly (punch an enemy in the back to make him stop and laugh, a great way to get silly taunt kills!), while others generally are a big improvement over the stock weapons (like the Degreaser). However most of the weapons are very situational and I prefer the stock weapons.
There are many game modes to play. Capture the point, capture the flag. Payload where you push a cart through the map while the other team try preventing you from doing it, and if you're a fan of tower defense, you will enjoy Mann Vs. Machine! You're a team of up to six people who are supposed to kill a huge army of robots before they move their bomb to your base. Some of them are small, others are big and really hurts, and others are big and runs fast. But what really makes this game mode different from the more traditional Team Fortress 2, is you can upgrade your weapons. Fire speed, damage, reload speed, damage resistances, running speed, jump speed and so on. It is really fun, and if you are lucky you can win a huge prize for completing a Tour!
Cosmetic items are a huge deal for many people. Hats! There are so many hats in this game, and they are all so different. There is no way you are not going to find one you like and will wear and be proud to wear every time you play. Many of the cosmetics can also be painted into your favourite colour!
Team Fortress 2 is free to play. Is it pay to win? No. All the weapons you see in the store, are weapons you can get simply by playing, or you can use items to craft the weapon you want. If you buy premium you will receive weapons faster, your backpack will be larger so you can keep more items, and you can trade with others. Trading is a good way to get the weapon you're looking for.

Get past the addiction for hats, and you have a polished and well balanced shooter that will keep you hooked.
With 9 different classes, each with their own unique weaknesses, strengths, and team oriented skills, there is a  variety of playstyles that can suit any player. The characters are colorful and distinct, which makes it easy to tell whats what among the chaos, something that most other shooters seem to lack without resorting to inelegant indicators.
There are several game modes, from capture the flag to pushing the cart, to king of the hill, with hundreds of official and community created maps to keep you occupied.
If you would like to take a break from playing against human players, you can try mann vs machine mode; this mode pits you and your team against hordes of computer controlled bots. Work together to endure the onslaught!
Although you may not begin with every weapon unlocked, each weapon has been balanced around those you already start with; you dont have to fear having grind or buy superior weapons, and you can have an impact in fights right away.
This game is totally free; any money you spend would be for cosmetics that you can gain over time, and that give no advantage whatsoever.
So if you're looking for an alternative to the yearly installments of grey and brown shooters that wont cost you 60 bucks every time, this is the game for you. Again, this is no candy crush that will try to squeeze you for everything you've got. I have been playing and enjoying this since a decade ago and have yet to spend a single penny.
One thing to be wary of is that there is no "free for all" mode; all games involve being in a team. That doesnt stop anyone from going rambo though. Seriously, this is one of, if not the best free to play games out there and has been for a long time.

I remember the countless hours I logged into this game playing by myself, going through many sleepless nights. Now this game  is even more fun with friends. The game is a class based FPS that blends teamwork and strategy. Will you rush the control point as a scout, using your ability to capture objectives twice as fast? Or will you team up with a medic and Uber your way through the point? There is so much variety to this game that it will fit a lot of players there is a class for everyone in this game, all 8 classes have their own benfits with the Spy being able to Cloak and backstab in one swift move or the heavy having 300 HP, acting as a juggernaut! The one big downside for me is items. So many players are judged over what they have, being called noobs for having a Ghostly Gibus or the Pyrovision goggles, it's a adventure to find hats that make you look like you know how to play. The weapons have lots of variety and bring lots of playstyles to work. Mann vs Machine is a great secondary gamemode, defending your stronghold against many robot hordes. There is also lots of In-game holidays, which has a special benefit to it, lots of items! Ever since it has relaesed to be free-to-play there is a huge flow of new players, keeping the game alive. I suggest you try it if you like strategy based shooters.

What can be said about Team Fortress 2 that hasn't been said already?
It's one of the best FPS' Valve has ever released, and the funniest one I've played. You basically pick your color, RED or BLU, then you pick from nine classes;
The Demoman - The scottish bomber with his trusty grenade launcher and his Stickybomb Launcher.
The Engineer - The texan that can create various stuff like a Sentry gun, a Dispenser, and Teleporters to assist his team.
The Heavy - A walking, talking Russian 'Incredible Hulk' with a minigun that costs $400,000 to fire for 12 seconds.
The Medic - The german doctor that uses a syringe gun and a neat little thing that'll heal his teammates and Ubercharge them.
The Pyro - The...uh...wherever-he's-from pyro that uses his powerful Flamethrower to heat up the competition.
The Scout - The american teen that can run like 'Sonic the Hedgehog' and double jump like 'Mario' uses a Scattergun and his trusty bat to knock his opponents out of the park.
The Sniper - Just like his name implies, this australian scopes his enemies in the distance, and throws a jar of♥♥♥♥♥♥at them.
The Soldier - This proud american uses his Rocket Launcher and his famous Frying pan to serve his country proud.
The Spy - This frenchie can sap an Engineer's inventions, turn invisible and backstab enemies, and even disguise himself as the enemy and infiltrate their base.
...and go out on an all-out-totally-hillarious war with-or-without your friends and test your skills to see who's better!
After you had a hooplah of fun online, you can go to the Mann Co. Store and buy brand new items made by the people at the Steam Workshop, and test them out the next time you go online.
My final verdict for "Team Fortress 2," is a 5/5. If you love Valve and FPS games, and games with cartoony graphics, download this game RIGHT NOW, after you're done reading my review. And also, check out Source Filmmaker, where you can create your own TF2 movies. I guess I'm gonna stop talking and let you download this game.

TF2 is a cash making cow. Valve literally prints their own money while this game runs. People go nuts for costume changes, weapons, kill counters, etc. Any accessory which perks their game play. They pay big money for keys to open boxes and get different items.
Think of this. A regular game costs $40 to 50? People buy keys for several (currently $2.49) dollars each with special keys going for as much as ten times that amount during special events. So during the course of a year a person will spend $100 to $200 dollars for keys and special bundles. Chaching!
Hacks and exploits are abundant. in the game. People use mule accounts to run the hacks and exploits, gain their booty, then trade it off to a main account or other account so that it isn't traceable. Since TF2 is a free game and you can always open another Steam account to play TF2 it doesn't matter that you get caught. At worst you might lose one or two items if you aren't moving stuff along the chain of storage accounts.
People also run low effect hacks which only give them a slight advantage over other players. They might get a little more speed or a little more damage. (EDIT)
A friend got me back in to the game for a little bit this year. I played for almost two months off and on through to Nov. I then quit the game completely and never will play it again. Valve does nothing to curb the cheaters and exploiters. They talk the talk but don't walk the walk.
TF2 is a cash making cow. Valve literally prints their own money while this game runs. People go nuts for costume changes, weapons, kill counters, etc. Any accessory which perks their game play. They pay big money for keys to open boxes and get different items.
Think of this. A regular game costs $40 to 50? People buy keys for several (currently $2.49) dollars each with special keys going for as much as ten times that amount during special events. So during the course of a year a person will spend $100 to $200 dollars for keys and special bundles. Chaching!
Hacks and exploits are abundant. in the game. People use mule accounts to run the hacks and exploits, gain their booty, then trade it off to a main account or other account so that it isn't traceable. Since TF2 is a free game and you can always open another Steam account to play TF2 it doesn't matter that you get caught. At worst you might lose one or two items if you aren't moving stuff along the chain of storage accounts.
People also run low effect hacks which only give them a slight advantage over other players. They might get a little more speed or a little more damage. It is just enough to give them an edge and not get caught. If they get caught usually players will vote them off the server, but if you only cheat a little bit then maybe no one will notice.
Either way, VAC servers are supposed to be self-supported and kick players/deleted players/ban players who cheat or use exploits. It's a slow process so a player who is abusing the system will run for weeks without being banned. By the time VAC gets around to actually deleting/banning them the damage has been done.
Valve is a completely worthless but profitable company. They people who are making the money don't give a♥♥♥♥♥♥about normal, legit players. If they did these exploits and hacks would never work. Valve would just change the code so that this stuff wouldn't work even if it was updated. However they don't change the code to stop it, they allow it because it is more profitable.
Do yourself a favor and save yourself time and money. Go find a different game on Steam to play. Do not play TF2. Leave it to the cheaters to cheat and let them have their way. Maybe when the game finally starts to cost money to maintain Valve might actually fix the problem.

Admittedly, I joined the Team Fortress hype after the release of the Orange Box, with the release of TF2. After clocking in 111 hours of playtime, it's safe to assume that I'm an adoring fan. TF2 does so many things well, the character classes, the shooting mechanics, the darkly absurd humor and (most importantly) the teamwork. Playing each of the classes feels like a new gameplay discovery everytime with an ever-changing multiplayer experience. But for all of the things that TF2 gets right, it's accomplished something I've always wanted in a multiplayer experience: fun. Too often multiplayer games turn into experiences where those that dedicate massive amounts of hours to playing, trample those just starting out, establishing little to no incentive to keep playing. TF2 is different, perhaps largely so by it's fun aesthetic, but really because of class and gameplay balance. A balance that continues to evolve with Valve's incredible post-launch support. TF2 is not going anywhere and now there's absolutely no reason not to try it out as it's free-to-play. Go do it. You can thank me later for the recommendation.

This is an excellent game, honestly. Everything feels polished and crafted with love. The only negative experience I've ever had with the game has come from the community-- a group called Summit Under Nothing (SuN), a wretched hive of scum and villainy (if I were to use a movie quote to describe them, at least). Other than them, of course, I've really enjoyed my hundred and fifty hours with this game. It's far from the "hat simulator" some people describe it as; although there are a lot of hats, there's also a distinct social element to the game, as well as a unique feeling to the combat. I'd recommend this game, and since it's free...why would you say no?

I remember the countless hours I logged into this game playing by myself, going through many sleepless nights. Now this game  is even more fun with friends. The game is a class based FPS that blends teamwork and strategy. Will you rush the control point as a scout, using your ability to capture objectives twice as fast? Or will you team up with a medic and Uber your way through the point? There is so much variety to this game that it will fit a lot of players there is a class for everyone in this game, all 8 classes have their own benfits with the Spy being able to Cloak and backstab in one swift move or the heavy having 300 HP, acting as a juggernaut! The one big downside for me is items. So many players are judged over what they have, being called noobs for having a Ghostly Gibus or the Pyrovision goggles, it's a adventure to find hats that make you look like you know how to play. The weapons have lots of variety and bring lots of playstyles to work. Mann vs Machine is a great secondary gamemode, defending your stronghold against many robot hordes. There is also lots of In-game holidays, which has a special benefit to it, lots of items! Ever since it has relaesed to be free-to-play there is a huge flow of new players, keeping the game alive. I suggest you try it if you like strategy based shooters.

Best. Game. Ever. Shall I list why?
-Graphics
The graphical style of this game is truly unique, sort of a cartoony, fun, but sometimes dark theme. Ambient light changes rapidly, affecting the mood, and it all has a sort of painted look that I haven't seen anywhere else. Halloween updates/maps are AWESOME, and look incredible with very creative modifications of normal maps.
-Map Design
The map design for TF2 is far more in-depth than other games, mainly because they have to balance the maps perfectly, while making them fun to play. Looking at a TF2 map, they look kind of jumbled and not balanced at all. But when you start playing, them, the amount of time put into designing a map becomes evident. Another thing they have to do, is make the map fun to play yet not too easy/OP for a certain class, in order for it to be fun for everyone.
-Classes
The classes are incredibly well designed, balanced, and perfected to the extent that I start to wonder if the developers of TF2 are human. I mean, what game can be this good? No matter what your play-style, there's a class for you, and a way to play that class. It's fun for everyone.
-Hats
Do I have to say anything about this? Gaben has created a monster which will suck the money from the world.
-Weapons
Weapons in TF2 are incredibly creative, with effects ranging from conditional crits, to chronological damage, to a f*cking ring of fire around you. In addition, they're all balanced out so no weapons are overpowered, though some weapons are a bit better than the stock items. This makes it so that F2P players can still do well, in addition to finding random drops which can be nearly any item.
-Voice Acting
TF2 voice acting is hilarious, clever, realistic, and believable. I have a strange feeling of friendship with Sniper that I feel like I should get checked out, and a protective feeling of Pyro, mostly due to the fact the he thinks he's handing out goddamn candy.
-Workshop
Anyone can create TF2 weapons and cosmetics, and that's how quite a lot of TF2 items were added. I think this is a very cool feature, because it really encourages players to get deeper into the game, and some of those submissions are pretty damn cool.
-Game Modes
Valve really went all out on game modes, and the game modes they didn't make up they put a fun, cool twist on that makes it totally their own.
-Storyline
The TF2 comics and videos are freakin' awesome.
I have done nothing but teleport heavies for 3 hours.
All in all, TF2 is one of the best games I've ever played, hands down.

If I was to summarise this game, I would simply describe it as the best first person shooter ever made. If you don't have it downloaded then hop right over to the steam library and go to the free games section.
However, if you're the type that likes a bit more detail in your descriptions, then team fortress is also the right game for you. It is truly a 'easy to learn, hard to master' type of game. Additionally, upon starting the game you will not be instantly swamped by players who can kill you easier because they have weapons that are better than you. Everything in tf2 is balanced beautifully, between the weapons, individual classes and the overall team dynamic. Each new item doesn't bring with it a new advantage, but a new way that you can tweak your playstyle, with it's own individual positive and negative aspects.
The overall feel of the game is great as well, due to the cartoony graphics and humorous quips that your team will constantly spout. Even in the worst matches, when I've had my head driven into the dirt by a more skilled team, I still walk away with an inward grin at that one time that four of my team mates and I walked a literal conga line through the enemy team's defence or airblasting an enemy scout and keeping him pinned against a wall while he shouted that I was a spy, followed by us sharing a high five and his character spontaneously exploding.
I could go on about this game for days, but you shouldn't be reading it. You should be playing it as I speak.

Team Fortress 2 has been around for quite a while now, so I'd be surprised to hear that you haven't heard of it! The game is in my opinion the BEST multiplayer FPS I have ever played; this is coming from a guy who HATES most FPS's. I won't sit here and break down the gameplay for you because, hey, there are in-game tutorials for that. What I will say, however, is that the game is very well balanced (mostly) and each of the classes are great fun to play, even if you may suck at them. The game looks and sounds wonderful, with the colorful and lovable art style and satisfying sound design it's a huge draw to the game as opposed to "Gritty FPS 20103015151." I love the smooth and responsive gameplay and especially the class system so that everyone gets their chance to play how they want! The economy is growing and a blast to participate with, and you can get some really nice cosmetics and maybe even a few friends this way(?), One big downfall to the game however is that the community can be rather toxic, ESPECIALLY if a server has loose moderators and admins. With the proper amount of patrolling and calling out the toxic people, this problem becomes easily solved and the left over pieces are a very solid multiplayer experience that you should surely try sometime!

This game is a very complicated and well-thoughtout game. It includes mandatory strategizing with strangers who surround you as well as your individual thinking patterns. In order to be successful in this multiplayer shooting game, you must be the game. What I mean by being the game is that you have to live and breathe every single item and class as well as study the complex system of accessories such as the hats and protective eyewear. Hats dwells into a very more developed system that I will discuss later on in this review. For now, I shall explain on why this game is very good. The moment I started playing this game, it put me onto a tutorial which is very good as many games do not have a tutorial or do no recommend/force you to do it. The tutorial is a crucial part in learning but it is not the primary of it. When playing this game following the tutorial, you are given the option to choose your own unofficial server or choose a game mode and let TF2 pick the server for you. The latter is a player-friendly function that allows new players and veterans alike to join any game mode that is available in almost an instant. When I entered the game, I was given the option to pick 9 classes and it was a very discriptive on how they explained on how each classes worked. When I was actually playing as a class, I was greeted with moderate graphics that did not put my computer under stress. The community is very friendly as well, but when there is the occasional "troll", you are free to screenshot it and report it to the TF2 Human Resources. This limits bullying as well as fights. The ability to talk on your microphone allows further strategizing against the enemy team and is good for people who want to go into the competitive TF2 scene (looking at you Sage). The actual game play is very good and thought out, and all items are balanced appropriately. Sure, when you're knew it seems like a lot of items are overpowered, and while some are on the stronger side of the spectrum, none are absurdly overpowered and must be nerfed immediately. The same goes with classes as well; each class has a role in the game and can shine in different game modes and maps. What is key to win in any game mode or map is the ability to pick a role and stick with it to combine with your other teammates to make a dominate team. There is no limit to a class on a single team though which can allow fun combos of perhaps 10 spies. Now onto the economy of TF2, it is very complex and how's it done has impressed me very much. The ability to trade items for other items, which includes weapons and accessories, is a freedom that others do not enjoy in other games. Also, the ability to find random items and unlock random items is a nice addition if you cannot buy items with real money. Overall, TF2 is a very nice game and I commend Valve for trumping TF1 with it.

TF2 is to Valve as Pokemon is to Nintendo.  The art design is fun and the originally innovative idea of taking quake styled gameplay and converting it to a team objective game was quite impressive for the time but casually designing the game (randomized critical hits as well as designing item stats around said probabilities) make learning the consistent fundamentals of the game very confusing and all around a frustrating experience especially when team responsibility is a crucial mechanic of the game.  This would also explain the community being as presumptuous and obnoxious as they are.   The game then becomes about aggrandizing oneself to the point of delusion.  That being said there is the competitive side of the community which aims to gradually change the games design by banning items in specific leagues along with voiding the previously stated "random critical hits" as well as damage spread.  This does not excuse the shoddy programming and economy, though.   Some aesthetics of the game are also broken such as items disappearing, hands becoming invisible and hastily implemented animations. Buying items in the game with real world money also contributes to how the design was put second to profit and marketability.  Programming as stated before is also very questionable, a major example being projected hitboxes.  Some ideas are innovative and others are gimmick ridden. The updates are few and far in between and never progress the game's design (or lack of design).  You would be hard pressed to have a genuine experience in this game.

This game is a very complicated and well-thoughtout game. It includes mandatory strategizing with strangers who surround you as well as your individual thinking patterns. In order to be successful in this multiplayer shooting game, you must be the game. What I mean by being the game is that you have to live and breathe every single item and class as well as study the complex system of accessories such as the hats and protective eyewear. Hats dwells into a very more developed system that I will discuss later on in this review. For now, I shall explain on why this game is very good. The moment I started playing this game, it put me onto a tutorial which is very good as many games do not have a tutorial or do no recommend/force you to do it. The tutorial is a crucial part in learning but it is not the primary of it. When playing this game following the tutorial, you are given the option to choose your own unofficial server or choose a game mode and let TF2 pick the server for you. The latter is a player-friendly function that allows new players and veterans alike to join any game mode that is available in almost an instant. When I entered the game, I was given the option to pick 9 classes and it was a very discriptive on how they explained on how each classes worked. When I was actually playing as a class, I was greeted with moderate graphics that did not put my computer under stress. The community is very friendly as well, but when there is the occasional "troll", you are free to screenshot it and report it to the TF2 Human Resources. This limits bullying as well as fights. The ability to talk on your microphone allows further strategizing against the enemy team and is good for people who want to go into the competitive TF2 scene (looking at you Sage). The actual game play is very good and thought out, and all items are balanced appropriately. Sure, when you're knew it seems like a lot of items are overpowered, and while some are on the stronger side of the spectrum, none are absurdly overpowered and must be nerfed immediately. The same goes with classes as well; each class has a role in the game and can shine in different game modes and maps. What is key to win in any game mode or map is the ability to pick a role and stick with it to combine with your other teammates to make a dominate team. There is no limit to a class on a single team though which can allow fun combos of perhaps 10 spies. Now onto the economy of TF2, it is very complex and how's it done has impressed me very much. The ability to trade items for other items, which includes weapons and accessories, is a freedom that others do not enjoy in other games. Also, the ability to find random items and unlock random items is a nice addition if you cannot buy items with real money. Overall, TF2 is a very nice game and I commend Valve for trumping TF1 with it.

This comes from the perspective of someone who is relatively new-ish, having only played the game for not even half a year.  I also do not play on sponsored or competitive servers, which would probably be more ideal for me.  Quite a bit of my playtime has been in pub servers; think of it as being thrown into a cesspool (like your average high school).  Overall, considering how much time I have sunk into this game (not to mention the money) I feel it is time to say a word or two about it, good and bad.
Team Fortress 2, as indicated by the first word in its name, is built on the concept of teamwork.  The second word indicates the difficult obstacle of surpassing an enemy team and whatever "fortress" contains the objective.  And the number "2", because there was a game before this one.  Unlike any other multiplayer game I have ever played, teamwork is embodied by the numerous strategies and accomplishments of its various and unique classes working together.  Skill plays a part, as always, but a great team will overcome any obstacle and utterly wall an incompetent one.
You will then be disappointed to learn that most players will learn of this concept, think briefly for a moment, then toss the book in the river.  Never is this game more frustrating when witnessing "team"-mates make many, many, MANY uninformed or questionable decisions that literally toss the enemy team a cookie every five seconds or exuberates the small, but notable, technical issues of the game that can work against you.
I could fill a novel with examples, such as pyros never extinguishing their allies or medics withholding ubers while under heavy enemy fire or, indeed, players who spam engineer and sniper class and spend most of the game sitting on their♥♥♥♥♥doing nothing, but that would be redundant.  I will also spare you the rant of "easy button" weapons or technical issues because I am sure people have made entire documentaries on great topics such as "Sticky Spam" or "Baby Face Speed Demon" or, without a doubt, the famous "Hit Detection, Myth or Reality?" that has the praise and contempt of many scholars on the subject.
What, just barely, makes all the nonsense that would make any sane person french kiss Sasha (with the trigger pulled, of course) worth it are the moments when teammates abide by the concept.  When that sniper headshots a heavy about to bear down upon you, or the pyro airblasts an ubered heavy-medic combo from a sentry nest, or the scout protects the medic from another hounding scout, or a group works in concert to protect their heavy-medic combo with covering fire while pushing forward, and so on and so forth.
Those moments are amazing and make any game, even one that is utlimately lost, a joy to play through.  When people work together and are willing to make sacrifices for their allies, even at the cost of their precious killstreak, and in turn those allies are thankful and return the favor somehow, is that not what this game is about?  Is this not TEAM Fortress 2?
This is a game that contains some of the greatest multiplayer experiences you will ever come to know and remember, but only when you and others understand and abide by the name of the game.  Otherwise, you will tred many boring stalemates or be on the wrong end of a one-sided conflict or simply run into the wrong crowd of people before you ever happen upon the right game.  But, again, I suppose it is worth it for the moments where you meet amazing people and taste sweet victory achieved by all of your sweat, blood, and rage-inducing spasms.

For a long time, I've been playing TF2.
Yes, I know there's a CoD game that released like a month ago.
Yes, Rainbow Six Seige is more realistic.
Yes, Battlefield Hardline is not that impressive. (Believe me, I watched the AngryJoeReview on it. Definitely not buying that.)
But all of these FPS, TF2 just gives us a huge varied gameplay, at the same time, making it free to play. It's even more fun than those whack F2P FPS games you download in Asia.
This game features 9 classes, and each of them has its own unique talent.
The Scout for example, can capture points twice as fast than any other class in the game.
These classes have their own advantages and disadvantages, all in which adds in a strategic flavor on the game. (Unless you're just placing a sentry in the middle of the brigde of 2Fort for fun. Just saying.)
It all involves teamwork. One works on taking on the enemy front lines, the other takes on the objective, the other defends, and the other supports the team. You might encounter one small sentry nest and call it, "Unfair", but with wits, teamwork, and a bunch of explosives and Sappers, you can take on that nest, and come through, stronger than ever before. It's just an amazing feeling to do that, no?
The maps are indeed complex and colorful. Each twist and turn leaves you to excitement that there might be someone on that corner over there. And if you played this game long enough, and you started in a familiar map, You know exactly what to do, and that's not a bad thing.
Playing this game is just better than playing those cheap F2P FPS games just by your internet cafe.
And after years and years of constant new things, I will always expect the new content to be great, adding an awesome experience to an already awesome game.

This game defines the first-person shooter genre for a new generation in the same way that several games such as Doom, Duke Nukem 3D, Wolfenstein 3D, and Goldeneye 007, as well as Valve's own Half-Life have done in the past. The classes are well balanced, while still providing a challenge, and no matter what mode you play on, the results are always changing due to the concepts of whether the team will work together or not. This can usually be a good thing though. In other words, the odds are evened a tad bit more than other online shooters like Call of Duty. You're more likely to do better if there are more people in the game, as this allows for more stealth as a spy, more people to heal as medic, or in some cases with others, more people to slaughter with your weapons.
It's no wonder this game continues to be a hit even after seven years since its release on Steam.
However, the only downside is that this game only has an online mode. Reccommended only for those with a good running PC, and a solid Internet connection.

After playing over 200+ hours of Team Fortress 2 i'd thought i'd give my review of the game. Let's start off with the gameplay. Basically you get to play 9 unique classes Scout,Soldier,Pyro,Demoman, Heavy, Engineer, Medic, Sniper, and Spy. Every class i've played with seems to have a weakness but i guess that's what makes them unique for example, the scout runs really fast with 125 hp but they seem to get killed easily if you're not dodging every bullet your enemy shoots at you. The spy has 125 hp same as the scout but it relies on disguises to keep themselves well hidden but it doesn't last very long till someone discovers who you really are.
While i was playing the game i also notice that they have a shop, so i checked it out and they had all kinds of stuff, they had outfits,weapons, and even taunts for every class now for me i really don't buy things in the game with REAL MONEY but i did buy a couple of things that looked pretty cool to me.
Another thing i did like but really didn't dove into is the trading. Everyone in the TF2 community loves to trade things such as hats,weapons,taunts,keys,trading cards etc you name it they'll trade it. Unfortunately you can't really trade anything till you buy something from the store.
Now for the community, most of the people in the community consist of little kids, people who like MLP, and obnoxious ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s but i don't let that bother me since i have the option to mute or block them. People in this community don't really like F2P players cause according to them they are considered noobs and in order to not be a F2P player you can buy something from the store and you won't be considered one.
Anyways that is my review of Team Fortress 2 if you're into fps games then this is for you hope you all have a wonder day/night.

I remember when I first discovered Team Fortress Classic, I had no idea that in a not-to-distant future I would be playing one of the most legendary games of all time.
Team Fortress 2 (TF2) when it first started was pretty awesome and everyone was pretty excited for The Orange Box. If you'd like an idea of what that was like I believe they gave up on updating the Xbox 360 version of the game, you can still go back and play basically vanilla Team Fortress 2.
TF2 is a well balanced game where two teams, Red and Blu, compete to complete the objective first whether it's getting enough capture points or planting a bomb and much more gamemodes thanks to the extensive modding community. It's a lot of fun to play with your friends or to just relax to and kill some time.
Now, when it comes to my personal experience with this game I can say that I've had my fair share of fun, especially when the whole items system was added. Countless nights I spent trying to collect everything, get every achievement item, unlock it all to show it off. I wasted a lot of time and money playing this game, but I can say I sure as hell enjoyed every minute of it. I remember the thrill of opening a crate and then finding a rare unusual and everyone congradulating you on the server while others started spamming trade requests. I can honestly say, from my experience that if anyone was thinking about giving this game a try then do it, but be prepared to lose countless hours and or days. Besides, if this positive review and all of the others don't convince you enough to try it then the fact that it's FREE will.
This game will always have a place in my heart, as corny as that sounds, but it's the truth. The whole market system is so amazing, if you know how to play it right you can honestly make a lot of money. A long time ago, maybe a year or so, I was in need of cash and I turned to the Team Fortress 2 trading servers which were full of people looking to spend their money on others items. I sold a few unusual hats and made actually quite a bit of money, I was stoked and I didn't have to worry about needing money anymore at least for a while. If you know what you're doing you can really make it big.
Now I don't really play much of TF2 anymore. Occasionaly I'll play it with my friends who are just getting into it, or who want to just kill some time and relax. Although I sold all of my tradeable items in my backpack it's still fun. Even though I may never fully get back into it, I can definitely say if you're thinking of trying it out - DO IT. You won't regret it.

This is a well made, stylized, team based first person shooter. Teamwork is needed to win at higher levels of play, though lone wolfing is fine on lower skill levels such as on most public servers. There are 9 classes to choose from. Each class has unique weapons and abilities that allow each to fulfill a unique roll as part of a larger team. This provides for a challenging and rewarding experience when faced against opponents of similar or better skill levels. The game has an active dev team that continues to release updates to the game that add new content such as weapons or game modes.
At the time of this review, there are two official modes of play: player versus player and 'Mann Versus Machine'.
Player versus player is a mode where one team of players battles against another team of players. Within this mode, there are different types of maps. Each type of map has it's own objective or objectives for each team to achieve.
'Mann Versus Machine' is a mode where a team of up to 6 players battles against waves of bots. Players collect money from destroyed bots. The money is divided equally among players in the team and can be used to purchase upgrades and abilities for the next wave of bots. The pay to play sub-mode, "Mann Up", gives rewards upon completing a "tour".
In addition to the official modes of play, there are several player made mods that introduce other modes of play such as 'Versus Saxton Hale', where a team of players battles against a player playing as a character named Saxton Hale; 'Dodge Ball', where two teams of players playing as Pyros must airblast rockets and other projectiles back and forth in order to stay alive; 'Zombie Mod', where a team of players must make it to the end of the map without dying to zombies that are played by other players; to name just a few of the many player made mods available.
In addition to game play, players will randomly receive free items from the game. Some of the free items given out are weapons, hats and crates. Hats can be worn by a class to change the appearance of that class. Crates can be opened with a key. Keys can be purchased from the Mann Co Store or from the Steam Community Market or traded for from another player. Most crates will list which items can be found within them.
The game has several communities for a player to choose from if a community is what you are looking for. The game is easy to pick up and play, either alone or with friends, yet has a depth of play that will keep you from becoming bored too quickly. The dynamics between the different classes, weapons, play styles, skill levels, modes and maps provides content for many hours of play. I have been playing since November 2014 and I still return to the game on a regular basis.

It has been a few years since my previous review was created, and a lot has happened with TF2 since then. The infamous Meet Your Match Update caused an unprecendented uproar within the community, and Valve has since worked to ship an update that would breathe new life into this decade old game. With the Jungle Inferno Update, I believe that the devs working on Team Fortress 2 have recaptured the attention of a lot of gamers. The newly implemented changes have been well received by the community, and it seems like the developers have finally listened to the issues and feedback of the players. Was it too late? Was this update enough to bring back TF2 to it's former glory? You'll get different answers from different people, but this TF2 player will tell you that Team Fortress 2 is still a game with a lively community, and that it will see prosperity in the years to come.
================================================================
About a year ago I was relatively uninterested in this game as I felt like it lacked what a "normal" FPS game would usually offer. As you can probably tell I played a lot of COD, Battlefield, etc. All of this changed when I revisited TF2 almost a year ago, I realized that TF2 was a unique game that was different than most FPS on the market, the well balanced classes, the near unendless amount of content that can be achieved as you play the game, and not to mention the incredible balance of the weapons at your disposal makes TF2 a must have in everyones game library. All of this plus the fact that the game is Free-To-Play is just a cherry on top (although it is highly recommended that you upgrade to premium), my thoughts on this title has changed dramatically over the past couple of years and I've found that it takes an FPS player to adapt to the different play style compared to other FPS titles. Although I still put many hours in COD TF2 gotten a spot in my rotation, and boy does it earn it.
